## Session and execution control routes

The control routes find the owner workspace from the ID alone. The URL does not carry a workspace. The helpers `ws_of_session`, `ws_of_gate`, `ws_of_execution`, and `ws_of_decision` scan every open workspace and ask its database whether it holds the ID. The route returns 404 when no workspace holds it. IDs are unique across workspaces because they come from UUID version 7 values (see the section on IDs).

These rules apply to the control routes:

- **Create.** `create_session` calls `engine.create_session`. The classify judge picks the projects when `projects` is empty.
- **Amend.** `AmendRequest.delivery` is a `ContextDelivery`. The default `queue` lets running executions finish on the old request, and the next step sees the new context. The value `now` interrupts running executions and runs them again with the new context.
- **Pause, resume, stop.** Each route calls the engine method of the same name and returns the new `SessionSummary`. [Engine runtime](engine-runtime.md) owns what each one does.
- **Answer a gate.** `answer_gate` passes `AnswerGate.answer` to `engine.answer_gate`. [Judges, decisions, and YOLO mode](judges-and-yolo.md) owns the answer kinds.
- **Override a decision.** `override_decision` calls the engine, then reads the decision again from the database and returns it.
- **Cancel and resume an execution.** Both call the engine, then return a fresh `ExecutionView`.
- **Get an execution.** `get_execution` sets `has_terminal` to true when the engine view says so or when the harness runtime still holds a terminal for the ID.
- **Inspect.** `inspect_execution` calls `engine.inspect_execution`, which reopens the session of an ended harness run read-only. The route returns the view of the new execution.
- **Session diff.** `diff` collects the changed files of the review loops of the session. It reads at most 200 files and skips any file that resolves outside the project root, because an agent can leave a symlink that points outside the project. Each row has the `HEAD` text and the current text.
- **Ask.** `ask` rejects an empty question with 400. The answer streams on `execution:<id>` of the returned ID.

Execution views carry a one-line `summary`. `summary_line` collapses whitespace and cuts the text to `SUMMARY_CHARS` (120) characters with an ellipsis. For a tool call, `tool_summary` uses the first present input key of these eight: `file_path`, `command`, `pattern`, `url`, `path`, `query`, `skill`, `notebook_path`. It removes the workspace root prefix from the value.

## Work lock rules for workspace changes

Each `WorkspaceRt` has a `work` lock. The route code uses it so that a workspace removal and the start of new work never overlap. The code comments name this "Rule W4".

### What happens when

- **A route starts work.** `init_project`, `create_session`, `inspect_execution`, and `ask` call `start_work`. It takes the lock for read. If the lock flag is true, the workspace is being removed, and the route returns 404 "No workspace". The caller holds the read guard when it starts the work. A removal then cannot pass its busy check in between.
- **A route changes shared files.** `artifact_move`, `artifact_delete`, and `book_delete` call `try_write` on the lock. If a session is starting, the call fails, and the route returns 409 "Try again in a moment, because work is starting in this workspace." This rule makes sure that no session starts between the busy check and the move or the removal.
- **A workspace is deleted.** `App::delete_workspace` holds the write lock of the workspace map, calls `rt.retire()`, and removes the entry only if `retire` succeeds. If it fails, the route returns 409 and the workspace stays open.
- **A git operation runs.** `clone_project`, `pull_project`, and the git dock routes run in a separate `tokio::spawn` task. A client that closes its tab does not stop git halfway, so no partial checkout stays behind.

## Request body limits

Three routes replace the axum default body limit. The default is 2 MB.

| Route | Limit | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/uploads` | `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` + 1,024 bytes | Room for the HTTP framing around the largest allowed upload. |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/artifacts` | `MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES` + 1,024 bytes | The same reason. |
| `PUT .../projects/{key}/file` | `8 * TEXT_CAP` (8 MiB) | JSON escaping can double a text that is at the edit cap. |

`POST /api/auth/exchange` reads at most 64 KiB of body. `GET /api/artifacts` returns the content only when the file is at most `ARTIFACT_LIMIT` (4 MiB) and is valid UTF-8. Otherwise it returns `binary: true`, an empty `content`, and the `size`, so the client uses the download route.

## The WebSocket at /ws

One browser tab opens one socket. The socket carries all live data for the tab: session events, execution output, workspace changes, terminal bytes, and editor hints. The tab chooses what it receives by subscribing to channels. Without channels, every tab receives the events of every session.

The handler in `crates/ostra-server/src/ws.rs` reads the cookie from the upgrade request and sets the message and frame size limit to `MAX_MESSAGE` (1,048,576 bytes). A terminal paste is the largest expected message. The task `run` then owns the socket. It uses one `tokio::select!` loop with these inputs:

- A timer every `RECHECK` (5 seconds).
- The revoke broadcast of `Auth`.
- Terminal frames from the `term_rx` queue.
- Hint answers from the `hint_rx` queue.
- Pushed messages from `app.push`.
- Incoming client messages.
- Engine notices from `app.hub`.

The client sends only text frames. The server ignores binary frames from the client. The server sends JSON text frames for `ServerMsg` values and binary frames for terminal bytes.

### Channels

A channel is a string. The server keeps a set of channel names for each socket. It does not check that the ID in a channel name exists.

| Channel | Receives |
| --- | --- |
| `session:<id>` | `session_event` and `session_updated` for one session. |
| `execution:<id>` | `execution_delta` and `execution_status` for one execution. |
| `workspace:<id>` | `workspace_updated`, `session_updated`, `project_fs_changed`, `git_progress`, `tree_patch`, and `activity` for one workspace. |
| `home` | `session_updated` for all workspaces, `harness_status`, and `workspace_updated` after a workspace is deleted. |
| `term:<execution>` | Binary terminal frames. See the next part. |

When a client subscribes to `home`, the server first sends the current `harness_status`. For every subscribe, the server then sends `subscribed` with the channel name. A repeated subscribe to a channel is allowed and does not count twice against `MAX_CHANNELS`.

### Client messages

The `ClientMsg` enum in `crates/ostra-core/src/api.rs` uses a `type` field with snake_case values.

| `type` | Fields | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subscribe` | `channel` | Adds the channel. A `term:` channel also starts a terminal stream. |
| `unsubscribe` | `channel` | Removes the channel and stops its terminal stream. |
| `term_input` | `execution`, `data` | Writes `data` to the PTY of the execution. |
| `term_resize` | `execution`, `cols`, `rows` | Resizes the PTY. |
| `code_complete` | `id`, `workspace`, `key`, `path`, `text`, `line`, `col`, `trigger`, `retrigger` | Asks for completions. |
| `code_signature` | same fields as `code_complete` | Asks for signature help. |
| `code_navigate` | `id`, `workspace`, `key`, `path`, `text`, `line`, `col`, `target` | Asks for supertypes or implementations. |

### Server messages

| `type` | Sent on | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session_event` | `session:<id>` | An event that the engine appended. Carries `session`, `seq`, `at`, `event`. |
| `execution_delta` | `execution:<id>` | Streamed output of one execution. Carries `seq`, `at`, `delta`. |
| `execution_status` | `execution:<id>` | The new `ExecutionStatus`. |
| `session_updated` | `session:<id>`, `workspace:<id>`, `home` | A new `SessionSummary`. |
| `workspace_updated` | `workspace:<id>` | Projects or the workspace changed. The page refetches the workspace. |
| `harness_status` | `home` | The installed harnesses. |
| `subscribed` | reply | The server accepted a subscribe. |
| `error` | reply | A text `message`. |
| `project_fs_changed` | `workspace:<id>` | Project-relative paths that an execution or the user wrote. An empty list means reload every listing. |
| `git_progress` | `workspace:<id>` | One line of git progress for a clone. At most four per second for each clone. |
| `tree_patch` | `workspace:<id>` | A changed or new node of the Sessions tree. At most four per second for each session. |
| `activity` | `workspace:<id>` | New running executions, open gates, or spend. At most two per second for each workspace. |
| `code_completion`, `code_signature_help`, `code_navigation` | reply | The answers to the hint requests. Each carries the `id` of the request. |

The rate limits come from `TREE_TICK` (250 ms), `ACTIVITY_GAP` (500 ms), and `PROGRESS_EVERY` (250 ms) in the server. The server also coalesces file writes over `DEBOUNCE` (150 ms) into one `project_fs_changed` message for each project.

### How an engine notice reaches a socket

The engine does not know about sockets. When the server opens a workspace, `App::attach` starts a forwarder task. The task reads `EngineNotice` values from the engine and lets the file and navigation caches observe each one. Then it sends the notice into the `hub` broadcast channel as a `HubMsg` with the workspace ID. Each socket reads `hub` and calls `route`, which maps a notice to channels and one `ServerMsg`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Engine
  participant Forwarder as Forwarder task
  participant Hub as hub channel
  participant Socket as ws::run task
  participant Browser
  Engine->>Forwarder: EngineNotice
  Forwarder->>Forwarder: files.observe and nav.observe
  Forwarder->>Hub: hub.send(HubMsg)
  Hub->>Socket: rx.recv()
  Socket->>Socket: route(msg) picks the channels
  Socket->>Browser: ServerMsg JSON if subscribed
```

The `route` function maps each notice as follows:

| `EngineNotice` | Channels | `ServerMsg` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Event` | `session:<id>` | `session_event` |
| `Delta` | `execution:<id>` | `execution_delta` |
| `ExecutionStatus` | `execution:<id>` | `execution_status` |
| `SessionUpdated` | `session:<id>`, `workspace:<id>`, `home` | `session_updated` |
| `ProjectsChanged` | `workspace:<id>` | `workspace_updated` |

The server also originates messages that no engine notice causes. Code in the file, git, navigation, and harness setup modules sends a `Pushed` value (a channel list and a `ServerMsg`) into the `app.push` channel. Each socket sends a pushed message only when one of its channels matches.

### What happens when

- **A socket reads too slowly.** The `hub` and `push` channels have fixed capacities. [Architecture](architecture.md) owns those capacities. If a socket falls behind, the server sends `error` with the message `lagged`. The page then refetches its REST snapshot.
- **A client sends text that is not a valid `ClientMsg`.** The server sends `error` with `Unreadable message.` and keeps the socket open.
- **A client subscribes to more than 256 channels.** For a new channel, the server sends `error` and does not add it. The message tells the client to unsubscribe from channels it no longer shows. `MAX_CHANNELS` is 256.
- **The cookie expires or a sign-in is revoked.** The server closes the socket with code `4401` and the reason `Signed out`. A revoke from this server closes the socket at once through the revoke broadcast. A revoke from the CLI closes it within `RECHECK` (5 seconds). The server also checks the cookie once after it subscribes to the revoke channel, because a revoke between the upgrade and the subscription goes to no one.
- **The socket ends in any way.** The `Streams` value aborts every terminal and hint task of the socket when it drops.

## Terminal channels

A `term:<execution>` channel streams the terminal of a harness execution. The ID can also be the ID of a setup terminal (see the part on harness setup). The server sends terminal data as binary frames. Each frame has this layout:

- Byte 0: the length `n` of the execution ID in bytes, at most 255.
- Bytes 1 to `n`: the execution ID.
- All remaining bytes: terminal output.

The test `pty_frame_layout` shows the layout. The frame for `x_1` and `hi` is `[3, 'x', '_', '1', 'h', 'i']`. A client reads the prefix to learn which terminal the bytes belong to, because one socket can show many terminals.

`stream_terminal` runs as a task for each `term:` subscription. It works as follows:

1. If the harness runtime holds no PTY for the ID, the task reads the stored transcript once from `paths::terminal_transcript` and sends it as one frame. The client shows it read-only. Then the task waits for the registry to insert a PTY. This wait covers a run that has not started its PTY yet.
2. When a PTY exists, the task sends its current screen as one frame. Then it sends each output chunk as a frame.
3. If the viewer lags behind the PTY buffer, the receive fails with `Lagged`. The task then sends a fresh screen and starts again. The PTY buffer holds 256 chunks (`STREAM_BUFFER`).
4. If the PTY ends, the stream closes. The task then waits for another PTY with the same ID.

A repeated subscribe to the same `term:` channel stops the old task and starts a new one, so the client gets the screen again. Frames pass through the `term_tx` queue, which holds `TERM_QUEUE` (64) frames for each socket. A slow socket makes its PTY streams lag and resync. The server does not drop the socket.

### Terminal input and resize

- `term_input` with `data` longer than `MAX_TERM_INPUT` (65,536 bytes) returns `error` "Terminal input is limited to 64 KiB per message. Paste in smaller parts." The limit exists so that one paste cannot fill the PTY write queue alone. That queue holds 256 writes (`WRITE_QUEUE` in `ostra-exec-harness`).
- If the PTY refuses the write, the server sends `error` "The harness is not reading terminal input right now, so the input was dropped." If no PTY exists for the ID, the server drops the input and sends no error.
- `term_resize` with `cols` or `rows` of 0, `cols` above `MAX_COLS` (1,000), or `rows` above `MAX_ROWS` (500) returns `error` "Terminal size is out of range." Otherwise the server calls `ptys().resize`. The PTY defaults are 120 columns and 40 rows, and the harness page lists the minimum size.

See [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) for how the PTY runs and for the transcript file.

### Harness setup terminals

`POST /api/harnesses/{harness}/setup` starts a terminal in the home folder of the user. The action `install` runs the vendor installer. The action `login` runs the CLI login command and returns 409 "Install ... first" when the program is not on the `PATH`. The terminal ID has the form `setup_<harness>_<action>`, for example `setup_agy_login`. If a terminal for the same harness and action still runs, the route returns it and starts no second one. The client streams the output on `term:<terminal>` and types with `term_input`. When the process exits, the server detects the harnesses again and sends `harness_status` on `home`.

## Editor hints over the socket

The three hint messages serve the file editor. They use the socket and not REST because a hint request starts on each keystroke and a newer request makes the older one useless.

These rules apply to `code_complete`, `code_signature`, and `code_navigate`:

- The request carries a number `id`. The answer carries the same `id`.
- Lines are 1-based. Columns are 0-based UTF-16 code units. The request carries the unsaved `text` of the file.
- Each kind has one in-flight slot in `Streams`, under the keys `hint:complete`, `hint:signature`, and `hint:navigate`. A newer request of the same kind aborts the older task, and the older request never gets an answer.
- Answers pass through a queue of `HINT_QUEUE` (8) messages for each socket.
- Each answer has `result` and `error`. If the workspace does not exist, `result` is null and `error` holds the text. For `code_signature` and `code_navigate`, a null `result` also means "nothing to show".
- A hint waits up to 3 seconds (`HINT_WAIT` in `code.rs`) for a language server that is still starting. The code index answers completions in the meantime.

[Code navigation](code-navigation.md) owns how the index and the language servers produce the answer.

## Embedded web build

`crates/ostra-server/src/assets.rs` embeds the folder `web/dist` into the binary with `rust_embed`. The binary needs no separate web server. If you change the console, run `npm run build` in `web/` and rebuild `ostra`.

`static_handler` serves each request that no API route matched:

1. It removes the leading `/` from the path. If the path is not empty and names an embedded file, it returns the file with a MIME type from `mime_guess`.
2. Files under `assets/` get `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, because the build puts a content hash in each file name. All other files get `no-cache`.
3. Some paths return 404: a path that starts with `api/`, `internal/`, or `assets/`, and a root-level file name with a dot that does not end in `.html` (for example `/favicon.ico`).
4. Every other path returns `index.html`. This lets the client router load a route directly, also a route that ends in a file name such as `/w/ws_1/f/app/src/main.rs`.

The service worker file `/sw.js` is served from the root so that it covers the whole app. If the build is missing, the handler returns status 200 with the text "The web build is missing. Run `npm run build` in web/ and rebuild ostra." The test `client_routes_load_the_app_and_missing_assets_404` checks these rules.

## App state and startup

`crates/ostra-server/src/app.rs` holds the process-wide state. There are two layers. `Shared` holds what every workspace uses. `App` holds `Shared` and the parts that serve requests.

| Field of `Shared` | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `global_path`, `global_cache` | The path of the machine config file and its last good copy. |
| `registry` | The `RegistryDb` with workspaces, credentials, and push subscriptions. |
| `providers` | The model providers, built from the config and the saved credentials. |
| `native` | The `NativeExecutor`. |
| `harness` | The `HarnessRuntime` for CLI harness executors, with the PTY registry. |
| `notifier` | The Web Push sender with the VAPID keys. |
| `mcp` | The `McpGateway`: connections to the MCP servers of each workspace. |
| `env` | The detected harnesses and tools (`EnvStatus`). |
| `exe`, `port` | The path of the running binary and the listen port. |

| Field of `App` | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `shared` | The `Arc<Shared>`. |
| `workspaces` | A map from `WorkspaceId` to `Arc<WorkspaceRt>`. |
| `hub` | The broadcast channel of `HubMsg`. See [Architecture](architecture.md) for its capacity. |
| `push` | The broadcast channel of `Pushed`. See [Architecture](architecture.md) for its capacity. |
| `auth` | The `Auth` object for sign-in. |
| `files`, `code`, `code_tools`, `nav` | The file caches, the code index, the agent code tools, and the Sessions tree. |
| `dev` | The `--dev` flag. |

`Shared::global()` reads the config file on each call, so an edit applies without a restart. If the file does not parse, or the sandbox section does not validate, `global()` logs a warning and returns the last good copy. `Shared::protected_paths()` lists the binary, the config file, the data directory, and the assets directory. The policy refuses agent writes to these paths.

### Startup order

`run` in `app.rs` starts the server:

1. It reads the global config and computes the listen address: the `--bind` flag, else `server.bind`, else `127.0.0.1`. The values `localhost`, `all`, and `*` are accepted. The values `all` and `*` mean `0.0.0.0`.
2. It binds the port: the `--port` flag, else `server.port`. With an explicit port, it uses only that port. Without one, it tries `DEFAULT_PORT` (7878) and the next 19 ports, and then asks the system for a free port.
3. If no other server runs, it stops processes that earlier sandboxes left, removes stale egress sockets, and removes stale decoys.
4. `build` creates `Shared` and `App`. It stops with an error if the sandbox section of the config is invalid. It starts the price refresh, unlocks the registry with the master key, writes the embedded assets to the data directory, builds the providers and executors, and loads or creates the VAPID keys.
5. On Unix, it starts the hook bridge socket that serves `internal_routes()`. Only sandboxes use this socket. Windows has no sockets of this kind and no sandbox. Unsandboxed harness hooks reach `/internal/*` over loopback HTTP.
6. It starts the background tasks `run_touches` (file write notices) and `nav::run` (Sessions tree and activity).
7. It attaches every registered workspace. A workspace whose `workspace.toml` is missing gets a warning and is skipped. A workspace that fails to open gets an error log, and the server still starts.
8. It removes the tool caches of ended sessions, writes the server file, prints the sign-in URL, and opens a browser unless the flags say otherwise.
9. It serves the router with graceful shutdown on Ctrl+C. At the end it removes the bridge socket and the server file.

When the server listens on an address that is not loopback, it prints a warning. The warning says that the traffic is plain HTTP and names the SSH tunnel and TLS proxy options. See [Running Ostra](running-ostra.md) for the flags.

### Attach, recover, and delete a workspace

`App::attach` is idempotent. It returns the open workspace when one exists. Otherwise it opens a `WorkspaceRt`, calls `engine.recover()` to rebuild the session state from the event log, starts the forwarder task, and inserts the workspace into the map.

`App::delete_workspace` unregisters the workspace and deletes its settings and database, but it leaves the projects on disk. After the unregister, it clears the navigation cache and the MCP connections for the workspace root. Then it pushes `workspace_updated` on `workspace:<id>` and `home`.

`stop_offline` implements `ostra stop`. If a server runs, it refuses and names `POST /api/sessions/{session}/stop`. Otherwise it opens the registry, finds the workspace database that holds the session, and ends the session there.

`open_registry` sets file mode `0600` on the registry database and its `-wal` and `-shm` files on Unix, because the registry holds provider keys, git credentials, and the push signing key.

## Services glue for the engine

The engine does not call the server. It calls the `Services` trait. `crates/ostra-server/src/services.rs` implements it as `ServerServices`, which holds the `Shared`, the workspace root, and the workspace ID. `Shared::services` (the `WorkspaceHost` method) creates one for each workspace. [Engine runtime](engine-runtime.md) owns how the engine uses these methods.

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `global` | Returns `Shared::global()`. |
| `workspace` | Loads `workspace.toml`, then applies the trust overlay with `ostra_workspace::trust::effective`. If the file does not load, it uses `WorkspaceSettings::seeded("workspace")`. |
| `executor` | `ExecutorKind::Native` returns the shared native executor. A harness kind returns the harness executor for the current global config. |
| `factory` | Returns `AgentsFactory`. |
| `judge` | Finds the provider and model of the route, then calls `ostra_providers::structured`. Errors return as text. |
| `notify` | Does nothing unless `notifications.push` is on. Otherwise it sends a Web Push to each subscription that has no workspace or this workspace. The URL is `/w/<workspace>` plus the notice URL. |
| `protected_paths` | The shared list plus `workspace.toml` and the workspace database. |
| `command_approved` | Asks the trust store whether the user approved a format command. |
| `add_allow_rule` | Adds a permission allow rule to the workspace settings and saves it, only if the rule is not there yet. |

In `notify`, a push result of `Gone` removes the subscription from the registry. A `Failed` or error result logs a warning. [Integrations](integrations.md) owns the push encryption.

## Project commands route

`crates/ostra-server/src/commands.rs` backs `PUT /api/workspaces/{ws}/projects/{key}/commands`. It saves the commands in `.ostra/project.toml`. The engine and the policy read the profile again for each execution, so a saved command applies to the next run.

The route cleans each of the seven fields: `build`, `test`, `test_one`, `format`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `run`.

- The route trims a value. A blank value, or a value of one em dash character (U+2014), becomes no command.
- A value with a line break is an error. The message tells the user to write the command on one line and to chain steps with `&&`.
- A value with a control character is an error. The message tells the user to remove the control characters.
- A value longer than `MAX_COMMAND_LEN` (2,000, counted with `str::len`, so in bytes) is an error.

If any field has an error, the route returns 422 with one issue for each field. The issue path is `commands.<field>`. If `.ostra/project.toml` does not exist, the route returns 409 and tells the user to initialize the project first. If the file does not parse, the route returns 409 with the parse error. After a save, the route calls `trust::saved_format` with the old and new format command. It also announces `workspace_updated`, because `ProjectView` carries the profile.

## Management tools for agents

`crates/ostra-server/src/manage.rs` implements the tools `PROJECT_LIST` and `PROJECT_CREATE` for agents that hold the `ManageProjects` capability. `Management::open` returns no handle for an execution without that capability or without a session. The policy has already checked the call, and the user has already approved `PROJECT_CREATE`, when the call arrives.

`PROJECT_LIST` returns the workspace root and one line for each project: key, path, stack, init status, and whether the project is in the session scope.

`PROJECT_CREATE` runs these steps:

1. Parse the input and ask the session state for a refusal reason.
2. Compute the target folder with `create_target`.
3. Claim the folder so no other git operation uses it.
4. Create the folder. If the input asks for git, run `git init --quiet` with `QUICK_TIMEOUT` (30 seconds).
5. Import the project into the workspace and announce `workspace_updated`.
6. Add the project to the session scope with `add_created_project`.

If git init or the import fails, the code calls `clear_failed` to undo the folder, so nothing stays behind. If only the last step fails, the project exists but is not in the session. The error text says so.

## Model price refresh

`crates/ostra-server/src/prices.rs` keeps the price catalog for cost reports. The cache file is `models-dev.json` in the data directory. A restart without network still prices every execution, because `start` installs the cached catalog first.

The background task works as follows. It refreshes when the cache file is older than `REFRESH_EVERY` (24 hours). If a refresh fails, it keeps the cached prices, logs a warning, and tries again after `RETRY_AFTER` (1 hour). A refresh request times out after 60 seconds. A catalog with no priced models is refused. The code writes a temporary file and renames it, so a failed refresh never replaces the old file. The environment variable `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` (`URL_ENV`) replaces the catalog URL. An empty value turns the fetch off, for tests and air-gapped machines. The default URL is `MODELS_DEV_URL` in `ostra-core/src/pricing.rs`.

## IDs and shared API types

`crates/ostra-core/src/ids.rs` defines six ID types with one macro: `WorkspaceId` (`ws_`), `SessionId` (`s_`), `ExecutionId` (`x_`), `GateId` (`g_`), `DecisionId` (`d_`), and `MessageId` (`m_`). Each ID is a prefix plus a UUID version 7 value in simple hex form. Because UUID version 7 values are time-ordered, the lexical order of IDs matches the order of creation. The types serialize as plain strings, and `ts-rs` exports them as the TypeScript type `string`.

`crates/ostra-core/src/api.rs` holds every request, response, and socket type of this page. The `#[ts(export)]` attribute makes `ts-rs` write a TypeScript binding for each type. Run `cargo test -p ostra-core export_bindings` to regenerate the bindings. The web console imports them, so a change to a type here changes the console build.

Three more constants live in this file:

- `UI_STATE_MAX_BYTES` is 64 KiB. It is the largest UI state document that the server stores.
- `RoutingPreset::HARNESS_AGENTS` is `["implementer", "write-test"]`. A harness preset moves these two agents off the native loop. The presets are `Native`, `Codex`, and `Claude`.
- `SUMMARY_CHARS` is 120. The part on the control routes describes it together with the 8 input keys of `tool_summary`.

## Limits and constants of the server API

| Name | File | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_MESSAGE` | `ws.rs` | 1,048,576 bytes | Largest client message and frame. |
| `MAX_TERM_INPUT` | `ws.rs` | 65,536 bytes | Largest `term_input` data. |
| `MAX_CHANNELS` | `ws.rs` | 256 | Most channels for one socket. |
| `TERM_QUEUE` | `ws.rs` | 64 frames | Binary frames queued for one socket. |
| `HINT_QUEUE` | `ws.rs` | 8 messages | Hint answers queued for one socket. |
| `HINT_COMPLETE`, `HINT_SIGNATURE`, `HINT_NAVIGATE` | `ws.rs` | `hint:complete`, `hint:signature`, `hint:navigate` | Keys of the in-flight hint slot for each kind. |
| `RECHECK` | `auth.rs`, used in `ws.rs` | 5 seconds | How often an open socket checks its cookie. |
| Close code | `ws.rs` | 4401 | Close code for a signed-out socket. |
| `hub` and `push` capacity | `app.rs` | See [Architecture](architecture.md) | Broadcast buffers for engine notices and pushed messages. |
| `DEFAULT_PORT` | `app.rs` | 7878 | First port to try. The server tries 20 ports in all. |
| `ARTIFACT_LIMIT` | `api.rs` | 4 MiB | Largest session file that `GET /api/artifacts` returns as text. |
| Exchange body | `api.rs` | 64 KiB | Largest `/api/auth/exchange` body. |
| Session diff files | `api.rs` | 200 | Most files in one session diff. |
| Memory list | `api.rs` | 500 | Most lessons in one list response. |
| `MAX_COMMAND_LEN` | `commands.rs` | 2,000 bytes | Longest stored project command. |
| `REFRESH_EVERY` | `prices.rs` | 24 hours | Age at which the price cache refreshes. |
| `RETRY_AFTER` | `prices.rs` | 1 hour | Wait after a failed price refresh. |
| `URL_ENV` | `prices.rs` | `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` | Replaces the catalog URL. Empty turns the fetch off. |
| `UI_STATE_MAX_BYTES` | `ostra-core/src/api.rs` | 64 KiB | Largest saved UI state. |
| `SUMMARY_CHARS` | `ostra-core/src/api.rs` | 120 characters | Longest `ExecutionView` summary. |

The constants of the code, file, git, and auth modules are on [Reference: server, code, store, and notify limits](reference-server-limits.md).

## What the API does not guarantee

- The WebSocket does not check that a channel ID exists. A client can subscribe to any channel name and receives nothing for an unknown ID. The cookie is the only access check, and it covers all workspaces of the machine.
- The control routes find a workspace by a scan of all open workspaces. The cost grows with the number of workspaces.
- A lagged socket loses messages. The server does not replay them. The page must refetch its REST snapshot after `lagged`.
- The server sends hint answers at most once for each in-flight slot. A newer request of the same kind drops the older answer.
- The server gives the plain HTTP protection of the guard and the headers. It does not encrypt traffic. See [Server security](server-security.md) for what the sign-in and the checks do and do not cover.

sections.title: Project files, git, and workspace search
sections.summary: How the server lists, reads, saves, diffs, and watches project files, runs git commands and stores git credentials, browses folders, and ranks workspace search hits.
sections.body:
Ostra agents change project files, and the user must see which session changed which file, review the diff, and run git on the result without a terminal. This part of `ostra-server` gives the browser that view. If the Files view is missing, the user cannot see which execution wrote a file. The browser can overwrite a file that an agent is writing. A git command can change a checkout under a running session. The page covers these areas:

- The Files view: tree, file read, save, diff, and changes.
- Attribution of changed files to session executions.
- Live watching and the caches it clears.
- Git status marks and the Git dock commands.
- Clone, pull, and saved git credentials.
- Folder browsing for the project picker.
- The Sessions tree, the activity summary, and workspace search.

The route table is in [Server API](server-api.md). The numeric limits of this part are also in [Reference: server, code, store, and notify limits](reference-server-limits.md). Credential encryption is in [Server security](server-security.md).

## Project root and path containment

Every Files route takes a project key, and the server maps the key to one canonical folder. `project_root` in `files/mod.rs` returns that folder. If the key is unknown, the route answers 404 with `No project `key` in this workspace.` If the folder is gone, the route answers 404 and names the missing path.

The special key `_artifacts` (the constant `TAG_ROOT`) shows the workspace artifacts instead of a project. For this key, `view_roots` creates two folders when they are missing: the visible artifacts folder and the hidden one. The tree lists both, and a hidden artifact shows with `hidden_from_agents` set so the user can find and unhide it. A new artifact path inside a hidden folder goes into the hidden folder (Rule W2), so what the user adds to a hidden folder is hidden too. The artifact rules are in [Artifacts and structured documents](artifacts-and-documents.md).

### Containment

`tree::contain` turns a request path into a `Contained` value with three fields: `rel` (normalized, joined with `/`, empty for the root), `lexical` (`root/rel`), and `real` (symlinks resolved). The function refuses these paths:

- An absolute path: `Use a path relative to the project root.`
- A path with `..` that climbs above the root.
- A path whose resolved target is outside the root, including a symlink that leads out.

The route answers 403 for each refusal. A symlink that stays inside the project is allowed. The function uses the same resolution as the write-scope guard, so a link cannot lead out of the project through the browser when it cannot lead out through an agent. The guard is in [Policy engine](policy-guards.md).

## Folder tree

`GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/projects/{key}/tree` lists one folder. The query fields are `path` (default: the project root), `depth` (default 1, clamped to 1 to 4 by `MAX_DEPTH`), and `hidden` (default `false`).

The listing follows these rules:

- Folders sort before files. Each group sorts by lowercase name, then by exact name.
- `.git` is never listed. A name that starts with `.` is listed only when `hidden` is `true`.
- The listing uses the same ignore sources as the Grep and Glob tools: `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`, the global git ignore file, and the ignore files of parent folders. A project does not need a git repository for these rules to apply. Because the sources are the same, the Files view and the agents agree on what is ignored.
- An ignored folder and a symlinked folder are listed but not entered. The entries of an ignored folder have `ignored` set.
- The listing stops at `TREE_CAP` (5,000) entries and sets `truncated`.

Each entry carries more fields from other sources. A file has `git` (the git mark), `staged`, and `changed_by` (the attribution). A folder has `has_changes`, which is `true` when any file under it has a git mark. An untracked folder gets the mark `?`. An entry that is hidden from agents has no git mark and no changes.

## Read a file

`GET .../projects/{key}/file?path=` returns a `ProjectFile`. The server reads at most `TEXT_CAP` (1 MiB, 1,048,576 bytes) of the file.

- If the first 8,000 bytes hold a NUL byte, the file is binary. The response has `binary: true`, no `content`, and no `hash`. This is the same test that git uses.
- If the file is longer than the cap, the response has `truncated: true`. The server cuts the text at the last complete UTF-8 sequence, so the cap does not leave a broken character.
- The `hash` field is the SHA-256 of the whole file. The server sets it only when the text is the complete and valid UTF-8 file. A truncated or non-UTF-8 file has no hash, so the browser cannot save it.
- The response also carries `git`, `staged`, `changed_by`, and `read_only`. `read_only` is a text that says why the browser cannot write the file, or empty.

If the path is a folder, the route answers an error that points to the tree route. If the file does not exist, the route answers 404.

## Save a file from the browser

The browser editor writes one file with `PUT .../projects/{key}/file`. The body has `path`, `content`, and `base_hash`. This is the only write that the Files view makes, besides folder creation. The route accepts a body of up to 8 times `TEXT_CAP` (8 MiB), because JSON escaping can double a text at the edit cap and pass the 2 MB default of the web framework.

### The save checks

`Files::save` runs these checks in order:

1. The path must name a file, not a folder or the root.
2. For `_artifacts`, a new artifact path must be valid, and the workspace must have room for another artifact.
3. The text must not be larger than `TEXT_CAP`. If it is, the route answers 400 with `The text is larger than 1 MB, the size Ostra edits in the browser.`
4. `read_only_reason` must return nothing (see the next list).
5. The save takes the `saving` lock. Saves run one at a time, so the hash check and its write cannot be split by another save.
6. `save_file` compares `base_hash` with the SHA-256 of the file on disk, then writes.

`read_only_reason` refuses a write for these files:

- A file with a `.git` path part: `Files under .git are read-only here. Use git to change them.`
- Ostra state in the workspace runtime folder (artifacts excepted) and the project memory folder. The reason is that a direct edit skips the validation of the Settings screen.
- A file that a running execution is writing: `A running execution is writing this file...`

The status is 409 when a running execution holds the file, and 403 for the other reasons.

### The hash rule and the atomic write

`save_file` accepts the write only when the disk still holds the version that the edit started from:

| Disk state | `base_hash` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File missing | none | Create the file |
| File missing | present | 409 on `base_hash`: the file was deleted after you opened it |
| File exists | none | 409 on `base_hash`: the file already exists |
| File exists | equals the disk hash | Write |
| File exists | differs from the disk hash | 409 on `base_hash`: the file changed on disk |

The write uses a temporary file with the prefix `.ostra-save-` in the same folder. The server writes the text, calls `sync_all`, copies the permissions of the old file, and renames the temporary file over the target. On Unix, a new file gets mode `0644`, because a temporary file starts at `0600`. A reader never sees a half-written file.

After a save, the server records the save time in `user_edits`. A save supersedes older attribution for that file (see the attribution part). The route handler then calls `announce_save`, which tells the code index and sends `project_fs_changed` with the saved path.

### Create a folder

`POST .../projects/{key}/mkdir` creates a folder with its missing parents. An empty path answers 400. A folder that exists answers 409 on `path`. The same read-only rules apply. The response is the listing of the parent folder with hidden entries included.

## Diff and changes

### One file diff

`GET .../projects/{key}/diff?path=&base=` returns a `FileDiff` with parsed hunks, `added`, `removed`, `binary`, and `truncated`. The base is a commit, branch, or tag name, and the default is `HEAD`.

- `valid_base` accepts a base of at most 200 bytes that does not start with `-` and holds only letters, digits, and `._/~^@{}-`. The reason is that the base goes to git as an argument, so it must never read as an option. A bad base answers 400.
- `resolve_base` resolves `base^{commit}`. In a repository with no commits, `HEAD` resolves to the empty tree, so the files of a new project show as added. Any other unknown name answers 400: `No commit named ... in this repository.`
- A tracked file runs `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames -U3 <commit> -- <path>`. An untracked file runs `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <path>`.
- Output stops at `DIFF_CAP` (4 MiB). The server then stops git and sets `truncated`.
- A project that is not in a git repository answers an empty diff. The `_artifacts` root also answers an empty diff, because artifacts have no history.

### The changes list

`GET .../projects/{key}/changes` lists the files that sessions changed and that still differ from `HEAD`. Each row has the path, the git mark, `staged`, the added and removed line counts, and `changed_by`.

- The rows come from the attribution map, not from git. A file that git marks as changed but that no session wrote is not in the list.
- In a git project, a row stays only when the file has a git mark. In a project with no git repository, every attributed file stays.
- The list holds at most `CHANGES_CAP` (500) rows.
- The line counts come from one `git diff --numstat` against `HEAD`. An untracked file counts its text lines as added. Binary files count 0 and 0.
- The `_artifacts` root answers an empty list.

## Attribution of changes to sessions

Attribution answers the question: which execution last changed this file? `Files::attribution` builds a map from project-relative path to `ChangedBy` (session, execution, agent, phase, tests flag, `staged`, `running`, and time). It reads two sources and one override.

1. **Finished work.** The server reads the sessions that include the project key, newest `updated_at` first, and keeps the first `ATTRIBUTION_SESSIONS` (20). For each session, `ostra_engine::view::file_changes` reads the `changed_files` list in the submit result of each finished implement or test execution. A reported path becomes a project-relative path with `/` separators, and a path outside the project is dropped. For one path, the execution with the latest end time wins across sessions.
2. **User saves.** An entry is dropped when the user saved the file in the browser after the execution ended. The reason is that the user's text is now the newest change.
3. **Running executions.** The `live` map holds each file that a running execution wrote, before its submit reports it. The server adds the entry with `running: true` when the execution is still running. It skips the entry when the finished-work map or a user save is as new or newer.

The `live` map for one project holds at most `MAX_LIVE` (5,000) paths. When it is full, the server clears it. The result is cached for `ATTRIBUTION_TTL` (3 seconds). A `running` row makes the browser read-only for that file, which prevents the browser and the agent from overwriting each other.

## Live file watching

The server does not watch the disk with a file system watcher for the Files view. It learns about writes from the tool calls of executions, and it clears caches when it sees one. The reason to use tool calls is that they also give the execution that wrote the file, which attribution needs.

### Touch sources

A `Touch` holds the workspace, the execution, the written paths, and an optional base folder for relative paths. Two sources produce a touch:

- **Native executions.** `ToolWatch::observe` reads the engine notices. A tool call named `Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`, or `ApplyPatch` stores its target paths under its `call_id`. When the matching tool result arrives without an error, the watch sends a touch. A failed result sends nothing, because a failed edit changed nothing. A result pairs only once.
- **Harness executions.** The hook bridge calls `policy_observe` after a tool call. If the outcome is not an error and the call is a write, the bridge sends a touch with `workspace: None`. The base is the `cwd` of the call, or else the repository folder of the run. Harness executors are in [Harness executors](harness-executors.md).

The pending map of `ToolWatch` holds at most `MAX_PENDING` (4,096) calls, because hook-bridge calls log no result. When it is full, the server clears it. When an execution ends, the watch drops the pending calls of that execution.

### From touch to message

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Exec as Execution
    participant Watch as ToolWatch or bridge
    participant Run as run_touches
    participant Files as Files caches
    participant Code as Code index
    participant Browser as Browser socket
    Exec->>Watch: write tool call and result
    Watch->>Run: Touch
    Run->>Run: collect touches for 150 ms
    Run->>Files: invalidate project, record_live
    Run->>Code: touch path
    Run->>Browser: project_fs_changed with paths
```

`run_touches` takes the first touch, then collects more touches for `DEBOUNCE` (150 ms). For each path, `absorb` does these steps:

1. Resolve the path against the base, or against the project folder of the execution.
2. Find the project that holds the path. `locate` picks the deepest project root, and it skips the project root itself.
3. Invalidate the index, git, and attribution caches of the project.
4. Tell the code index to reindex the path (see [Code navigation](code-navigation.md)).
5. Record the path in the `live` map with the execution and the time.

The server then sends one `project_fs_changed` message for each project on the channel `workspace:<id>`. The message holds at most `MAX_PUSHED_PATHS` (500) paths. The reason for the debounce is that an agent can write many files in a short time, and one message for each project is cheaper than one for each file.

### Writes that Ostra does not see

A write by a shell command, an editor, or any process outside the write tools sends no touch. These changes show up when the caches expire:

| Cache | Constant | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File name index | `INDEX_TTL` | 30 seconds |
| Git status | `GIT_TTL` | 5 seconds |
| Attribution | `ATTRIBUTION_TTL` | 3 seconds |

A cache entry is also invalid when the project root changes. `Files::invalidate` drops all three caches of one project.

### Git and save announcements

- `announce_git` invalidates the caches and sends `project_fs_changed` with an empty path list. An empty list tells every browser listing of that project to reload, because git can change many files at once (pull, checkout).
- `announce_save` tells the code index about the path and sends `project_fs_changed` with that one path. The save, folder creation, and artifact save routes call it.

## Git marks and read-only git calls

`files/git.rs` gives the Files view its git facts. It runs `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --untracked-files=normal --ignore-submodules=all -- .` once for each project, and `GitStatus` holds the result for `GIT_TTL`.

Every call in this file is read-only and uses these settings:

- The `AUTOMATIC` config from `ostra-core`: no fsmonitor program, no `ext::` transport, no askpass program, and a hooks folder that holds no hooks.
- `--no-optional-locks`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, and `--literal-pathspecs`. Because git takes no optional locks, these calls never contend with the engine's own `git add`.
- `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, a null stdin, and `kill_on_drop`.
- A timeout of `GIT_TIMEOUT` (15 seconds). A timeout or a start failure returns `None`. Output is capped for each call: 32 MiB for status, 8 MiB for numstat, and the caller cap for diffs.

The `GitMark` values are `M` (modified), `A` (added), `D` (deleted), `R` (renamed or copied), and `?` (untracked). `mark(x, y)` reads the index side `x` and the work tree side `y`:

| Condition | Mark |
| --- | --- |
| `x` is `R` or `C` | `R` |
| `x` is `A` | `A` |
| `x` or `y` is `D` | `D` |
| Any other change | `M` |

A file is `staged` when `x` is not `.`. An unmerged file (record type `u`) is `M` and not staged. An untracked folder arrives as one entry, and every path under it reads as untracked.

A project can sit in a subfolder of a repository. `git rev-parse --show-prefix` gives the project prefix, and the parser drops every entry outside it. A folder with no git work tree gives `repo: false`, and the tree reports `is_git: false`.

## The Git dock: status, branches, and commands

`repo.rs` serves the Git dock. The read routes are `GET .../projects/{key}/git` (status) and `GET .../projects/{key}/git/branches`. The command routes are `POST .../git/stage`, `unstage`, `commit`, `fetch`, `push`, and `checkout`.

### Status

`repo::status` runs `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z` and returns a `GitRepoStatus`:

- `branch` (none when HEAD is detached), `head` (the first 7 characters of the commit id, none in a new repository), `upstream`, `ahead`, and `behind`.
- `staged`, `unstaged`, and `conflicted` lists. A file with changes on both sides appears in both `staged` and `unstaged`. A rename carries `orig_path`. Each list holds at most `LIST_CAP` (2,000) paths, and `truncated` shows that a list is cut.
- `staged_elsewhere`: the count of staged paths outside the project prefix. A commit takes them too, because a commit covers the whole index.
- `busy`: a text that names a session that works in the project, or empty.

### Branches

`repo::branches` lists local and remote-tracking branches with `for-each-ref`, at most `BRANCH_CAP` (500). The current branch comes first, then local branches, then remote ones, each sorted by name. The remote `HEAD` pointer is skipped.

### The rules that every command follows

`Op::run` wraps each changing command:

1. It refuses the command when a session works in the project. `session_in` looks for a session in the status `Running`, `Waiting`, or `Paused` that lists the project, or an init session for it. The answer is 409: `Stop session ... or wait for it to finish, then try again, because it is working in ...`. The reason is that a checkout change under a running agent corrupts its work.
2. It refuses a folder outside a git work tree: `... is not in a git repository. Run git init in it first.`
3. It takes the project claim (see the claim part below).
4. It runs the command, then calls `announce_git`, even when the command failed.
5. It returns the command output and the new status.

The route runs each command in its own task. The reason is that a closed browser tab must not stop git halfway.

### Commands

| Route | Git command | Timeout | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | `git add -A -- <pathspecs>` | `LOCAL_TIMEOUT` 60 seconds | No paths means the whole project (`.`). |
| `unstage` | `git restore --staged -- <pathspecs>` | 60 seconds | Before the first commit, it runs `git rm --cached -r -q --ignore-unmatch`, because there is no HEAD to restore from. |
| `commit` | `git commit --no-edit -m <message>` | `COMMIT_TIMEOUT` 5 minutes | Needs a non-empty message and no conflicted file. Needs at least one staged path in the project, or a staged path outside the project (`staged_elsewhere` is not 0). Commit hooks can run formatters and tests, so the timeout is long. |
| `fetch` | `git fetch --prune -- <remote>` | `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` 10 minutes | Uses the credential for the fetch URL. |
| `push` | `git push --porcelain [--set-upstream] -- <remote> <refspec>` | 10 minutes | Needs a branch. The refspec is `HEAD:<branch.merge>`, or `HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` with `--set-upstream` when no upstream exists. Uses the credential for the push URL. |
| `checkout` | `git switch ...` | 60 seconds | See the next list. |

Each pathspec goes through `contain`, so it must stay inside the project. The server adds `--literal-pathspecs`, so a name with a glob character is not a pattern.

The remote for `fetch` and `push` is the `branch.<name>.remote` setting. If none exists, it is `origin`. If `origin` does not exist but the repository has one remote, it is that one. With no remote, the answer is `Add a remote to the repository first...`. With several remotes and none chosen, the answer asks the user to set an upstream.

`checkout` takes `branch`, `create`, and `start`:

- The name must pass `branch_ok` (no leading `-`, no `..`, no space, control character, or any of `~^:?*[\`), and must not end with `/` or `.lock`.
- With `create`, the server runs `git switch -c <name> [start]`. If a local branch with that name exists, it answers status 400 (`GitError::Invalid`): `A branch named ... already exists.`
- Without `create`, a local name runs `git switch <name>`.
- A remote name such as `origin/feature` runs `git switch --track origin/feature`. If a local branch with the short name exists, it runs `git switch <short>` instead.
- A name that exists nowhere answers `No branch named ...`.

After a checkout, the server also sends `workspace_updated`, because a branch change can change the project files that settings read.

### Error status codes

`git_err` maps the `GitError` kinds to HTTP status codes:

| `GitError` | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Busy` | 409 | A session works in the project, or another git command holds the claim. |
| `Git` | 502 | Git ran and failed, or did not start. |
| `Invalid` | 400 | The request cannot run as asked. The text says what to change. |
| `Import` | 400 or 500 | A cloned checkout could not be imported. |

## The git claim

A claim prevents two git commands from working on the same project at the same time. `claim` in `git.rs` records the pair (project key, folder) in `w.cloning` and returns a `Claim` value. Its `Drop` removes the record, so the claim ends on success, failure, or a panic.

`claim` refuses when:

- The workspace is starting or deleted. The workspace work lock cannot be read, and the answer is `Busy` with the workspace starting text.
- The key is already claimed, or the folder is inside or around a claimed folder. The answer is `Git is already running in `key`. Wait for it to finish, then try again.`

Clone, pull, and every changing Git dock command take a claim.

## Clone a project

`POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/clone` clones a repository and imports it as a project. The work has two parts.

### Validate the request

`clone_plan` checks the request and returns every problem on its field: `url`, `key`, `stack`, `path`, `branch`, or `credential`.

- **`url`:** `parse_remote` accepts `https://`, `http://`, `ssh://`, and `user@host:path`. It refuses an empty value, a value that starts with `-`, a value with a space or control character, a local path, `file://`, `ext::`, and any other scheme. The reason is that a local or `ext::` remote reads or runs things on the machine that runs Ostra. It also refuses any URL that is not ssh and holds a password, which includes `https://` and `http://`: `Remove the user name and token from the URL and save them as a git credential, because git keeps the URL in the project's .git/config.`
- **`key` and `stack`:** the project key rules of the workspace apply. See [Workspaces, projects, and settings](workspaces-and-settings.md).
- **`branch`:** must pass `branch_ok`.
- **`credential`:** an explicit credential id must exist and must match the URL type (ssh or https). If the request gives none, `credential_for` picks one.
- **`path`:** must be absolute. The default is `<workspace root>/<key>`. The folder must be new or empty.

### Run the clone

`clone` takes the claim and runs `git clone --progress [--branch <b>] -- <url> <dest>` with a timeout of `CLONE_TIMEOUT` (30 minutes). The route runs it in its own task, so a closed tab does not leave a partial checkout.

- Progress lines go to the channel `workspace:<id>` as `git_progress` messages, at most one every `PROGRESS_EVERY` (250 ms). The server redacts the secret from each line.
- If git fails, `clear_failed` removes the destination. If the folder existed empty before the clone, it only empties the folder.
- If git succeeds, the server imports the checkout with `import_project` and sends `workspace_updated`.

## Pull a project

`POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/projects/{key}/pull` fast-forwards the current branch. The route answers 400 when the project folder has no `.git`, and 409 when a session works in the project.

`pull` takes the claim, then reads the branch (`symbolic-ref`). A detached HEAD answers `The project has no branch checked out...`. The remote is `branch.<name>.remote`, else `origin`. The command is `git pull --ff-only` with a timeout of `PULL_TIMEOUT` (10 minutes). The reason for `--ff-only` is that a pull must never create a merge commit or a conflict in a checkout that agents use. The result holds `branch`, `updated`, `before`, `after` (short commit ids), and the last output lines. The server calls `announce_git` and `workspace_updated` after the pull.

## Git credentials

A git credential lets Ostra clone, fetch, push, and pull with a private remote. The browser manages credentials with `GET` and `POST /api/git/credentials`, and `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/git/credentials/{id}`. Every route answers the list of `GitCredentialView` values. A view shows `id`, `label`, `host`, `kind`, `username`, and `has_secret`, and never the secret.

### Storage

The server saves each credential as JSON in the registry database with `secret_set`, under the key `git_credential:<id>`. The id is `gc_` plus a UUIDv7. The secret lives next to the provider keys and is encrypted by the registry store (see [Server security](server-security.md)). The `Debug` output of `SavedGitCredential` leaves out the secret. A record that cannot be read is skipped with a warning.

### Validation

`apply` validates a new credential or an edit, and returns every issue on its field:

- `kind` must be `https` or `ssh`.
- `host` is normalized: it loses the scheme, a user part, and slashes at the ends, and the host name becomes lowercase. It can hold a `:port` and a path prefix, such as `github.com/acme`.
- `username` must not hold a space or control character.
- An `https` secret must have no space or line break.
- An `ssh` secret must be a whole private key (`PRIVATE KEY-----`). A public key is refused. A new key with `ENCRYPTED` is refused, because Ostra runs git with no terminal to ask for a passphrase.
- When an edit gives an empty secret, the saved secret stays. The label defaults to the host.

### Which credential a remote uses

`credential_for` picks the credential for a remote URL:

- The credential type must match the remote: `ssh` for an ssh remote, `https` for an http remote.
- A plain `http://` remote (not loopback) matches no credential. The reason is that a token must never cross the network unencrypted.
- The credential host must equal the remote host, or be a path prefix of the remote key on a segment boundary. `github.com/acme` matches `github.com/acme/shop` but not `github.com/acmeish/shop`.
- A credential host with no port matches the host on any port. A credential host with a port matches only that port.
- The longest matching host wins.

### How git receives the secret

`GitAuth::new` builds the arguments and the environment for one git process. The secret reaches git only through the process environment and one-off `-c` options, and never lands in `.git/config`.

- **All processes:** `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so a prompt fails instead of waiting. On Windows, also `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`, because the Credential Manager asks in a window that no one answers on a server.
- **https:** the arguments clear the user's own credential helpers, so git does not copy the token into them. A helper from `-c` answers only for the credential host, so a remote that `url.*.insteadOf` rewrites never gets the token. The arguments also set `http.proxy=` and `http.sslVerify=true`, so the token goes to the remote over verified TLS, whatever the repository config says. The user name is the saved one, or `x-access-token` (`DEFAULT_TOKEN_USER`).
- **ssh:** the key goes into a new file with mode `0600` in a private temporary folder under the Ostra data folder, which the sandbox hides. `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` uses `BatchMode=yes`, `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`, `IdentitiesOnly=yes`, and `-i <key>`. The folder is deleted when the `GitAuth` value drops.
- **No credential:** ssh runs with `BatchMode` and `accept-new`, unless the `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` variable is already set.

`run_git` adds more protection for every command:

- It removes a planted `commondir` before it runs, because that file can hand the command the config of another repository. Git then runs the credential helper or the SSH command of that config on a push or pull.
- It applies `NO_EXEC` (no fsmonitor, no `ext::`, no askpass) and the submodule filter overrides.
- It sets `LC_ALL=C`, so the output text is stable.
- It reads stdout and stderr together, keeps the last `TAIL_LINES` (12) lines, and replaces the secret with `***` when the secret has 4 or more characters.
- On a timeout, it stops git: `git did not finish within N minutes and was stopped.`
- If git is missing, the text is `Install git on the machine that runs Ostra, because cloning and pulling run the git command.`

## Browse folders for the project picker

`GET /api/fs?path=&prefix=&limit=` returns folder names for the type-to-browse picker. It reads one folder, never recurses, never starts git, and never returns file contents. `POST /api/fs/mkdir` creates a folder with its missing parents.

### Path rules

`expand` turns the typed text into a path:

- An empty text or `~` is the home folder. `~/x` is under home. A relative text is taken from home.
- On Windows, `/` or `\` alone is the drive list (`DRIVE_LIST`), `C:` is the root of that drive, and a Git Bash `/c/...` path becomes `C:\...`. The drive list uses `GetLogicalDrives`, so no drive is touched and an empty card reader cannot stall the picker.

### The answer

- `limit` defaults to `DEFAULT_LIMIT` (200) and clamps to 1 to `MAX_LIMIT` (2,000).
- Only folders are listed. A symlink to a folder counts as a folder.
- Names that start with `.` show only when the typed `prefix` starts with `.`. On Windows, a folder with the hidden or system attribute shows only when its name starts with the prefix.
- `filter_names` ignores case. Names that start with the prefix come first, then names that contain it, each sorted. `truncated` shows that more names matched.
- Each entry has `is_git` (a `.git` exists) and `is_ostra_project` (the project inventory file exists).
- When the path does not exist or cannot be read, `nearest` holds the deepest folder above it that exists, so the picker can step back.
- `BrowseCache` keeps each folder read for `CACHE_TTL` (2 seconds). The read stops after `MAX_SCAN` (50,000) entries, so a folder the size of `/usr/lib` stays fast.

`mkdir` accepts only an absolute path, `~`, or `~/...`. It refuses a path that is a file or the Windows drive list. After it creates the folder, it clears the whole cache, because every cached ancestor can miss the new folder.

## Sessions tree and workspace activity

`nav/mod.rs` builds the Sessions tree of the console and pushes changes. `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/tree` returns every session node, newest `updated_at` first. `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/activity` returns the activity summary.

Engine notices mark sessions and executions as dirty: a session event, a session update, an execution status, and a tool call or status message of an execution. A ticker runs every `TREE_TICK` (250 ms). It rebuilds each dirty node and sends `tree_patch` only when the node differs from the cached one. So the console gets at most 4 patches each second for each session. If notices are lost, `lagged` marks every session dirty.

The activity summary has the running executions (oldest first), the open gates, and the spend for today and for the week. `windows` computes both windows from local midnight: today starts at local midnight, and the week starts at local midnight 6 days earlier, so a week is today plus the 6 days before it. If a daylight saving change skips a midnight, the window starts at the first hour that exists. The server sends `activity` at most once each `ACTIVITY_GAP` (500 ms) for each workspace, and only when the summary changed.

When the server builds a node, it also indexes the artifacts of the session for search: the label, the file name, and the headings. It skips a file when its label and modification time match the index. A file larger than `ARTIFACT_INDEX_CAP` (4 MiB) is indexed by its file name only. The reason for this index step is that agents write artifacts with their tools, so the index catches up when the node is rebuilt.

## Workspace search

`GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/search?q=&limit=` returns one ranked list across seven kinds of hit: `session`, `execution`, `artifact`, `file`, `project`, `lesson`, and `setting`. The `limit` defaults to `DEFAULT_LIMIT` (50) and clamps to 1 to `MAX_LIMIT` (200).

### Sources

| Kind | Source | Matching |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session` and `artifact` | Full-text index of the workspace database (`TEXT_ROWS` 200 rows) | Index row, then scored in memory |
| `execution` | Executions in the Sessions tree | In memory: agent name and run label |
| `artifact` | Artifact label and file name in the tree | In memory |
| `file` | The file name index of each project (see the file index part) | In memory, path scoring |
| `project` | Project key and folder name | In memory |
| `setting` | `SETTING_KEYS`: key, last key part, and description | In memory |
| `lesson` | The memory store of each project, `LESSONS_PER_PROJECT` (20) each | Memory full-text search |

A project that has no memory database is skipped, because opening a store creates its file, and search must not write into a project. An empty query returns the recent sessions, newest first, with scores that fall from 1.0 by 0.001 each.

### Scoring

Every source scores a match from 0 to 1, so one sort merges them. `Needle` lowercases the query once.

| Text match (`text_score`) | Base score |
| --- | --- |
| Equal, ignoring case | 1.0 |
| Text starts with the query | 0.9 |
| Query starts at a word | 0.8 |
| Query is a substring | 0.65 |
| Every query word appears, in any order | 0.55 |
| Query is a subsequence | 0.3 |

| File path match (`file_score`) | Base score |
| --- | --- |
| File name equals the query | 1.0 |
| File name starts with the query | 0.88 |
| File name contains the query | 0.74 |
| Path contains the query | 0.6 |
| Query is a subsequence of the file name | 0.4 |
| Query is a subsequence of the path | 0.3 |

A length penalty lowers each score by 0.0005 for each extra character, at most 0.05, so a shorter match ranks first among equals. Each kind then adds an offset: sessions +0.04, artifacts +0.03, projects +0.03, and executions +0.02. A match that the text index found by word prefix, but that the in-memory scorer cannot place, gets `INDEX_ONLY` (0.45). Hint text is cut to `HINT_CHARS` (80) characters.

`merge` sorts by score (higher first), then by shorter label, then by id. It keeps the best hit for each id and cuts the list to `limit`. For files, `rank_files` keeps only the best `limit` of each project before the merge. A test requires a query over a 50,000-path index to finish in less than 50 ms in a release build.

## What this part does not guarantee

- Containment checks a path when the request arrives. A process on the machine can still change a symlink between the check and the read.
- The Files view sees a write only when a write tool reports it, or when a cache expires. A shell command that writes files shows up after `GIT_TTL`, `INDEX_TTL`, or `ATTRIBUTION_TTL`.
- Attribution comes from what an execution reports in `changed_files` and from write tool calls. A file that changed through a shell command has no `changed_by` until an execution reports it.
- Attribution reads only the 20 newest sessions of the project. An older change has no attribution.
- The file name index stops at 50,000 paths and the tree at 5,000 entries. Search and the tree set `truncated` and show no more.
- The git claim and the session check cover Ostra's own commands. A git command that the user runs in a terminal does not take the claim.
- Redaction replaces only the exact secret text, and only when it has 4 or more characters.
