sections.title: Web console: screens, state, and shortcuts
sections.summary: How the React console in web/ boots, routes, keeps live state, draws each screen, handles keyboard shortcuts, protects the terminal, and edits files, with the limits and the reasons for each rule.
sections.body:
The console is the React app in `web/`. Without it, a user must call REST routes and read log files to start a session, answer a gate, or read agent output. The console shows the live state of one workspace and sends each answer to the server. This page covers the build, the boot, the routes, the shell, each screen, the API client, the socket, mock mode, the mobile shell, keyboard shortcuts, terminal safety, and the editor.

Other pages own related facts. [Server API](server-api.md) owns the REST routes and the socket messages. [Design system](design-system.md) owns the `@ostra/design` components. [Reference: web console and design constants](reference-web-limits.md) lists the constants in tables. [Session pipeline](session-pipeline.md) explains the lanes, stages, and gates that the screens show.

## Build, layout, and commands of the web app

The Rust server embeds the built `web/dist` folder in the binary. `build.sh` builds the web app first, because `crates/ostra-server/src/assets.rs` embeds `../../web/dist` with `rust_embed`. [Running Ostra](running-ostra.md) owns `build.sh`. The root `package.json` lists `design`, `web`, and `site` as npm workspaces, so one `npm ci` at the repository root installs all three.

### Stack

`web/package.json` names these libraries:

- `react` and `react-dom` 19.3, with `react-router` 8.4 for routes.
- `vite` 8.3 to build, `typescript` 7, and `vitest` 5 with `jsdom` to test.
- `@biomejs/biome` 2.5.14 to lint and format.
- `@monaco-editor/react` 4.7 and `monaco-editor` 0.56 for the file editor and the diff view.
- `@xterm/xterm` 6 and `@xterm/addon-fit` for harness terminals.
- `react-markdown` 10 with `remark-gfm` to render agent-written Markdown.
- `@ostra/design`, the workspace package in `design/`.

### Source folders

| Folder | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/auth.ts` | The route table, the boot, and the sign-in token exchange. |
| `src/api/` | The REST client, the socket manager, and the mock API. `src/api/gen/` holds one generated type file for each exported Rust type. |
| `src/shell/` | The chrome of one workspace: title bar, left dock, tabs, quick dock, status bar, palette. |
| `src/screens/` | One screen for each resource id, and the setup wizard in `screens/setup/`. |
| `src/mobile/` | The phone-width shell and its screens. |
| `src/features/` | Parts that screens share: gates, file tags, uploads, and the book model. |
| `src/lib/` | Pure helpers and hooks: tabs, resource ids, shortcuts, shared stores, events. |
| `src/content/` | Static text tables: lane and stage descriptions, agent route keys, sandbox and permission help. |
| `src/components/` | `Markdown` and the local Monaco setup in `monaco.ts`. |

The `ts-rs` tool generates the files in `src/api/gen/` from the Rust types. `src/api/types.ts` re-exports them, so a screen imports every server type from one place. Do not edit a file in `src/api/gen/`, because the next generation overwrites it.

### Commands

Run these commands in `web/`:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Starts Vite on port 5173 and proxies `/api`, `/ws`, and `/mcp/oauth` to the server. |
| `npm run dev:mock` | Starts Vite with `--mode mock`, so the console runs on fixtures with no server. |
| `npm run build` | Writes `web/dist`. Source maps are off. |
| `npm run typecheck` | Runs `tsc --noEmit`. |
| `npm test` | Runs `vitest run` on `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`, with `VITE_MOCK=1`. |
| `npm run lint`, `npm run format`, `npm run check`, `npm run check:fix` | Run Biome. |

The proxy target is the environment variable `OSTRA_DEV_SERVER`. Its default is `http://127.0.0.1:7878`. The OAuth redirect of an MCP server returns to the page origin, so `/mcp/oauth` is also proxied.

### Chunks and lazy loading

The build puts `react`, `react-router`, `lucide-react`, and the Markdown libraries in separate chunks. A change in app code then keeps those chunks in the browser cache. The warning limit for a chunk is 4000 KB (`chunkSizeWarningLimit`).

Three modules load with `lazy()`: the file editor, the Monaco diff, and the xterm screen. Import them only through their lazy wrappers. A static import moves Monaco or xterm into the main chunk.

## Boot, sign-in, and the 401 path

The browser has no session cookie when it first opens the console. The boot in `src/main.tsx` gets a cookie from the one-time token in the URL. The app shows a sign-in screen if the server still answers 401. [Server security](server-security.md) owns the token and cookie rules.

### Boot steps

`boot()` in `src/main.tsx` does these steps in order:

1. Call `watchInstall()`. The browser fires `beforeinstallprompt` only once for each page load, so the listener must exist at the start.
2. If the build is not mock, call `exchangeTokenFromUrl()` and wait for the result.
3. If the build is not mock, call `watchForTokens()` and `registerServiceWorker()`. The worker file is `/sw.js`.
4. Render `App` inside `StrictMode`, with the exchange error as a prop.

### Token exchange

`exchangeTokenFromUrl()` in `src/auth.ts` reads `#token=<value>` from the URL hash. It follows these rules:

- If the page is in a browser prerender, it waits for the `prerenderingchange` event. A background prerender must not spend the one-time token, because the real visit then holds a used link.
- It keeps each token in a `Set`, so one page load spends a token once.
- It removes the hash with `history.replaceState` before it posts the token. The token then stays out of history and out of a copied link.
- It posts the token to `POST /api/auth/exchange`. On failure it returns the error message, and `SignIn` shows it.

A new link pasted into an open tab changes only the hash, and a hash change does not reload the page. `watchForTokens()` therefore reloads the page on `hashchange` when the hash holds a token.

### What happens when

- **A request returns 401.** `request()` in `src/api/client.ts` calls every `onUnauthorized` listener before it throws. `App` then renders `SignIn` in place of the router. The state resets only when the page reloads.
- **The user pastes a sign-in link.** `tokenFromInput` accepts a link with `#token=` or a bare token of 16 or more hexadecimal characters. Other text produces the message to paste the whole link.
- **The exchange succeeds.** `SignIn` calls `location.replace("/")`.
- **The build is a mock build.** The boot skips the exchange, the token watch, and the service worker.

The `SignIn` text says that each link works once and expires after 15 minutes. It tells the user to run `ostra url` on the server for a new link.

## Routes, resource ids, and redirects

A reload or a deep link must open the same screen. The console achieves this with one rule: every thing that can open in a tab has a resource id, and the URL is a function of that id. A URL maps back to exactly one id. The code is in `src/lib/resource.ts`.

### Resource ids

| Resource id | URL | Screen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws:overview` | `/w/:ws` | `WorkspaceScreen` |
| `ws:cost`, `ws:settings`, `ws:memory`, `ws:skills`, `ws:docs` | `/w/:ws/cost`, `/settings`, `/memory`, `/skills`, `/docs` | `CostScreen`, `SettingsScreen`, `MemoryScreen`, `SkillsScreen`, `DocsScreen` |
| `book:<id>` | `/w/:ws/b/:id` | `BookScreen` |
| `session:<id>` | `/w/:ws/s/:id` | `SessionScreen` |
| `exec:<id>` | `/w/:ws/x/:id` | `ExecutionScreen` |
| `artifact:<absolute path>` | `/w/:ws/artifact?path=<path>` | `ArtifactScreen` |
| `project:<key>` | `/w/:ws/p/:key` | `ProjectScreen` |
| `file:<key>:<path>` | `/w/:ws/f/:key/<path>` | `FileScreen` |
| `dep:<key>:<uri>` | `/w/:ws/d/:key?uri=<uri>` | `DependencyFileScreen`, read-only |

A project key never contains a colon, but a path or a URI can. `parseResource` splits `file:` and `dep:` ids at the first colon after the key. Workspace artifacts use the reserved project key `_artifacts` (`ARTIFACTS_ROOT`), so an artifact file has the id `file:_artifacts:<path>`.

### Route table

`src/App.tsx` exports `routes`. The path `/` renders `Home`. The path `/w/:ws` renders `WorkspaceShell`, with children for each URL in the table above. Every child renders `RouteScreen`, which calls `resourceFromPath` and passes the result to `ScreenFor`. `ScreenFor` sets `key={id}`, so each tab starts with fresh state.

The route `/w/:ws/d/:key` is not listed in `routes`. The catch-all child `*` handles it, and `resourceFromPath` reads the `uri` query value.

### Redirects and special routes

- `/s/:id` renders `SessionRedirect`. It loads the session and replaces the URL with `/w/<workspace>/s/<id>` plus the hash. A push notification knows only the session id, so it links to this path.
- `/x/:id` renders `ExecutionRedirect`. It finds the session of the execution and then the workspace. If the execution has no session, the page shows that the execution belongs to no session.
- `/w/:ws/projects` redirects to `/w/:ws`. Projects were one page, and now each project opens in its own tab.
- Any other path renders `NotFound`.
- `/_design` renders the design gallery. The route exists only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true.

### Scrolling

A screen either scrolls itself or the shell scrolls it. `selfScrolling(id)` in `src/screens/index.tsx` matches the ids that start with `artifact:`, `file:`, `dep:`, `project:`, or `book:`. For these, the shell sets `overflow: hidden` on the center pane and gives the screen the whole pane.

## The workspace shell

The shell is the chrome around every screen of one workspace. It keeps the open tabs, the layout, and the keyboard handler in one place, so screens can stay simple. The code is in `src/shell/WorkspaceShell.tsx`.

### Layout

From top to bottom, the shell holds a title bar, a middle row, and a status bar. The middle row holds the left dock (when `sidebarOpen` is true), the center pane with the tab strip, and the quick-question dock (when `dockOpen` is true). `WorkspaceShell` renders `MobileShell` on a phone-width viewport and `Shell` elsewhere. It sets `key={ws}`, so tabs, stores, and dialogs never carry over between workspaces.

The title bar has the workspace switcher, the breadcrumbs of the active tab, the palette button, and the buttons for the two docks. The switcher menu lists the workspaces and the workspace pages (Overview, Cost, Settings, Memory, Skills, Documentation). It also has **New workspace**, **Add project**, and **Run the setup guide again**.

The center pane shows the screen for the active tab. If no tab is open, it shows a note with the palette shortcut. If `api.workspace` fails and no data exists, it shows **Workspace not available** with a button back to the workspace list. Above the screen, `PendingCommandsNotice` shows a banner when folder commands wait for approval. It does not show on the settings tab, where the full list is.

### Tabs

`tabsReducer` in `src/lib/tabs.ts` owns the tab rules. A tab has an `id`, a `preview` flag, and a `pinned` flag.

- **Preview tab.** At most one tab is a preview tab. It shows in italic. The next preview open replaces it. Rows in lists open with `preview: true`. An explicit action opens a normal tab. A double click on the tab or on the center pane keeps it.
- **Pinned tabs.** Pinned tabs sit before the other tabs. They are never preview tabs. They survive every bulk close.
- **Close.** If the active tab closes, the tab at the same index becomes active. If it was the last tab, the new last tab becomes active. A middle click on a tab closes it.
- **Bulk close.** The tab menu offers **Close others**, **Close to the left**, **Close to the right**, and **Close all**. It offers a choice only if the choice closes at least one unpinned tab.
- **Move.** A tab moves only inside its group, pinned or not. A moved preview tab becomes a normal tab. The key Ctrl or Cmd with Shift and an arrow moves the focused tab. The `Tabs` component of the design package handles that key.
- **Open beside.** The option `beside` puts a new tab after the active tab, but never inside the pinned group.
- **Restore.** `normalizeTabs` drops duplicates and extra preview tabs, puts pinned tabs first, and makes sure that `active` names an open tab.

A session tab shows a status dot. The tones are `running` accent (it pulses), `waiting` warn, `completed` ok, and `stalled` and `failed` bad.

### URL and tab sync

The URL and the active tab follow each other. `routeId` comes from the URL. If the URL changes and the shell did not cause the change, the shell dispatches `activate`, and a missing tab opens as a normal tab. If the active tab changes, the shell navigates to `resourcePath(ws, id, anchor)`. If no tab is active, it navigates to `ws:overview`. A ref named `shellNav` marks a URL change that the shell made, so the two effects do not loop.

The option `anchor` of `nav.open` becomes the URL hash. The screens use it to scroll to an element, for example `#gate-<id>` on the session board.

### Console context

`ConsoleContext` in `src/lib/nav.ts` gives each screen three objects:

- `useNav()` returns `open`, `close`, `keep`, `href`, `activeId`, `tabs`, and `ws`.
- `useShell()` returns `openDock`, `closeDock`, `taskDraft`, `setTaskDraft`, `newWorkspace`, `addProject`, `runSetup`, `browseFiles`, `theme`, and `toggleTheme`.
- `useWorkspace()` returns the `WorkspaceDetail` that the shell loaded and a `reload` function. The shell reloads it on each `workspace_updated` message.

The mobile shell provides the same context, so shared screens work in both shells.

### Saved layout

The shell keeps the layout in two places: `localStorage` and the server. The layout holds the tabs, the active tab, and these prefs: `leftTab`, `filesProject`, `sidebarOpen`, `dockOpen`, and `theme`.

1. The shell writes the layout to `localStorage` under `ostra.ui.<workspace id>` after each change.
2. On mount, the local copy wins. If the browser has no local copy and the server has a non-empty copy, the shell restores the server copy.
3. After the first `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/ui` finishes, the shell sends `PATCH /api/workspaces/{ws}/ui` 800 ms after the last change (`PATCH_DELAY_MS`). A failed patch is ignored.

The local copy is the fast path, and the server copy is the fallback for a browser with no local copy. `workspaceEntry` in `src/shell/TitleBar.tsx` uses the saved active tab, so opening a workspace lands on the tab that the user left.

### Panel widths

Panel widths are saved per browser in `localStorage` under `ostra.panels`, because they depend on the screen and not on the workspace.

| Panel | Default | Minimum | Maximum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Left dock (`sidebar`) | 264 px | 180 px | 640 px |
| Quick dock (`dock`) | 380 px | 260 px | 900 px |

A double click on a resize handle restores the default width. The arrow keys change the width by 16 px, or by 48 px with Shift.

### Theme and the live mark

`resolveTheme` returns the stored `light` or `dark`. If nothing is stored, it follows `prefers-color-scheme`, and the last fallback is `dark`. `applyTheme` sets `data-theme` on `<html>`. It also stores the choice under `ostra.theme`, so `Home` and `SignIn`, which have no workspace, use the last theme.

The browser tab icon shows the state of the active session. `markState` draws 8 arcs, one for each lane from `research` to `docs`. Arcs before the current lane are done. The current lane shows run, wait, or fail. The center shows the same state. A completed session shows all arcs done. `useLiveFavicon` sets the icon link to an inline SVG and restores the static icon when the shell unmounts.

## Left dock, palette, quick dock, and status bar

These four parts help a user move between screens and ask short questions without leaving the current tab.

### Left dock

The left dock has four tabs: **Sessions** (with a count), **Files**, **Artifacts**, and **Git**.

- **Sessions** lists each session from the workspace tree. A session expands to **Board**, **Executions**, and **Artifacts**. A group of one run shows as one row. A group of more runs shows with a count (`×N`) and expands. It starts expanded if a run is active or running. A text box filters the sessions. A second list shows the projects, with a button to add one.
- **Files** browses one project. It has a project select, reveal of the open file, a dotfile toggle, **New file**, **New folder**, **Collapse all**, a find box, and a **Changed by sessions** list. A file row can be dragged onto a request field to tag it.
- **Artifacts** uses the same panel on the workspace artifacts. It adds upload, download, hide, move by drag, and delete. Delete asks for confirmation.
- **Git** shows the changes of one project and polls the status every 10 seconds when the page is visible (`POLL_MS`). It can stage, unstage, commit, fetch, pull, push, switch a branch, and create a branch.

The commit box commits on Ctrl+Enter and on Cmd+Enter. The handler in `web/src/shell/GitPanel.tsx` tests `e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey`. The placeholder text names only Ctrl+Enter.

[Project files, git, and workspace search](project-files-and-git.md) owns the server side of these actions.

### Command palette

The palette opens with the `palette` shortcut (Ctrl+K or Cmd+K by default). It has three sources, which `mergePalette` in `src/lib/palette.ts` combines:

1. Server search: `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/search` with `limit` 30. `useSearch` waits 100 ms after the last key.
2. Local rows from data that the shell already holds: sessions, executions, artifacts, projects, and files of one project.
3. Commands: **New task**, **New workspace…**, **Add project…**, **Cost**, **Settings**, **Keyboard shortcuts**, **Ask a quick question**, **Toggle light and dark theme**, and the keyboard lock command when the browser supports it.

An empty query shows local rows (without files) and commands. A query shows the server hits sorted by score. If the search request fails, the palette marks the search as unavailable and filters the local rows instead. Then it also loads the file index of the Files tab project, so file search still works. The palette keeps at most 200 result rows before the commands (`MAX_ROWS`) and removes duplicate ids.

The groups appear in this order: Sessions, Executions, Artifacts, Projects, Files, Lessons, Settings, Workspace, Actions. A row id that starts with `cmd:` runs a command. An id that starts with `lesson:` opens Memory, and an id that starts with `setting:` opens Settings. The id becomes the URL anchor, so the screen selects the lesson or rings the field.

### Quick-question dock

The dock gives a read-only answer outside the pipeline. A user opens it with the `dock` shortcut (Ctrl+/ or Cmd+/ by default). The dock sends `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/ask` with the question and the session of the active tab. The server starts a `quick-answer` execution. The dock subscribes to `execution:<id>`, folds the deltas, and shows the answer. The answer text is the `answer` field of the `submit_quick_answer` call. If the call has not arrived, the text is the streamed text so far.

The dock shows the count of lookups and the end state (**Done** or **Ended: <status>**). The button **Turn into task** copies the question to the New task form through `setTaskDraft`, opens the overview, and closes the dock. If the active tab belongs to a session, the answer can read the artifacts of that session.

### Status bar

The status bar shows these items from left to right:

- The connection state. **Live · <host>** means the socket is open. **Connecting** and **Offline, reconnecting** show the other states. In mock mode it shows **Mock data**.
- The count of running executions, with a menu that opens each one.
- The count of gates that wait for the user. One gate opens its session at the gate. More gates open a menu.
- **Shortcuts locked**, when the keyboard lock is active. A click releases it.
- **YOLO on** or **YOLO off** for the session of the active tab.
- The spend of the week. The tooltip shows the spend of today. A click opens the Cost screen.
- The theme toggle.

The data comes from the `activity` message on the workspace channel. See [Judges and YOLO](judges-and-yolo.md) for what YOLO answers.

## API client

Every screen reaches the server through one object, `api`. The object has one function for each REST route that the console uses. The code is in `src/api/client.ts`. [Server API](server-api.md) owns the routes.

### Request rules

`request(method, path, body, signal)` follows these rules:

- It sends `credentials: "same-origin"`, so the session cookie goes with each call.
- It adds `Content-Type: application/json` only when a body exists.
- On a 401 answer, it calls the `onUnauthorized` listeners first.
- On any other non-2xx answer, it throws `HttpError`. The message is the `error` string of the JSON body, or the status line if the body is not JSON. The `issues` array of the body becomes `HttpError.issues`.
- A 204 answer returns `undefined`.

A 422 answer with `issues` lets a form place each message on its field. A 409 answer with the issue path `base_hash` tells the editor that the file changed on disk.

Two functions bypass `request`. `rawPost` posts a `Blob` as `application/octet-stream` and reads JSON. `uploadFile` does the same for a request upload. Download links are plain URLs: `artifactDownloadUrl` and `downloadUrl`.
