## Socket and the PTY frame

One WebSocket serves every screen. Without a shared socket, each screen opens its own connection, and a reconnect leaves each screen with stale data. `SocketManager` in `src/api/socket.ts` owns the connection. `socket()` creates one shared instance with the URL `ws://<host>/ws` (or `wss://` on HTTPS). In mock mode it uses the mock socket. [Server API](server-api.md) owns the message definitions.

### Channels and messages

A screen subscribes to a channel. The channels are `session:<id>`, `execution:<id>`, `term:<execution>`, `workspace:<id>`, and `home`. `channelsFor` decides which channels get a server message:

| Server message | Channels |
| --- | --- |
| `session_event` | `session:<session>` |
| `execution_delta`, `execution_status` | `execution:<execution>` |
| `session_updated` | `session:<id>`, `workspace:<workspace>`, `home` |
| `workspace_updated` | `workspace:<workspace>`, `home` |
| `harness_status` | `home` |
| `project_fs_changed`, `git_progress`, `tree_patch`, `activity` | `workspace:<workspace>` |
| `subscribed`, `error` | None. Only `onAny` listeners see them. |

The client sends `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `term_input`, `term_resize`, `code_complete`, `code_signature`, and `code_navigate`.

Channels are reference counted. The first handler of a channel sends `subscribe`. The last handler to leave sends `unsubscribe`. `send` drops a message when the socket is not open, and it does not queue. A subscription made when the socket is closed still works, because the `onopen` handler sends `subscribe` for every channel in the handler map.

### Reconnect

When the socket closes, the manager schedules a new connection after `min(10000, 500 * 2^attempts)` milliseconds. That is 500 ms, 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, and then 10 s. A successful open resets `attempts` to 0. After each open, the manager resubscribes every channel. If the socket opened before, it then calls the `onReconnect` listeners, so screens fetch their REST snapshot again. A message sent when the socket was closed is lost, and the snapshot fetch makes up for it.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Screen
  participant Store as SharedStore
  participant Socket as SocketManager
  participant WS as Server WebSocket
  participant REST as REST API
  Screen->>Store: useShared(store, key)
  Store->>Socket: subscribe workspace channel
  Socket->>WS: subscribe message
  Store->>REST: GET the workspace tree
  WS-->>Socket: tree_patch
  Socket-->>Store: feed.update with the patch
  Store-->>Screen: new snapshot
  Note over Socket,WS: the connection closes
  Socket->>Socket: wait 500 ms times 2 to the power n, at most 10 s
  Socket->>WS: open a new socket, subscribe each channel
  Socket-->>Store: onReconnect callback
  Store->>REST: GET the workspace tree again
  Store-->>Screen: new snapshot
```

### Terminal frames

A terminal channel carries binary frames. `terminal(execution, handler)` subscribes to `term:<execution>`. `decodePtyFrame` reads a frame like this: byte 0 is the length `n` of the execution id, the next `n` bytes are the id, and the rest are terminal bytes. A frame shorter than `1 + n` bytes is dropped. The manager passes the bytes to each handler of that execution.

### Code hints

`hint(type, request)` asks for completions, signature help, or a supertype or implementation jump. It sends the request with a new number `id` and waits for the matching reply. The call resolves to `null` in these cases:

- The socket is not open.
- The server does not answer in 30 seconds (`HINT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`).
- A newer request of the same type replaces it. The manager settles the older request with `null`, because the server also stops it.
- The socket closes when the request waits.

[Code navigation](code-navigation.md) owns the server side.

## Shared stores and live data

Many components need the same data, for example the sessions tree. Without sharing, each component fetches the data and subscribes on its own. `SharedStore` in `src/lib/store.ts` gives one fetch and one socket subscription for each key. The hooks in `src/lib/live.ts` use it.

### How a store works

A store entry starts when its first reader subscribes. It then does three things: it calls `live(key, feed)` to attach the socket handler, it registers an `onReconnect` reload, and it calls `load(key, feed)` for the first value. The snapshot is `{ data, error, loading }`.

- A counter `gen` makes a late answer harmless. A load that finishes after a newer load started is ignored.
- When the last reader leaves, the store waits one timer tick (`setTimeout` 0) before it stops. A remount in the same tick, from `StrictMode` or a tab switch, then keeps the subscription.
- The last value stays cached after the last reader leaves. A screen that returns renders at once and refreshes in the background.
- `throttle(fn, ms)` calls `fn` at most once for each `ms`, with one trailing call.

### Stores and hooks

| Hook | Source | Live update |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useWorkspaceTree(ws)` | `GET .../tree` | `tree_patch` and `session_updated` on `workspace:<ws>`. The list keeps its sort by `updated_at`. |
| `useSessionSummaries(ws)` | `GET .../sessions` | `session_updated`. This list carries `yolo`, which the tree does not. |
| `useActivity(ws)` | `GET .../activity` | `activity` messages. |
| `useFileIndex(ws, key)` | `GET .../files` | A reload on `project_fs_changed`, at most once each second. |
| `useProjectChanges(ws, key)` | `GET .../changes` | The same reload. |
| `useWorkspaces()` | `GET /api/workspaces` | A reload on `workspace_updated` or `session_updated` on `home`, at most once each second. |
| `useSearch(ws, query)` | `GET .../search` | None. The request waits 100 ms after the last key. |
| `useSocketState()` | The socket manager | `onState`. |

Older hooks stay in `src/lib/hooks.ts`. `useAsync(load, deps)` loads data and reloads when `deps` change and after a reconnect. `useChannel(channel, handler)` subscribes for the life of a component. `useThrottled(fn, ms)` is the hook form of `throttle`. `useStoredFlag(key, initial)` keeps a boolean in `localStorage`.

### What happens when

- **The socket drops.** The status bar shows **Offline, reconnecting**. After the reconnect, every store and every `useAsync` reload their snapshot.
- **The server sends a patch before the snapshot arrives.** The result depends on the store. A store that already holds a value applies the patch to that value, and the snapshot then replaces it. `treeStore` has no value at this time, so it drops a `tree_patch` or a `session_updated` message. Only `summariesStore` starts from an empty list, so it keeps the update. The execution hook holds early deltas for this case, as the execution part below explains.
- **A search request fails.** `useSearch` returns `unavailable`, and the palette searches the rows it holds.

## Mock mode and the homepage shot

Mock mode runs the full console on fixtures with no server. Developers use it to build screens, and the test suite uses it for every test. Set `VITE_MOCK=1` or run `npm run dev:mock`. The vitest config sets `VITE_MOCK` to `1` for all tests.

- `mockApi` in `src/api/mock/mockApi.ts` implements the same `Api` type as `httpApi`. State such as settings, gates, lessons, and skills is mutable, so an answer or a save sticks until the page reloads.
- Each mock answer waits 80 ms and returns a `structuredClone` of its value. A thrown error becomes `HttpError` with status 404, like the missing-path answers of the server.
- The fixtures come from `fixtures.*.ts`, `mockCode.ts`, `mockGit.ts`, and `projectFiles.ts` in `src/api/mock/`. The mock sessions include one session for each gate kind.
- `mockSocket` opens 50 ms after creation. It streams the fixture deltas of running executions on `execution:<id>`, one item every 1800 ms (`STEP_MS`). It sends each terminal backlog 120 ms after the subscribe, then the live chunks, and it echoes `term_input` back. Under vitest it never opens, so tests have no timers.
- The URL query `?first-run` shows the first-run setup in mock mode.
- The status bar shows **Mock data** in place of the connection state.

The homepage shot is a mock build for the project site. `VITE_SHOT=1` (`vite --mode shot`) sets `isShot`. In this mode the router is a memory router that starts at the path in the `?path=` query, limited to `/w/` routes. The page around the iframe sends `ostra-shot` messages to open tabs and set the theme, and the console reports the tab or theme that the visitor picks. The build adds a `Content-Security-Policy` meta tag, because a static host cannot send the header that the server sends.

## Session board

The session board is the main screen of a task. Without it, a user cannot see which stage runs, which gate waits, or what the agents decided. `SessionScreen` in `src/screens/SessionScreen.tsx` renders the resource `session:<id>`. [Session pipeline](session-pipeline.md) explains the lanes, stages, and gates that it shows.

### Data and live updates

The screen loads `GET /api/sessions/{id}` and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events`. It subscribes to `session:<id>`. Each `session_event` adds a row to a live list and refreshes the detail at most once each 400 ms. A `session_updated` message replaces the summary. `mergeEvents` removes duplicates by `seq` and sorts by `seq`, so the snapshot and the live rows can overlap.

### What the board shows

From top to bottom, the board holds:

1. The header: title, the original request with tagged files and uploads, added context, status chips, cost, start time, the **YOLO** switch, **Pause** or **Continue**, and the stop button.
2. A banner when the session is paused, and a banner when YOLO is on and the session has not ended.
3. One `BlockerNotice` for each active security block.
4. The lane stepper, with one entry for each lane. `laneStates` builds it from the stage cards. A lane with no stage is `skipped` if the session completed or a later lane started, and `pending` otherwise.
5. Two tabs: **Overview** (with the count of open gates) and **Decisions** (with the count of decisions).

The **Overview** tab holds the **Waiting for you** gates, the completion report, **Decided for you** (the YOLO decision list, split from the report by `splitDecidedForYou`), the context composer, the lane panel, the phase graph, a button for the answered gates, and a button for the event log.

### Rules of the board

- **Default lane.** `defaultLane` picks the lane of the current gate. If no gate is current, it picks the first lane that waits for the user, then the first current lane, then the session lane.
- **Gate order.** `openGatesInOrder` puts the current gate first. The other open gates follow, oldest first. `answeredGates` sorts the newest answer first.
- **Gate anchor.** A hash `#gate-<id>` scrolls to that gate. If the gate is answered, the board first expands the answered list and selects the **Overview** tab.
- **Phase graph.** The graph shows for the lanes `design`, `build`, `review`, and `test` (`PHASE_LANES`). A phase starts when every phase that it depends on has passed review. Phases of one project run one at a time, and phases of different projects run in parallel. If a phase fails, the phases that depend on it leave the queue.
- **Security block.** `activeSecurityBlocks` keeps the latest `security_block` event for each project, phase, and test flag. An event with no findings clears the block. The banner has no dismiss action, because only a passing review clears the block, and the session cannot complete when the block is open.
- **Event log.** The log shows one line for each event: the time, the event type with `_` written as `.` and padded to 20 characters, and a description.

### Header controls

- **YOLO** switch: `POST /api/sessions/{id}/yolo`. It is disabled when the session ended. The change applies from the next gate or tool call.
- **Pause** or **Continue**: `POST .../pause` or `POST .../resume`. Pause stops every running agent and starts nothing new. Each agent resumes where it stopped. A user can still answer gates and add context when the session is paused.
- **Stop the session**: a dialog asks for confirmation, then `POST .../stop`. Ostra cancels each running execution, denies each waiting permission ask, and marks the session failed. Files that agents already wrote stay in the project.

### Context composer

The composer adds text, tagged files, and uploads to a running pipeline session. It sends `POST /api/sessions/{id}/amend` with `delivery` set to `queue` or `now`.

- **Queue for the next step** (Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter) delivers the context at the next step. Running agents finish first.
- **Send now** asks for confirmation. Ostra stops the running executions, and each one starts again from the beginning with the context. The progress of those runs is lost, the files that they wrote stay, and their spend stays on the bill. The button is disabled when nothing runs, because queued context is used right away.
- An empty form shows the message to write the context, tag a file with `@`, or upload one.

[Engine runtime](engine-runtime.md) owns the amend flow.

## Gates and decisions

A gate stops the pipeline until the user answers. The console must send an answer in the exact shape that the engine accepts. `src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` mirrors `runner::validate_answer` of the engine, so the form catches an invalid answer before the request. `GateCard` in `src/features/gates/GateCard.tsx` renders one gate. It shows the answer form when the gate is open and the recorded answer after the answer.

### Gate kinds and answer shapes

| Gate kind | Answer kind | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `questions` | Each question needs an option or a free-text **Other** answer. The recommended option comes first and has the label **(Recommended)**. |
| `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` | `approval` | **Approve** or **Request changes**. A change request needs text, because the engine rejects an empty one. The gate opens only after a fact-check PASS, and the card shows LOW findings. |
| `closing_gate` | `closing` | For each project, a check box for tests and a check box for docs. Only the questions that the gate asks appear. |
| `permission` | `permission` | **Allow once**, **Always in this workspace** (with the rule that it adds), or **Deny**. |
| `skill_approval` | `skills` | For each skill: `generate`, `regenerate`, `reuse`, or `drop`. |
| `fact_check_recurring`, `review_cap`, `stuck`, `phase_blocked`, `harness_failure`, `execution_failed`, `budget_reached`, `implementation_review` | `choice` | The buttons in the next table. |

### Choice options

| Gate kind | Option and label | Text field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `another-round` **Run another fact-check round**, `stop` **Stop the session** | Optional for the first |
| `review_cap` | `another-pass` **Run another fix and review pass**, `stop` **Stop and block the phase** | Optional for the first |
| `stuck` | `fact` **Re-run with this fact**, `block` **Block this work** | Required for `fact` |
| `phase_blocked` | `retry` **Retry the phase**, `leave` **Leave the phase blocked** | Optional for `retry` |
| `harness_failure` | `retry` **Retry after login**, `native` **Run on the native executor** | None |
| `execution_failed` | `retry` **Retry the execution**, `abandon` **Abandon this work** | None |
| `budget_reached` | `raise` **Raise the budget**, `stop` **Stop the session** | Optional for `raise` |
| `implementation_review` | `done` **Accept the implementation**, `feedback` **Send feedback** | Required for `feedback` |

For `budget_reached` with `raise`, text must be a positive dollar amount such as `10` or `$12.50`. An empty text adds the budget again. `choiceAnswer` returns an error message if a required text is empty or the amount is not valid.

### What happens when

- **The user answers.** `POST /api/gates/{id}/answer` sends `{ answer }`. The form shows the error text if the call fails. It dims when the call runs.
- **The gate is answered.** The card shows one summary line from `answerSummary`. The source `yolo` marks an answer that YOLO gave. The source `engine` shows **Closed by Ostra:** before the summary.
- **A gate kind has no form.** The card falls back to the design `GateCard` with the title and explanation.

### Decisions

The **Decisions** tab lists each judge decision as a choice, a reason, and the basis. `DecisionsPanel` in `src/screens/session/SidePanels.tsx` renders it. A decision shows **Override** only if `can_override` is true, which means that the work that depends on it has not started. The override dialog shows the decision output as JSON. The user must write valid JSON in the same shape and must give a reason. The call is `POST /api/decisions/{id}/override` with `{ output, reason }`. The record keeps the reason. [Judges and YOLO](judges-and-yolo.md) owns the judge outputs.

## Execution screen

An execution is one agent run. The screen shows what the agent did and lets the user cancel or resume it. `ExecutionScreen` in `src/screens/ExecutionScreen.tsx` renders `exec:<id>`.

### Header and controls

The header shows the agent name, the run label, the project, a status chip, the stage, the executor chip, the model, and the duration. A select lists the other runs of the same agent and project. The buttons follow these rules:

- **Cancel** shows when the execution runs. It calls `POST /api/executions/{id}/cancel`.
- **Resume** shows when the run has ended, `can_resume` is true, the run is not a read-only inspect session (`!inspects`), and no terminal exists (`!e.has_terminal`). It calls `POST .../resume`.
- **Open the session** shows only when all of these conditions are true:
  - The run has ended.
  - The run is not itself a read-only inspect run (`!inspects`).
  - The run has the `terminal` stream.
  - The run has a harness session id (`native_session_id`) and a parent session.
  - The run has no live terminal (`!e.has_terminal`).

The button **Open the session** calls `POST .../inspect`, which reopens the harness session read-only. The screen then opens the new execution. A banner on that execution explains that Ostra refuses every tool call, because the work is done.

### Usage strip and spawn parameters

The usage strip shows **Input**, **Output**, **Cache reads**, **Tool calls**, **Cache / call** (only if tool calls exist), **Build time** (only if it is more than 0), **Cost**, and **Duration**. A clock ticks each second when the run is active (`useNow`). The collapsible **Spawn parameters** part shows the exact parameter block that the agent received (`spawn_block`), the report path as a link, and the harness session id. See [Agents and prompts](agents-and-prompts.md) for the spawn contract.

### Activity stream

A native run uses the **Activity** stream. `useActivity` loads the REST snapshot and then applies each `execution_delta`. It keeps these rules:

- `applyDelta` ignores a delta with a `seq` at or below the last `seq` that it saw. A snapshot and the live stream can therefore overlap.
- The hook holds deltas that arrive before the snapshot and applies them after it.
- After a reconnect, the hook fetches only the items after the last `seq`.
- Consecutive text deltas merge into one block, and so do thinking deltas. A tool call collects its policy decision, live output, and result.
- The cost of one native model response is divided evenly over the tool calls of that response.

Tool paths show relative to `repo_root`. An `Edit`, `Write`, or `ApplyPatch` call shows an inline diff with its count of added and removed lines. A `Write` shows the first 400 lines (`MAX_WRITE_LINES`) and then a note with the count of lines not shown. A tool output over 20000 characters is cut (`MAX_OUTPUT`). A `Bash` call shows `$ <command>` and the output.

A call that the policy refused or asked about shows its layer, rule, and reason. For a refusal by a guard, it also shows advice that `GUARD_ADVICE` holds for the guard id. For a deny rule it points to the workspace settings. For an ask it offers to allow the call once or for the workspace. [Policy engine](policy-guards.md) owns the guards.

### Terminal stream and tool calls

A harness run uses the **Terminal** stream, and a second tab **Tool calls** (`HookLog`). The log has one row for each call that the hook bridge saw. It shows the tool, the input, the decision (**Allowed**, **Denied**, **Asking you**, **Asked you**, or **No decision**), the rule, and the time. [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) owns the hook bridge.

### Permission notice

When a run waits for a permission answer, `PermissionNotice` shows above the stream with **Allow once** and **Deny**. The holder is named **The hook bridge** for a terminal run and **Ostra** for a native run. If another gate names the run, such as a stuck or failed gate, the banner **A gate waits on this run** links to the gate on the session board.

### What happens when

- **A gate opens or closes.** The screen reloads the execution within 400 ms, because `pending_gate` comes from the fold of the session.
- **An execution starts, resumes, or finishes in the session.** The screen reloads the session detail within 800 ms for the list of sibling runs.
- **The execution cannot load.** The screen shows **Ostra could not load this execution** with **Try again**.
- **The run ended with an error.** A banner shows the error text.

## Terminal safety and the xterm screen

A harness runs inside a PTY on the server, and the console shows its terminal output. The output comes from a program that can print any byte sequence, so the console treats it as untrusted. `src/screens/execution/terminalSafety.ts` holds the two rules that protect the user and the harness.

### Query replies are muted

A terminal program can send a query, such as a request for the cursor position or the device attributes, and wait for a reply. The server answers each query once, whether any browser or no browser watches the run. If xterm.js also answers in the browser, a second reply reaches the harness as typed input. `muteQueryReplies` registers a handler that returns `true` for each query, so xterm sends no reply. The handlers cover these sequences:

| Kind | Sequences |
| --- | --- |
| CSI | `n` and `? n` (status reports), `c`, `> c`, and `= c` (device attributes), `$ p` and `? $ p` (mode reports), `> q` (version), `? u` (keyboard mode) |
| CSI `t` | Only the window report values 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, and 21 (`WINDOW_REPORTS`). Other values move or resize the window, and xterm ignores them. |
| DCS | `$ q` and `+ q` |
| OSC | 4, 10, 11, 12, 17, and 19, only when the data contains the query mark `?` |

### Links need confirmation

`linkHandler` sets `allowNonHttpProtocols` to `false`. `safeLinkTarget` accepts only `http:` and `https:` addresses. A click shows the address in a `window.confirm` dialog. Only after the user agrees does the page open the address in a new window with `noopener,noreferrer`. The reason: the output is untrusted, so only web pages open, and only after the user sees the address.

### The xterm screen

`XtermScreen` in `src/screens/execution/XtermScreen.tsx` creates the terminal. It uses a scrollback of 10000 lines, the font size 12.5, the line height 1.2, and `allowProposedApi: false`. The colors come from the `--term-*` design tokens, and the pane is dark in both themes. The screen subscribes to `term:<execution>`. The first frame after the subscribe is the backlog: the screen so far for a live run, or the stored transcript for an ended run.

- **Input.** In live mode, `term.onData` sends `term_input` with the typed text. In read-only mode, input is off.
- **Size.** `FitAddon` fits the terminal when it mounts, when the container resizes, when the fonts finish loading, and after a reconnect. In live mode the screen sends `term_resize` with the new columns and rows. A read-only replay sends no resize.
- **Mode.** `terminalMode` returns `live` if a PTY exists or the run is active, `replay` if an ended run has a stored transcript, and `none` otherwise.

`TerminalStream` adds the frame. In `replay` mode a banner says that input is off and offers **Resume** when `can_resume` is true. In `none` mode a banner says that no terminal output was stored. The **Maximize** button fills the pane. **Escape** restores it, but only when the focus is outside the terminal. Inside the terminal, Escape belongs to the harness, so only Shift+Escape restores it.

## Overview, settings, and workspace pages

The overview and the settings pages configure what Ostra does in a workspace. [Workspaces, projects, and settings](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the meaning of each setting.

### Overview and New task

`WorkspaceScreen` renders `ws:overview`. It shows banners for settings problems, for a workspace with no project, and for projects that are not initialized. It then shows the **New task** form and the sessions table.

- A settings banner shows the count of problems. **Fix it** or **Fix N** calls `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/settings/fix`. **Open settings** opens the settings tab. An agent whose route does not resolve cannot start, so the user must fix the problem before work.
- A pipeline task cannot target an uninitialized project. Each banner button opens the project at **Initialize <key>**. **Check again** reloads the workspace.
- **New task** sends `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/sessions` with the request, the options `tests`, `docs`, and `yolo` (and `track` if chosen), the pinned projects, the tagged files, and the upload ids. The **Start** button needs a non-empty request, no upload in progress, and at least one initialized project. Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter starts the task.
- The track buttons are **Auto**, **Light**, and **Full**. **Auto** lets Ostra pick after research. **Light** builds and reviews with no spec or plan. **Full** adds a spec, a fact-check, and a plan that the user approves.
- If **Write docs** is on, a select lists the books. The default is a new book or one that matches the projects.
- The YOLO box starts from the workspace default `yolo.default`. A banner states that guards, deny rules, the fact-check PASS requirement, and security blocks still apply.
- A text typed with `@` tags a file. `@project/path` names a project file, and `@_artifacts/<path>` names an artifact. A file can also be dropped from the Files tab or chosen as an upload. [Artifacts and structured documents](artifacts-and-documents.md) owns the upload rules.
- **Turn into task** from the quick dock fills the request once through `taskDraft`.

The sessions table filters by status, kind, project, and text. The status tabs are **All**, **Active** (running or waiting), **Waiting**, **Completed**, and **Failed** (failed or stalled). Each tab shows the count of sessions that it lists when the other filters stay the same. The text filter matches all words against the title, request, id, stage, category, and projects. Rows sort by the newest update.

### Settings screen

`SettingsScreen` renders `ws:settings` as forms. The form model in `src/screens/workspace/settingsForm.ts` is not the settings object, so a text field keeps what the user typed, such as a trailing newline in a rule list. `fromForm` derives the settings and the local issues from the form.

The tabs are **General**, **Projects**, **Git**, **Routing**, **MCP servers**, **Permissions**, **Instructions**, **Notifications**, **Shortcuts**, and **Sign-in**. `tabOf` maps a settings path to its tab. Each tab shows the count of issues that it holds.

- **General.** The workspace name, the YOLO default, the limits (budget and parallel work), and a **Delete workspace** panel. Delete removes `.ostra/workspace.toml` and `.ostra/workspace.db` in the workspace root. Project folders and session folders stay on disk.
- **Projects.** The imported projects, with key, path, and stack.
- **Git.** The git credentials. A key file larger than 64 KB (`MAX_KEY_BYTES`) is refused, because a private key is a few kilobytes and a larger file is the wrong file.
- **Routing.** The executor, model, and effort for each agent, and the route for each phase complexity. A phase route wins over an agent route. The native provider credentials are in this tab too.
- **MCP servers.** One row for each server, with status, refresh, sign-in, and sign-out. [Integrations](integrations.md) owns MCP.
- **Permissions.** The permission mode, the tool enforcement, the sandbox mode, the network mode, the allowed hosts, the decoy files, the allow, ask, and deny rules, and the read-only global rules.
- **Instructions.** The text for all agents and for one agent.
- **Notifications.** The push toggle. [Integrations](integrations.md) owns Web Push.
- **Shortcuts.** The key bindings of this browser, as the shortcut part below describes.
- **Sign-in.** The browsers that are signed in. A revoke signs a browser out at once.

### Settings editor rules

`useSettingsEditor` in `src/screens/workspace/useSettingsEditor.ts` follows these rules:

1. If the form is dirty, it calls `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/validate` 400 ms after the last change (`VALIDATE_DELAY_MS`). Issues from the server and from the form show next to their fields.
2. **Save** is disabled when the form is clean, when a check or a save runs, and when any issue exists. The call is `PATCH /api/workspaces/{ws}`. The status text then reads **Saved to .ostra/workspace.toml**, and a banner says that the next execution uses the settings, with no restart.
3. If the save fails with issues, the editor shows them and jumps to the tab of the first issue.
4. If the file changes elsewhere and the form has edits, a banner offers **Load the saved settings**, and a save overwrites the file. If the form has no edits, the editor follows the file.
5. A fix from `WorkspaceDetail.fixes` has a `path`, a `label`, and a `value`. **Apply** puts the value in the form, and the user saves it with the other changes.
6. A URL anchor `#setting:<dotted key>` opens the tab of the field and rings the field for 2400 ms (`FLASH_MS`).

A model route is one of five kinds: not set, `default`, a tier (`fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, or `frontier`), a custom model name, or a per-executor table written as `executor = model, ...`. The efforts are `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. The complexities are `low`, `medium`, and `high`. Only `implementer` and `write-test` have routes for each complexity (`COMPLEXITY_AGENTS`). The agents `judge` and `quick-answer` always run on the native executor (`NATIVE_ONLY`).

### Pending commands

A folder file, such as `.ostra/project.toml`, can hold commands that Ostra runs. If the file changed outside Ostra, the commands wait for approval. `PendingCommandsNotice` shows a banner on every workspace screen except settings. `PendingCommandsBanner` on the settings screen lists each item with its kind: MCP server, Language server, Code provider, Format command, Allow rule, or Project outside the workspace. The approval calls `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/approve`. Ostra runs none of these commands until the user approves them.

## Cost, memory, skills, and docs screens

Four screens show data that belong to the workspace and not to one session.

### Cost

`CostScreen` renders `ws:cost`. A segmented control selects **This week** or **All time**. The week starts at `WorkspaceActivity.week_since` from the server (today and the six days before it), so the totals match the status bar. The request is `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/cost` with `since` for the week.

The summary strip shows the total, today, the runs, the cache reads, the tool calls, the cache reads for each tool call, and the build time. Four tables follow: **By session**, **By stage**, **By agent**, and **By executor**. Each table sorts by cost, highest first. It shows the runs, input, output, cache reads, cache writes with a 5-minute and a 1-hour lifetime, the cache for each tool call, the build time, the cost, and the share. The key `side-panel` shows as **Side-panel questions**.

The screen explains two numbers. Cache reads for each tool call show how much context each step reads again, and the number grows when an agent loops. Build time shows how long agents spend in build and test commands, because a run with many consecutive build failures spends without progress. The screen reloads at most once every 2000 ms after an `activity` or `session_updated` message. A cost table code comment states that Anthropic prices cache writes at 1.25 times the input rate for 5 minutes and 2 times for 1 hour.

### Memory

`MemoryScreen` renders `ws:memory`. A lesson is a project fact that an agent recorded because it cost real effort to find. Agents recall lessons before they work in an area and after a failure, so a wrong or stale lesson misleads them. The screen lets a user edit or delete any lesson.

- The project picker is a set of tabs for 6 or fewer projects (`MAX_TABS`), and a select for more.
- The search box waits 250 ms (`SEARCH_DELAY_MS`) and calls `GET .../memory?q=`.
- The table shows **Area**, **Lesson**, and **Recorded by**. The calls are `PATCH .../memory` to save and `DELETE .../memory?id=` to delete. Delete asks for confirmation.
- The URL `?project=<key>` or the anchor `#project:<key>` picks a project. The anchor `#lesson:<key>:<id>` selects and rings a lesson.

[Storage](storage.md) owns the lesson store and its recall.

### Skills

`SkillsScreen` renders `ws:skills`. Only skills registered in `.ostra/project.toml` reach agents, through the repo brief. The screen lists, for each project, the registered skills and the skills in a harness folder such as `.claude/skills/`. A skill shows one of these states: the harness folder, **File missing**, **Not registered**, or its kind (`creation`, `test`, `convention`, or `other`).

- **New skill** opens an editor with a `SKILL.md` template that has `name` and `description` front matter. The save call is `PUT .../skills/{name}`.
- A harness skill has **Adopt**. It copies the skill into `.agents/skills/` under a name, a kind, and a use-for text, and it registers it.
- A warning says that agents do not load a skill that is not registered, and an error says that `SKILL.md` is missing.
- The URL `?project=<key>` narrows the list. The search box filters by name, description, and component type.

[Agents and prompts](agents-and-prompts.md) owns skills.

### Documentation books

`DocsScreen` lists the workspace books, newest first. `BookScreen` renders `book:<id>` as Markdown pages with a sidebar, a table of contents, search (at least 2 characters, `MIN_QUERY`), **Delete**, and **Export HTML**. `bookModel.ts` builds the pages from the book. [Documentation books](documentation-books.md) owns the book format.

The export writes one HTML file. The file has the Content-Security-Policy `default-src 'none'`, `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, and `img-src data:` (`EXPORT_CSP`). The function `clean()` in `web/src/features/docs/exportHtml.ts` strips the page before the export. It follows these rules:

- It removes scripts, frames, objects, forms, inputs, buttons, and other elements that load or run code (the `DROP` list).
- It removes every attribute that starts with `on`, so event handlers are gone.
- It removes every `src` that is not a `data:image/` URL. An image from another origin is therefore removed.
- It removes an `href` or `xlink:href` only when the value does not start with `#`, `http:`, `https:`, or `mailto:`.
- It keeps links to other origins as plain anchors and adds `rel=noreferrer` to them.

The file loads nothing and runs nothing, because of the `default-src 'none'` policy and the `src` removal. A reader can still click a link to another origin, and the browser then leaves the file.

## Project, dependency graph, and artifact screens

These screens show one project or one session file.

### Project screen

`ProjectScreen` renders `project:<key>`. The header shows the key, the init status chip, the checked-out branch (read from `.git/HEAD`) or **not a git checkout**, the path, and the stack. **Pull** fast-forwards the branch from its upstream with `POST .../pull`. **Browse files** switches the left dock to the Files tab. Two tabs follow: **Overview** and **Dependencies**.

The overview depends on `init_status`:

| Status | What the overview shows |
| --- | --- |
| `missing` | A **Folder missing** banner and **Remove from workspace**. Removing deletes nothing on disk. |
| `not_initialized` | **Initialize this project**. The button calls `POST .../init` and opens the init session. |
| `initializing` | The progress panel and **Open the init session**. |
| `initialized` | The commands, the skills, the module map, the lessons, and maintenance actions. |

The init stepper has six steps: **Detect**, **Scout**, **Propose skills**, **Your approval**, **Generate**, and **Inventory**.

`CommandsPanel` edits the seven commands in `.ostra/project.toml`: `build`, `test`, `test_one`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `format`, and `run`. A blank value removes the command. The save call is `PUT .../commands`. A 422 answer places each issue on its field (`commands.<name>`). Agents and the engine read the profile for each execution, so a saved command applies to the next run.

### Dependency graph

The **Dependencies** tab draws `GET .../code/graph`. The view is one of four: every package, the files of one package, the neighborhood of one file, or the calls of one definition. The server numbers the columns, and a node uses nodes to its right. `layout` sorts each column by the average row of its neighbors, so links cross less. A column of more than 10 rows (`MAX_ROWS`) wraps into side-by-side lanes. The focused type lists up to 12 members inside its box (`MAX_INLINE_MEMBERS`).

| Constant | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_W`, `NODE_H` | 208, 44 | Node width and height in pixels. |
| `MEMBER_H` | 20 | Height of one member row. |
| `COL_GAP`, `ROW_GAP`, `LANE_GAP` | 80, 14, 16 | Gaps between columns, rows, and lanes. |
| `PAD`, `HEADER` | 20, 28 | Outer padding and the header height of the file and symbol views. |
| `MIN_ZOOM`, `MAX_ZOOM` | 0.2, 2.5 | Zoom limits. |

**Rebuild the index** calls `POST .../code/reindex`. If the index size cap left files out, the banner says so. A chip **some nodes or links left out** shows when the graph is truncated. [Code navigation](code-navigation.md) owns the index and its caps.

### Artifact screen

`ArtifactScreen` renders `artifact:<path>`, a file in the session folder. The call is `GET /api/artifacts?path=`. The kind is the `ArtifactRef.kind` of the owning session, or it comes from the file name: `research`, `spec`, `plan`, `phase`, `report`, `ledger`, `completion`, or `upload`.

- An outline of the headings up to level 3 sits beside the content. The outline marks the last heading above the top of the view. A `#<id>` hash scrolls to a heading with an offset of 16 px.
- A research, spec, plan, or phase file that has a typed document renders as chapters with marks for fact-check findings. A button switches to plain Markdown.
- A spec or plan shows **Fact-check PASS** and approval chips from the stage cards and gates. Specs, plans, and phase files also show a note on how to read EARS requirements. The user can hide the note, and the choice is stored in `localStorage` under `ostra.earsNoteHidden`.
- A review ledger renders in a lazy Monaco diff.
- `Markdown` renders agent-written text. It renders no raw HTML, and it loads an image only from a `data:image/` address, because an image address that an agent chose makes the browser request that address.

[Artifacts and structured documents](artifacts-and-documents.md) owns the document formats.

## Files and the editor

A user must read a project file, see what a session changed, and fix a small thing without leaving the console. `FileScreen` renders `file:<key>:<path>`. It reloads the file, the diff, and the code data when `project_fs_changed` names the path.

### Views

The views are **File**, **Rendered** (for Markdown files that have content), and **Changes** (a unified diff against HEAD, when a session changed the file). The default view is **Changes** if a diff exists. The header shows which agent and phase changed the file, for example `Implementer · Phase 2`. A `#L<n>` hash marks a line.

The File view is one Monaco editor. In read-only mode a click on a name selects it for the code pane beside the editor: the outline, the usages, and the dependencies of the name. A gutter mark shows each changed line as **Added**, **Changed**, or **Removed below**. A click on a mark shows the HEAD text in a zone under the block.

### Edit and save

The pencil starts an edit. `useFileEdit` in `src/screens/project/code/useFileEdit.ts` keeps the edit state. Each save sends the hash that the edit started from (`base_hash`), and the server refuses the save if the file changed since. This stops one writer from silently overwriting another.

- **Conflict.** A 409 answer with the issue path `base_hash` shows a conflict. The file also reloads on `project_fs_changed`, so the conflict can show before the user saves. **Reload** takes the disk version and drops the draft. The other choice saves the draft over the disk version.
- **Clean draft.** A draft with no change follows the disk version without a message.
- **Discard.** The first press with unsaved changes asks for confirmation. The second press discards. If nothing changed, **Done** leaves the edit.
- **Page close.** A dirty draft registers a `beforeunload` warning.
- **Save shortcut.** Cmd+S or Ctrl+S saves in the editor and elsewhere on the screen, instead of the browser save dialog.
- **Locked file.** A file that is larger than the size that Ostra reads for the browser, a file that is not UTF-8 text, and a file with `read_only` cannot be edited. The screen says which reason applies.
- **New file.** The hash `#edit` opens a file that the Files tab just created in edit mode, once.

### Monaco setup

`src/components/monaco.ts` bundles Monaco locally, because the app runs on localhost and must not fetch code from a CDN. It imports each editor contribution by name, because `editor.api` loads none and `editor.main` loads every language worker. It registers 11 language definitions: Go, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Markdown, Python, Ruby, Rust, SQL, TypeScript, and YAML. `languageOf` maps 17 file extensions to language ids and falls back to `plaintext`. The two themes are `ostra-dark` and `ostra-light`. The font is JetBrains Mono at 12.5 px.

The editor keeps the scroll, cursor, and folds of the last 200 files (`MAX_VIEW_STATES`), because a tab switch unmounts the editor. It tints at most 2000 occurrences of the selected name (`MAX_TINTS`).

### Editor commands

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Cmd+S or Ctrl+S | Save. |
| Cmd+F or Ctrl+F | Find. |
| Cmd+Alt+F on a Mac, Ctrl+H elsewhere | Replace. Alt+R switches the pattern mode, and the replacement can name groups as `$1`. |
| Alt+Up, Alt+Down | Move the line. |
| Cmd+Shift+I or Ctrl+Shift+I | **Show base class**. |
| Cmd+Shift+M or Ctrl+Shift+M | **Show implementation**. |
| Cmd+click or Ctrl+click on a name | On a use, go to the definition. On a definition, list the usages. |

In read-only mode, find works in place. Replace and the line moves start an edit first. If the file is locked, the editor shows the reason.

### Hints over the socket

`registerHints` in `src/screens/project/code/hints.ts` registers one completion provider and one signature provider for every language. Each request goes over the socket as `code_complete` or `code_signature`, with the unsaved text, the 1-based line, and the 0-based UTF-16 column. Monaco columns are 1-based, so the code converts both ways. The completion trigger characters are `.`, `:`, `>`, `/`, `@`, `#`, `<`, `"`, and `'`. The signature triggers are `(`, `,`, and `<`, and `)` retriggers. The server answers an empty list after a character that its language does not use. A model answers only when `bindModel` names its project file.

A jump sends `code_navigate` with the target `supertypes` or `implementations`. A reply with one place goes there. A reply with many places opens a picker. A reply with none shows a note. If the user has unsaved changes, a jump to another file shows a message to save or discard first, because leaving the editor drops the changes.

### Dependency files

`DependencyFileScreen` renders `dep:<key>:<uri>`, a file outside the project that a language server pointed at, for example a library source. The screen is always read-only, and it says that the file belongs to a dependency. Base class and implementation jumps work only in project files.

## Setup wizard

A new user needs a workspace before the console is useful. The setup wizard creates one and checks the machine. The code is in `src/screens/setup/`. [Running Ostra](running-ostra.md) owns the first-run flow of the server.

### When the wizard shows

`Home` at `/` shows the full-screen `Onboarding` if `GET /api/onboarding` has no `onboarded_at`, the machine has 0 workspaces, and the user did not skip it. The menu item **Run the setup guide again** shows it at any time. **New workspace** opens `NewWorkspaceDialog`, which skips the **Welcome** step. When the wizard ends, `Home` calls `POST /api/onboarding/complete` and ignores a failure of that call. It then opens the new workspace. On a phone, `MWizard` does the same job.

### Steps

| Step | Rule to continue |
| --- | --- |
| **Welcome** | None. |
| **Check this machine** | None. It shows the keys and the harnesses from `GET /api/environment`. |
| **Name and folder** | The name is not empty, and the folder is a chosen absolute path (it can start with `~/`) that does not end in a separator. The folder can be new, because Ostra creates it. |
| **Add projects** | None. The user imports folders or clones repositories. |
| **Defaults** | None. The permission mode, the routing preset, YOLO, and push. |
| **Review** | The server validation must find no issue. |

The name follows the folder name until the user types a name. The initial folder is `~/`. A project key must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` and must be unique. `suggestKey` makes a key from a folder name with the same slug rule as the server.

The **Defaults** step offers the permission modes `default`, `acceptEdits`, and `plan`. It does not offer `bypass`. The routing presets are **All native**, **Implementers on Codex**, and **Implementers on Claude Code**. A harness preset appears only if that harness is installed and logged in. A harness preset moves `implementer` and `write-test` to the harness (`HARNESS_AGENTS`). The defaults are YOLO off and push on.

### Create flow

1. On **Review**, the wizard calls `POST /api/workspaces/validate` 150 ms after the last change. `stepForIssue` maps each issue path to a step, so the user can jump back.
2. The review shows a preview of `.ostra/workspace.toml` from `tomlFor`. The server adds the seeded model routes and limits.
3. **Create** calls `POST /api/workspaces`. A checklist advances one row each 420 ms (`TASK_MS`) and holds on its last row until the server answers.
4. A clone runs after the workspace exists, because the clone route needs the workspace. Each clone calls `POST .../clone`. A failed clone leaves the workspace in place and shows its reason.
5. The user can start the init session of a project. `useInitAfterCreate` opens that session, or the project screen if the start fails.

### Install and login terminals

The **Check this machine** step offers **Install** or **Log in** for a harness CLI. The button calls `POST /api/harnesses/{harness}/setup` with the action. The server returns a terminal, and the wizard shows it in `XtermScreen`. When the command exits, the server sends `harness_status` on `home`, and the wizard reloads the check if the statuses differ from the page.

The provider credentials form saves an API key or an auth token (Bearer) with `PATCH /api/providers/{name}`. An environment variable takes precedence over the saved value. The git credentials form takes an HTTPS token or an SSH private key. [Server security](server-security.md) owns how the server stores secrets.

## Mobile shell

A phone has no room for tabs and docks. At a width of 720 px or less (`MOBILE_QUERY = "(max-width: 720px)"`), `useIsMobile` is true, and `WorkspaceShell` renders `MobileShell` in place of the desktop shell. The value follows rotation and resizes. It is always false in shot mode.

### Structure

`MobileShell` in `src/mobile/MobileShell.tsx` shows one screen at a time under a header. The header has Back, the title with a sub-title (`mobileTitle`), and buttons for **Search**, **Ask a quick question**, and **Menu**. On the overview, a workspace mark opens the menu. The menu, the search, and the quick question are bottom sheets with `role="dialog"` and the labels **Menu**, **Search**, and **Ask a quick question**. The footer shows the connection (**Live**, **Connecting**, **Offline**, or **Mock data**), the running count, the waiting gates, and the spend of today.

The shell provides the same `ConsoleContext` as the desktop shell, with these differences:

- `nav.tabs` is empty, `keep` does nothing, and `close` goes back.
- Each pushed screen stores its `depth` in the history state. Back goes to the previous entry when `depth` is more than 0. Otherwise it replaces the URL with the overview. A deep link or a push notification starts with depth 0, so Back never leaves the workspace.
- `open` with `push: true` creates a history entry even for the same id, so Back closes a sub-page. The desktop shell ignores `push`.
- `browseFiles` opens the project screen.
- The keyboard shortcut handler does not exist. It lives only in the desktop `Shell`.

### Screens

| Resource | Mobile screen |
| --- | --- |
| `ws:overview` | `MHome`: the gate call-out, **New task**, the session list with the filters **All**, **Active**, **Blocked** (waiting, stalled, paused), and **Done**, and the projects. |
| `ws:settings` | `MSettings`. |
| `ws:cost`, `ws:memory`, `ws:skills` | `MWorkspace`. Search waits 250 ms. |
| `ws:docs`, `book:<id>`, `dep:<key>:<uri>` | The shared `DocsScreen`, `BookScreen`, and `DependencyFileScreen`. The last two scroll themselves (`mobileFills`). |
| `session:<id>` | `MSession` with the tabs **Phases**, **Executions**, **Artifacts**, **Decisions**, and **Event log**. It reuses `GateCard` and `BlockerNotice`. |
| `exec:<id>` | `MExecution`. It reuses `ActivityStream`, `PermissionNotice`, `TerminalStream`, and `useExecution`. |
| `artifact:<path>` | `MArtifact`. |
| `project:<key>`, `file:<key>:<path>` | `MProject` with the tabs **Overview**, **Files**, and **Git** (only for a git checkout). The URL hash picks the view: `#files`, `#git`, or `#dir=<folder>`. |

Two limits protect the phone. The Files search stops at 200 matches (`MAX_MATCHES`). The line diff of `lineDiff.ts` falls back to one replaced block when the table passes 4,000,000 cells (`MAX_CELLS`), because the table costs too much memory. The Git view polls every 10 seconds when the page is visible.

## Keyboard shortcuts

The console binds a few actions to keys. A browser or an operating system can take a key before the page sees it, and a key typed in a text field must type text. The code in `src/lib/shortcuts.ts` handles both problems. The shortcuts exist only in the desktop shell. Each workspace keeps its own bindings, in this browser only.

### Actions and defaults

| Action | Label | Default on a Mac | Default elsewhere |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `palette` | Open the command palette | Cmd+K | Ctrl+K |
| `dock` | Toggle the quick-question dock | Cmd+/ | Ctrl+/ |
| `sidebar` | Toggle the sidebar | Cmd+B | Ctrl+B |
| `files` | Show the Files tab | Shift+Cmd+E | Ctrl+Shift+E |
| `next-tab` | Next tab | Ctrl+Tab | Ctrl+Tab |
| `prev-tab` | Previous tab | Ctrl+Shift+Tab | Ctrl+Shift+Tab |
| `close-tab` | Close the focused tab | Cmd+W (reserved) | Ctrl+W (reserved) |
| `new-task` | New task | none | none |
| `settings` | Open settings | none | none |
| `theme` | Toggle light and dark theme | none | none |
| `keyboard-lock` | Lock or release keyboard shortcuts in fullscreen | none | none |

The `files` action toggles: if the Files tab is already open, it switches back to **Sessions**. `next-tab` and `prev-tab` follow the strip order and wrap at the ends. `new-task` opens the overview, and `settings` opens the settings tab.

A default is **reserved** if the browser keeps it unless the page can claim it. Only `close-tab` is reserved, because the browser uses Cmd+W or Ctrl+W to close its own tab. A reserved binding works only when the keyboard is locked or the console runs as an installed app (`runningAsApp`).

### Strokes and sequences

A stroke is a string like `ctrl+alt+shift+meta+<key>`, with the modifiers in that order. A shortcut is one stroke or two strokes pressed one after the other. `strokeOf` builds the stroke from a key event and follows these rules:

- A lone modifier key returns `null`.
- Shift and Alt change the character that a key types. For example Alt+K types a different character on a Mac. If Shift or Alt is held, or the character is not ASCII, the stroke uses the physical key (`KeyK` becomes `k`, `Digit1` becomes `1`, and `Slash`, `Backslash`, `Period`, `Comma`, `Semicolon`, `Quote`, `BracketLeft`, `BracketRight`, `Minus`, `Equal`, and `Backquote` become their characters).
- The space key is `Space`.
- The key names `Dead`, `Unidentified`, `Process`, `CapsLock`, `NumLock`, and `ScrollLock` use the physical key too.

`parseStroke` accepts a key of at most 24 characters, and it refuses a `+` inside the key unless the key is `+` itself.

### How a key press is handled

The shell registers one `keydown` listener on `window`. A stroke that types text (no Ctrl, Alt, or Cmd, and not a function key) is ignored when the focus is in a text field, a `contenteditable` element, a Monaco editor, or a terminal (`.ex-xterm`), unless a first stroke of a sequence is pending. Without this rule, typing a letter in a field could run an action.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["keydown event"] --> B{"strokeOf returns a stroke?"}
  B -- no --> X["ignore the event"]
  B -- yes --> C{"no pending stroke, stroke types text, focus in a field?"}
  C -- yes --> X
  C -- no --> D["matchStroke with the bindings"]
  D --> E{"Ctrl+W close-tab inside the terminal?"}
  E -- yes --> X
  E -- no --> F{"match.consume?"}
  F -- no --> X
  F -- yes --> G["preventDefault"]
  G --> H{"match.action set?"}
  H -- yes --> I["runShortcut(action)"]
  H -- no --> J["wait for the second stroke"]
```

`matchStroke` works on the live bindings: the bound actions that are not reserved, or all of them when `claimReserved` is true (keyboard locked or installed app). It checks in this order:

1. If a first stroke is pending and arrived within 1500 ms (`SEQUENCE_MS`), and a two-stroke binding matches both strokes, it returns that action.
2. If the stroke is the first stroke of any two-stroke binding, it stores the stroke as pending and consumes the event.
3. If a one-stroke binding matches, it returns that action.

The terminal keeps Ctrl+W, because Ctrl+W deletes a word in a shell.

### Change a shortcut

The **Shortcuts** tab of the settings (`ShortcutsSection`) records new keys. Click **Set** or **Change**, then press the keys. Press Esc to cancel. A second stroke must follow the first within 1200 ms (`SECOND_STROKE_MS`), or the first stroke becomes a one-stroke shortcut. A pair of strokes ends the recording at once. The recording box stops the console shortcuts, so a new shortcut does not run when the user presses it.

- **Conflict.** `conflicts` finds a binding with the same keys, or a binding whose first stroke is the new one-stroke shortcut (or the reverse). A banner offers to take the keys, and the old action becomes unbound.
- **Warnings.** `reservedBy` marks a stroke as `browser` or `system`. The tab warns that the browser or the system can keep it. It also warns that a stroke that types text works only outside text fields and editors.
- **Remove and reset.** **Remove** unbinds an action (a default becomes `null`). **Reset** puts one action back to its default. **Reset all** clears every change.

`reservedBy` uses these lists:

| List | Strokes |
| --- | --- |
| Browser, Mac | Cmd+W, Cmd+T, Cmd+N, Cmd+Q, Shift+Cmd+T, Shift+Cmd+N, Shift+Cmd+W |
| Browser, other | Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Shift+N, Ctrl+Shift+W |
| Browser, all | Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+PageUp, Ctrl+PageDown |
| System, Mac | Cmd+Tab, Shift+Cmd+Tab, Cmd+Space, Ctrl+Space, Cmd+H, Cmd+M, Ctrl+Up |
| System, other | Alt+Tab, Alt+Shift+Tab, Alt+F4, Ctrl+Alt+Delete, Ctrl+Alt+Left, Ctrl+Alt+Right, and every stroke with the Meta key |

### Storage

The bindings of a workspace are in `localStorage` under `ostra.shortcuts.<workspace id>` as `{ "v": 1, "bindings": { ... } }`. The value holds only the changes. An action that is missing keeps its default, and `null` unbinds it. `parseOverrides` drops anything that is malformed, because a user can edit the value. It drops unknown actions, a list of 0 or more than 2 strokes, and a stroke that does not parse. If the storage call fails, the change lasts in memory until the page reloads. A change fires the window event `ostra-shortcuts`, and the `storage` event updates other browser tabs. Every component and every tab of the browser therefore sees the change at once.

### Keyboard lock

The Keyboard Lock API sends browser-reserved keys to the page, but only in fullscreen and only in Chromium browsers. `useKeyboardLock` in `src/lib/keyboardLock.ts` enters fullscreen with `navigationUI: "hide"` and calls `navigator.keyboard.lock()`. If the lock fails after the page entered fullscreen, it leaves fullscreen. Leaving fullscreen releases the lock, and so does holding Escape. The palette shows the lock command and the status bar shows **Shortcuts locked** only where the browser supports it.

### Other keys

| Where | Key | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New task, Add context | Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter | Start the task, or queue the context. |
| Git commit box | Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter | Commit. |
| Tab strip | Ctrl or Cmd, Shift, and Left or Right | Move the focused tab. |
| Resize handle | Left or Right, with Shift for a larger step | Change the panel width. |
| Maximized terminal | Escape, or Shift+Escape inside the terminal | Restore the terminal. |

## Static content tables

Some help text is the same for every workspace, so the console keeps it in `src/content/` and not on the server. [Reference: web console and design constants](reference-web-limits.md) lists these tables.

- `LANES` and `STAGES` in `stages.ts` give each lane a title and a reason, and each stage a label, what it produces, and what it protects against. The session board and the cost screen use them.
- `ROUTE_KEYS` in `agents.ts` lists 15 route keys (14 agents and `judge`) with a one-line role. The routing form shows the role for each row. The list is a static copy, so a new agent needs a new row here.
- `TOOL_ENFORCEMENT`, `SANDBOX_MODES`, `SANDBOX_NETWORKS`, and `PERMISSION_MODES` give the label and help text of each choice in the permissions tab. An empty value follows the global setting. [Sandbox](sandbox.md) and [Policy engine](policy-guards.md) own the meaning of these choices.
- `UNSANDBOXED_EFFECTS` lists four effects of running agent commands with no sandbox. The permissions tab shows them in a warning when `runsUnsandboxed` is true: the mode is `off`, or the mode is `auto` on a machine with no sandbox backend.
- `DECOY_GUIDE` is a link to the sandbox guide on the repository, because the console ships no docs.

The choices of the permissions tab are:

| Setting | Choices |
| --- | --- |
| Tool enforcement | `disabled`, `enabled` |
| Sandbox mode | `required`, `auto`, `off` |
| Network mode | `none`, `allowlist`, `public`, `host` |
| Permission mode | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `bypass` |

## Browser storage and what the server keeps

The console writes a few values to the browser. Each value has one purpose.

| Key | Scope | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ostra.ui.<workspace id>` | One workspace | The layout and the tabs. The server also keeps a copy. |
| `ostra.shortcuts.<workspace id>` | One workspace | The changed key bindings. |
| `ostra.panels` | One browser | The widths of the left dock and the quick dock. |
| `ostra.theme` | One browser | The last theme, for pages with no workspace. |
| `ostra.earsNoteHidden` | One browser | Whether the EARS reading note is hidden. |

The server keeps the layout of each workspace (`GET` and `PATCH /api/workspaces/{ws}/ui`). It keeps no key bindings and no panel widths.

## Change and test the console

Follow these rules when you change the console:

- Open a resource only through `useNav().open`, because the shell must update the tab strip and the URL together.
- Add a screen by adding a resource type to `src/lib/resource.ts`, a case in `ScreenFor` in `src/screens/index.tsx`, and a case in `MobileScreenFor` in `src/mobile/screens.tsx`. Add the screen to `selfScrolling` if it scrolls itself.
- Add a REST route by adding a function to `httpApi` and the same function to `mockApi`. The `Api` type is `typeof httpApi`, so the compiler reports a missing mock function.
- Do not edit `src/api/gen/`. Change the Rust type and generate the file again.
- Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run check` in `web/` before you commit. [Testing](testing.md) lists the other commands of the repository.

The tests sit beside the code as `*.test.ts` and `*.test.tsx`. They run in jsdom with the mock API. Pure helpers hold the logic that matters, so tests need no browser: `tabsReducer`, `resource.ts`, `shortcuts.ts`, `gateAnswers.ts`, `board.ts`, `terminalSafety.ts`, `wizard.ts`, `settingsForm.ts`, and `sessionFilter.ts`.
