sections.title: Design system
sections.summary: The `@ostra/design` package: its exports, tokens, themes, components, lookup tables, brand mark, gallery, and docs renderer, and how the web console imports them.
sections.body:
Without a shared design package, each screen of the console defines its own colors, controls, and keyboard rules. The screens drift apart, and each control needs its own accessibility work. The `design/` folder holds one set of tokens and React components instead. The npm package `@ostra/design` exports them. The web console in `web/` uses them for every screen. This page covers the package layout, the tokens, the themes, the focus helpers, each component group, the lookup tables, the brand mark, the gallery, and the docs renderer. For the screens that use the components, read [Web console](web-console.md). For the lookup tables of constants, read [Reference: web console and design constants](reference-web-limits.md).

## Package layout and exports

The package has no build step. Each export in `design/package.json` points at a source file, and the Vite build of `web/` compiles it. The package is `private`, so npm never publishes it.

| Export path | File | What it gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@ostra/design` | `design/src/index.ts` | Every component, helper, and type. Also loads the styles. |
| `@ostra/design/index.css` | `design/src/index.css` | Tokens, component classes, bundled fonts, brand styles. |
| `@ostra/design/gallery` | `design/src/Gallery.tsx` | The gallery page (default export). |
| `@ostra/design/docs` | `design/src/docs/index.ts` | The docs renderer: `Docs`, `Markdown`, `Diagram`. |
| `@ostra/design/docs.css` | `design/src/docs/docs.css` | Styles of the docs renderer. |
| `@ostra/design/docs-standalone.css` | `design/src/docs/standalone.css` | Styles for an exported book, without fonts. |

The source folders are:

- `design/src/tokens/`: seven CSS files (`colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css`, `effects.css`, `base.css`, `components.css`, `fonts.css`).
- `design/src/components/`: six groups named `core`, `data`, `feedback`, `forms`, `navigation`, and `pipeline`, plus `brand`.
- `design/src/docs/`: the Markdown renderer and its model.
- `design/src/focus.ts`, `design/src/keys.ts`, `design/src/cx.ts`: three small helpers.
- `design/src/Gallery.tsx`: the gallery.

The package depends on `lucide-react` for icons, `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans` and `@fontsource/jetbrains-mono` for fonts, `mermaid` for diagrams, and the `mdast` and `micromark` packages for Markdown. React 19 (`^19.3.0`) is a peer dependency. The package description says that the console (`web/`) and the site (`site/`) share it. The root `package.json` lists `design`, `web`, and `site` as npm workspaces. This checkout has no `site/` folder.

## How the web app imports the package

The web app imports components from the package root and loads the styles in one place. The steps are:

1. `web/package.json` lists `"@ostra/design": "*"`. The npm workspace links the local folder.
2. `web/src/main.tsx` imports `@ostra/design/index.css`. This loads all tokens and component classes before the app renders.
3. Screens import components by name, for example `import { Banner, Button, Panel } from "@ostra/design"`. The file `design/src/index.ts` also imports `./index.css` as a side effect, so any import of the package root loads the styles.
4. `web/src/App.tsx` adds the route `/_design` only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. The route lazy-loads `@ostra/design/gallery`.
5. `web/src/screens/DocsScreen.tsx` imports `Markdown` and `MAX_HITS` from `@ostra/design/docs` and imports `@ostra/design/docs.css`.
6. `web/src/features/docs/bookModel.ts` builds a `Docs` object. `web/src/features/docs/exportHtml.ts` inlines `@ostra/design/docs-standalone.css` with the `?inline` suffix.

The design package has no code that calls the server. The web app passes data and callbacks into each component. For example, `FolderPicker` receives a `list` function and does not call `GET /api/fs` itself.

### What happens when

- If a file under `design/src` or `design/package.json` is newer than `web/dist/index.html`, `build.sh` rebuilds the web bundle. A design change therefore reaches the binary after the next `build.sh` run.
- The `Dockerfile` copies `design/package.json` and then `design/`, because `web/` builds against the shared package.
- A production build has no `/_design` route, because the route exists only in development.

## Tokens

Tokens are CSS custom properties on `:root`. The comment in `design/src/index.css` states that the files under `tokens/` are copied verbatim from the Claude Design project. The only changed file is `fonts.css`, which loads bundled fonts instead of Google Fonts. `index.css` imports the files in this order: `fonts.css`, `colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css`, `effects.css`, `base.css`, `components.css`, and `components/brand/brand.css`.

### Colors (`colors.css`)

- **Base grays:** a warm gray scale from `--gray-950` (`#0d0d0c`) to `--gray-10` (`#f7f7f5`), and `--white`.
- **Base blue:** `--blue-200` to `--blue-950`. The Ostra blue from the mark is `--blue-600` (`#2459c9`). The dark-mode tint is `--blue-400` (`#7ea3ff`).
- **Status hues:** `green`, `amber`, `red`, and `violet`, each with `-400`, `-700`, `-900`, and `-50` steps.
- **Surfaces:** `--surface-chrome`, `--surface-panel`, `--surface-editor`, `--surface-raised`, `--surface-sunken`, `--surface-overlay`, `--surface-terminal`, `--surface-hover`, `--surface-active`, `--surface-selected`, `--surface-scrim`.
- **Borders:** `--border-subtle`, `--border-default`, `--border-strong`, `--border-focus`.
- **Text:** `--text-primary`, `--text-secondary`, `--text-muted`, `--text-disabled`, `--text-on-accent`, `--text-link`.
- **Accent and status:** `--accent`, `--accent-hover`, `--accent-soft`, `--accent-fg`, then `--ok`, `--warn`, `--bad`, `--info`, each with a `-soft` background.
- **Terminal:** `--term-bg`, `--term-bar`, `--term-border`, `--term-fg`, `--term-muted`, `--term-blue`, `--term-green`, `--term-red`, `--term-amber`, `--term-cursor`.
- **Code and diff:** `--code-bg`, `--diff-add-bg`, `--diff-add-fg`, `--diff-del-bg`, `--diff-del-fg`, and five `--syntax-*` colors (`keyword`, `string`, `number`, `fn`, `comment`).

Code uses the semantic names. A component never uses a base gray or blue directly, because the semantic names change with the theme.

### Type, spacing, and effects

| Token family | Values |
| --- | --- |
| Fonts | `--font-sans`: IBM Plex Sans. `--font-mono`: JetBrains Mono. Both have system fallbacks. |
| Text sizes | `--text-2xs` 10.5px, `--text-xs` 11.5px, `--text-sm` 12px, `--text-base` 13px, `--text-md` 14px, `--text-lg` 16px, `--text-xl` 20px, `--text-2xl` 26px, `--text-code` 12.5px. |
| Line height | `--leading-tight` 1.25, `--leading-normal` 1.45, `--leading-relaxed` 1.6. |
| Weights | `--weight-regular` 400, `--weight-medium` 500, `--weight-semibold` 600. |
| Roles | `--type-ui`, `--type-prose`, `--type-title`, `--type-heading`, `--type-label`, `--type-code`. |
| Spacing | `--space-0` (0px) to `--space-12` (48px). The steps are 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48 px. |
| Control sizes | `--control-h-sm` 22px, `--control-h` 28px, `--control-h-lg` 32px, `--row-h` 26px. |
| Chrome sizes | `--titlebar-h` 36px, `--tabbar-h` 34px, `--statusbar-h` 24px, `--sidebar-w` 264px, `--dock-w` 380px. |
| Content widths | `--content-max` 1080px, `--prose-max` 760px. |
| Radius | `--radius-xs` 3px, `--radius-sm` 4px, `--radius-md` 6px, `--radius-lg` 8px, `--radius-pill` 999px. |
| Durations | `--dur-instant` 60ms, `--dur-fast` 100ms, `--dur-base` 160ms, `--dur-slow` 240ms. |
| Easing | `--ease-out` and `--ease-in-out`. |

The UI base size is 13px because the design is dense and similar to an editor. Prose reads at 14px. The comment in `effects.css` states the elevation rule: borders come first, and shadows appear only on floating layers. The tokens `--shadow-popover` and `--shadow-dialog` are the only shadows. The token `--ring-focus` is a 1px ring and a 3px ring at 28% opacity, both in `--border-focus`.

### Base rules and motion (`base.css`)

`base.css` sets `box-sizing: border-box` on every element, the body colors and font, link colors, and the style of `code`, `pre`, selection, and scrollbars. The rule `:focus-visible` removes the outline and draws `--ring-focus` as a box shadow. The file defines eight keyframes: `os-pulse`, `os-spin`, `os-fade-in`, `os-scrim-in`, `os-dialog-in`, `os-slide-in-right`, `os-slide-in-left`, and `os-rise`.

If the user sets `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, a rule in `base.css` sets every animation and transition duration to 1ms. The brand mark also stops its pulse in that case.

### Component classes (`components.css`)

The file `components.css` holds about 1,700 lines of classes for the components. Every class starts with `os-`, for example `os-btn`, `os-dialog`, and `os-menu`. The file comment states that plain HTML can use the classes without React. Three z-index values order the floating layers: the dialog scrim uses 80, the menu scrim uses 90, and the menu uses 91. The command palette sets its own z-index of 100 inline.

### Fonts (`fonts.css`)

Ostra runs offline, so `fonts.css` bundles the fonts. It holds 42 `@font-face` rules for woff2 files. The weights are IBM Plex Sans 400, 500, 600, and 400 italic, and JetBrains Mono 400, 500, 600. Each subset has a `unicode-range`, so the browser fetches only the subsets that a page needs. The file is generated from the `@fontsource` packages. Regenerate it when those packages change.

## Themes

Dark is the default theme. To get the light theme, set `data-theme="light"` on the `<html>` element. The block `[data-theme="light"]` in `colors.css` overrides the surfaces, borders, text, accent, status colors, code, diff, and syntax tokens. The block in `effects.css` sets only `--shadow-popover` and `--shadow-dialog`, and it replaces them with lighter shadows.

Only the two blocks in `design/src/tokens/colors.css` set `color-scheme`. The `:root` block sets `dark`, and the `[data-theme="light"]` block sets `light`. The block in `effects.css` does not set `color-scheme`.

The light theme does not override the gray scale or the `--term-*` tokens. The comment in `colors.css` states that the terminal is always dark in both themes, because it shows harness PTY output. The token `--surface-terminal` is `--gray-950` in both themes.

The web app applies the theme in `web/src/lib/theme.ts`. The function `applyTheme` sets `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` and stores the value under the `ostra.theme` key in local storage. If no value is stored, `resolveTheme` follows the `prefers-color-scheme` media query and falls back to dark.

## Focus and keyboard helpers

Three small modules give the components one keyboard behavior.

### `cx` in `design/src/cx.ts`

`cx(...parts)` joins class names and drops `false`, `null`, `undefined`, `0`, and empty strings.

### `activateOnKey` in `design/src/keys.ts`

`activateOnKey(fn)` returns a keydown handler for an element with `role="button"` that is not a `button`. The handler runs `fn` on Enter or Space and calls `preventDefault`. It ignores the key when `e.target` is not `e.currentTarget`. Thus a key press inside a child control, such as an input, does not activate the row. `ExecutionGroup`, `StageRow`, `PhaseNode`, and `ToolCall` use it.

### Focus helpers in `design/src/focus.ts`

- `focusables(root)` returns the focusable elements in `root`. The selector `FOCUSABLE` matches `a[href]`, enabled `button`, `input` (not hidden), `select`, `textarea`, and any element with a `tabindex` other than `-1`. The function drops elements inside an `[inert]` ancestor.
- `useFocusTrap(ref, active, initial?)` moves focus into `ref` when `active` becomes true. It uses the `initial` element, else the first focusable element, else the container. It restores the previous focus when `active` becomes false. It returns a keydown handler that wraps Tab and Shift+Tab inside the container. If the container has no focusable element, the handler blocks Tab.
- `arrowIndex(key, index, count, orientation, wrap = true)` returns the next index for ArrowDown or ArrowRight (next), ArrowUp or ArrowLeft (previous), Home (0), and End (`count - 1`). The orientation `vertical` uses the Up and Down keys. The orientation `horizontal` uses the Left and Right keys. It returns `null` for any other key and when `count` is 0. If `wrap` is false, the index stops at the ends.

`Dialog` and `CommandPalette` use `useFocusTrap`. `Menu`, `Tabs`, `TreeItem`, and `LaneStepper` use `arrowIndex`.

## Core components

Core components are the smallest controls. All of them are in `design/src/components/core/`.

- **`Button`** has `variant` (`default`, `primary`, `ghost`, `danger`), `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`), `icon`, `iconRight`, `kbd`, and `active`. The comment states the rule for the variants: `primary` is the one forward action, such as Approve. `danger` is for Deny and Cancel execution. `ghost` is for toolbars. The default `type` is `button`. When `active` is set, the button sets `aria-pressed`. Icons are 13px at size `sm` and 15px otherwise.
- **`IconButton`** needs `icon` and `label`. The label is the accessible name and the tooltip. The default variant is `ghost`. Icons are 13px at size `sm` and 15px at size `md`.
- **`Icon`** draws a Lucide icon by its kebab-case `name`. The default size is 16px. The stroke width is 1.75. The icon uses `currentColor`. An icon without `title` is decorative and has `aria-hidden`. An icon with `title` has `role="img"` and an `aria-label`.
- **`Kbd`** shows keys as separate caps. Pass `keys` as an array, or pass one child.
- **`ICONS` and `ICON_NAMES`** in `icons.ts` list the 129 icons that the package bundles. The type `IconName` is the union of those names. `ICONS` maps each name to a `lucide-react` component, so the bundle holds only these icons. To add an icon, import it from `lucide-react` and add it to `ICONS`.

## Data components

Data components show records and code. All of them are in `design/src/components/data/`.

- **`Panel`** is the only card shape. It is a bordered section with an optional header of 36px. It has `title`, `subtitle`, `icon`, `actions`, `tone` (`highlight`, `warn`, `bad`), `flush`, and `bodyFlush`. Use `bodyFlush` for tables and lists, because it removes the body padding.
- **`SectionLabel`** shows an uppercase 10.5px group label.
- **`Table`** takes `columns` and `rows`. A column has `key`, `label`, `num`, `width`, and `render`. A column with `num` is right-aligned and uses tabular mono digits, for cost, tokens, and durations. The `rowKey` prop names the key field and defaults to `id`. If a row has no key, the index is the key. If `onRowClick` is set, rows are clickable and focusable, and Enter on a focused row opens it. If `rows` is empty, the table shows the `empty` text, which defaults to `Nothing yet.`.
- **`CodeView`** is a read-only source view with line numbers and light syntax color. It has `language`, `startLine` (default 1), `highlight`, `added`, `removed`, `flush`, and `maxHeight`. A line number in `highlight` wins over `added`, and `added` wins over `removed`. The supported languages are `rs`, `ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `sql`, `toml`, `sh`, and `md`, and `txt`. The languages `md` and `txt` have no color. The language sets the comment syntax: `//` for every language except `sql`, `#` for `toml`, `sh`, `py`, and `md`, and `--` for `sql`.
- **`colorLine(line, language)`** colors one line with the same rules. The web app uses it in `web/src/screens/project/code/SourceView.tsx`.

`CodeView` colors with a regular expression, not a parser. The token classes are `os-tok-c` (comment), `os-tok-s` (string), `os-tok-n` (number), `os-tok-k` (keyword), `os-tok-f` (a name before `(`), and `os-tok-t` (a name that starts with a capital letter, matched by `TYPES`). The keyword set covers Rust, TypeScript, and JavaScript words together. Thus the coloring is approximate.

## Feedback components

Feedback components show state. All of them are in `design/src/components/feedback/`.

- **`Chip`** has `tone` (`neutral`, `accent`, `ok`, `warn`, `bad`, `info`), `icon` (11px), `mono`, `outline`, and `title`. The type `Tone` is exported and the web app uses it for its own status mapping.
- **`StatusDot`** is a dot of 7px. It has `tone`, `pulse` (a slow opacity pulse for live state), `hollow` (an outline for pending state), and `size`.
- **`Spinner`** has `role="status"`, the label `Loading`, and a default size of 12px.
- **`Banner`** has `tone` (`warn`, `bad`, `info`, `neutral`), `title`, `icon`, and `actions`. The default tone is `warn`. The tone `bad` uses `role="alert"`. Other tones use `role="status"`. The default icons are `triangle-alert` for `warn`, `octagon-alert` for `bad`, and `info` for `info` and `neutral`. The comment states the uses: `warn` for YOLO on or a project that is not initialized, `bad` for invalid settings, errors, and security blocks. The comment also states that security blocks never get a dismiss action.
- **`Dialog`** is a modal. It is described below.
- **`StatusChip`** maps a backend status value to a `Chip`. It is described below.

### Dialog

`Dialog` renders into `document.body` through a portal. The default width is 560px. It has a title, an optional subtitle, a body, and an optional footer. It uses `useFocusTrap` to keep Tab inside and to restore focus on close.

- **With `onClose`:** the close button, the Escape key, and a click on the scrim call `onClose`. The click closes the dialog only if the press and the release both happen on the scrim. A drag out of a text field therefore does not close the dialog.
- **Without `onClose`:** the dialog has no close button, and Escape and the scrim do nothing. The user must answer the dialog.
- **With `inline`:** the panel renders in place, with no scrim, no portal, no animation, and no focus capture. The gallery and docs use this form.
- **With `initialFocus`:** that element gets focus on open. The default is the first focusable element.

### StatusChip

`StatusChip` takes a `kind` (`session`, `execution`, `stage`, `phase`, `init`) and the backend `status` string. The function `statusTone(kind, status)` returns the `Tone`. It returns `neutral` for an unknown status. The label is the status with the first letter in capitals and each underscore replaced by a space. Three labels are different.

| Kind | Status to tone | Label override |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | `running` accent, `waiting` warn, `completed` ok, `failed` bad, `stalled` bad, `paused` neutral | `waiting` shows `Waiting for you` |
| `execution` | `running` accent, `ok` ok, `stuck` warn, `handoff` info, `waiting` info, `error` bad, `denied` bad, `interrupted` warn, `cancelled` neutral | none |
| `stage` | `pending` neutral, `running` accent, `waiting` warn, `done` ok, `skipped` neutral, `failed` bad, `blocked` bad | none |
| `phase` | `queued` neutral, `implementing` accent, `reviewing` accent, `passed` ok, `blocked` bad, `removed` bad | none |
| `init` | `initialized` ok, `not_initialized` warn, `initializing` accent, `missing` bad | `not_initialized` shows `Not initialized`, `missing` shows `Folder missing` |

The status values come from the Rust enums. For the meaning of each stage and gate, read [The session pipeline](session-pipeline.md).

## Form components

Form components are in `design/src/components/forms/`.

- **`Input`** has `label`, `hint`, `error`, `icon`, `multiline`, `rows` (default 3), `mono`, `size`, and `trailing`. With `multiline`, it renders a `textarea`. If `error` is set, the border turns red, `aria-invalid` is set, and the error text replaces the hint. An `aria-describedby` link connects the field to its note. If the input has a label, hint, or error, it renders inside a `label` element.
- **`Select`** wraps a native `select`. Each option is a string or a `{ value, label }` object.
- **`Switch`** is a checkbox with `role="switch"`. The tone `warn` paints the on state amber. The comment says to use it for YOLO. Read [Judges, decisions, and YOLO mode](judges-and-yolo.md) for what YOLO does.
- **`Checkbox`** is a checkbox, or a radio button when `radio` is set. The `description` prop adds a second line under the label.
- **`Combobox`** is a text field with a list of suggestions.
- **`FolderPicker`** picks a directory on the server.

### Combobox

The caller filters `items` for the query. The list shows only when the field is open, the query is not empty, and either the list has items or the `loading` flag is off. Arrow Down opens the list and moves the highlight down. Arrow Up moves it up. Enter picks the highlighted item. If no item is highlighted, Enter calls `onSubmit` with the text. Escape closes the list, but only when it is open. Then the event stops, so a parent dialog does not close. A blur closes the list. An item can have a `group`, a `sub` line, an `icon`, and a `hint`. The caller must sort items by group, because a group header shows when the group differs from the previous item.

### FolderPicker

The path field is the selection. A value without a trailing separator is the chosen folder. A value with a trailing `/` is a folder that the user is still browsing.

The picker has two modes:

- **With `list`:** the picker loads listings itself. It lists the directory part of the typed path after a debounce of `debounceMs` (default 120ms). It cancels the earlier request with an `AbortController`. If the field is empty, it lists `initialPath` (default `~`). The server expands `~`.
- **Without `list`:** the caller controls browsing with `browsePath`, `entries`, `parent`, `missing`, `nearest`, and `onBrowse`.

The type `FolderListing` matches the shape of `GET /api/fs?path=`. The fields are `path`, `parent`, `entries`, `exists`, `readable`, `nearest`, and `home`. An entry has `name`, `is_dir`, `is_git`, and `is_ostra_project`.

The keyboard rules are:

- Tab completes the highlighted match when the user has typed a name prefix.
- Arrow Up and Arrow Down pick a match.
- Enter uses the highlighted match, or uses the listed folder when there is no prefix and the folder exists.
- Backspace after a trailing separator goes up one folder.
- A click on a row opens the folder. A double click selects it.

The list shows folders that start with the typed prefix first, then folders that contain it. The list height defaults to 220px.

#### What happens when

- If the typed path is not absolute, the field is marked invalid and shows `Type an absolute path, starting with / or ~/.` For a Windows home it shows the Windows form of this message.
- If the folder is missing or not readable, the bar shows a red folder icon, an error row, and a disabled `Use this folder` button. If a nearest existing folder is known, a row opens it.
- If `mkdir` is set and the typed folder does not exist, a `Create` row appears. It creates the folder and its missing parents, like `mkdir -p`, then selects the new folder and lists it again. If `mkdir` fails, the error text shows below the row.
- If the listing request fails, the picker shows `Could not list <path>: <error>`.

The module also exports path helpers: `isWindowsPath`, `isAbsolutePath`, `endsWithSep`, `trimSep`, `withSep`, `baseName`, and `splitPath`. They handle both `/` and `\\`. A bare drive such as `C:` filters the drive list. On a Windows server, the path `/` is the list of drives. The web app and the tests use these helpers. Three regular expressions in the module detect a drive: see [Lookup tables in components](#lookup-tables-in-components).

## Navigation components

Navigation components are in `design/src/components/navigation/`.

### Tabs

`Tabs` has three variants. The variant `bar` is for editor tabs with icons and a close button. The variant `underline` (the default) is for sections of a page. The variant `segmented` is for compact toggles. The component is controlled by `value` and `onChange`. A tab has `id`, `label`, `icon`, `count`, `dot`, `italic` (a preview tab), `pinned`, and `title`.

Only the selected tab is in the Tab order. Arrow keys, Home, and End move between tabs and select the tab at once. Enter and Space also select. The `bar` variant adds these rules:

- `onClose` shows a close button, and the Delete key closes the focused tab.
- A pinned tab shows a pin button in place of the close button, and `onUnpin` runs on click.
- If `onMove` is set, tabs are draggable. The shortcut Ctrl+Shift+Left or Right (or Cmd) moves the focused tab. `onMove` receives the id and the index where the tab must end up. Without `onMove`, drag and the shortcut are off.

A strip that is wider than its box scrolls sideways, and a vertical wheel scrolls it (not for `segmented`). The function `revealSelectedTab(strip)` moves the strip so that the selected tab is in view. It changes only `scrollLeft` of the strip, because `scrollIntoView` also scrolls every ancestor, including a page that frames the console.

### Menu and ContextMenu

`Menu` is a dropdown. Place it in a `position: relative` wrapper next to its trigger. An item is an action, a `divider`, or a `heading`. An action has `label`, `sub`, `icon`, `hint`, `kbd`, `checked`, `danger`, `indent`, `active`, and `onSelect`. An item with `checked` set has the role `menuitemradio`. Other actions have the role `menuitem`.

When the menu opens, focus moves to the first item. Arrow keys, Home, and End move focus. Enter and Space select the item, run `onSelect`, and close the menu. Escape closes the menu. Tab also closes it. A click on the scrim, which has z-index 90, closes it. On close, focus returns to the trigger, but only if focus fell to the `body`. If the user moved focus to another element, the menu leaves it there.

`ContextMenu` is a `Menu` that opens at a viewport point `at`, for example the `clientX` and `clientY` of a right click. A `null` value closes it. The menu keeps 8px (`MARGIN`) from each viewport edge. The default width is 220px. The component estimates the height as `items.length * 30 + 8` pixels to place the menu above the point when there is not enough room below.

### CommandPalette

`CommandPalette` is the resource switcher that opens with Ctrl+K or Cmd+K. The caller owns the shortcut. The palette renders into `document.body` only when `open` is true. It is 560px wide with a maximum of `100vw - 32px`, starts 12vh from the top, and uses z-index 100. The list has a maximum height of 360px.

The default filter is `filterPaletteItems`. It keeps the items whose label, hint, or group contains the query, ignoring case, in the original order. A caller that searches the server passes `onQueryChange` and `filterItems` to replace the filter. Arrow keys move the highlight and stop at the ends. Enter opens the highlighted item, then closes the palette. Escape and a click on the scrim close it. Focus goes to the input on open and returns to the opener on close. If nothing matches, the list shows `Nothing matches “<query>”.`

### Trees, breadcrumbs, and steppers

- **`TreeItem`** is one sidebar row. Each depth level indents 14px, after a base of 6px. Pass `expanded` to show a chevron. Enter and Space activate the row. Arrow Right opens a collapsed row and Arrow Left closes an open row. Arrow Up and Down move focus between the `treeitem` rows of the enclosing tree. If a row has a chevron and `onToggle` but no `onClick`, a click on the row toggles it.
- **`TreeSection`** is an uppercase group header with optional actions. It uses `role="group"` and labels the group with its text.
- **`FileTree`** renders the rows of a lazy folder tree. See below.
- **`Breadcrumbs`** shows the path of the open resource. Every crumb except the last can navigate through `onNavigate`, with Enter on a focused crumb. The last crumb has `aria-current="page"`.
- **`Stepper`** shows wizard progress. Steps before `current` are done, and a click on a done step calls `onSelect`. The vertical orientation is a rail with hints. The horizontal orientation shows only the label of the current step.

### FileTree

`FileTree` renders rows only. Put it inside an element with `role="tree"`. The caller loads each open folder and answers `folder(dir)`, where the root is the empty string. A folder that is not loaded shows `Reading…` with a spinner. A folder with an error and no entries shows the error text. The tree sorts folders before files, and each group by name with `localeCompare`. An empty root shows the `empty` node.

The tree supports these extras:

- `row(entry)` sets the color, muted state, meta, trailing node, and title of a row.
- `onContextMenu` replaces the browser menu on a row.
- `onDragStart`, `dropEffect`, and `onDrop` add drag and drop. `dropEffect` answers `copy` for files from the computer (see `dragHasFiles`), `move` for rows of this tree, or `null` to refuse. The target folder row gets a highlight. A drop on a file targets the folder that holds the file, found with `parentDir`.
- `creating`, `onCreate`, and `onCancelCreate` show `NewEntryField` at the top of a folder. Enter creates the entry. Escape, or a blur with an empty name, cancels. The field trims the name and removes leading and trailing `/`. If `onCreate` rejects, the field shows the error and stays open.
- `fileIcon(path)` picks an icon from the extension of the last path segment. The `FILE_ICON` table holds the mapping: see [Lookup tables in components](#lookup-tables-in-components).

## Pipeline components

Pipeline components show the state of a session. They are in `design/src/components/pipeline/`. The web console builds its session screen from them. For the model behind them, read [The session pipeline](session-pipeline.md).

- **`LaneStepper`** shows nine lanes in the fixed order `LANE_ORDER`: `research`, `requirements`, `verification`, `design`, `build`, `review`, `test`, `docs`, `done`. A lane has `status` (`pending`, `current`, `waiting`, `done`, `failed`, `skipped`), an optional `detail` line, and an optional `why` tooltip. A lane that the caller leaves out is `pending`. The strip is a `tablist`. Arrow keys, Home, and End move between lanes and select them. The status icons are `check` (done), `hand` (waiting), `x` (failed), and `minus` (skipped). The current lane shows a pulsing dot.
- **`StageRow`** is one stage in a lane. The statuses are `pending`, `running`, `waiting`, `done`, `skipped`, `failed`, `blocked`. Running has a pulsing accent dot. A skipped or pending stage has a hollow dot. With `onClick`, the row is a button that sets `aria-pressed`.
- **`PhaseNode`** is one phase of the build lane. It shows the id, the title, and chips for the project, the complexity (`low`, `medium`, `high`), the test policy (`Required`, `Optional`, `Skip`), and the deliverable. The footer shows a `StatusChip` of kind `phase`, the review pass when it is above 0, a `security block` chip, and the dependencies as `← 1, 2`.
- **`PhaseDag`** lays out `PhaseNode` columns by dependency layer. Each column depends only on columns to its left. The first column has the label `No dependencies`. The next columns have the label `Step 2`, `Step 3`, and so on. The gap between columns is 28px.
- **`ExecutionGroup`** lists the executions of one agent in one project. A group of one run renders as a plain row. A group of two or more runs is collapsible and shows the count (`×3`), the executor chips, and the total cost. The group is open by default when any run has the status `running`. The component sums the cost by reading each `cost` string without `$`, and shows the sum with two decimals. A run with the executor `native` shows the `activity` icon. Any other executor shows `square-terminal`. The `DOT` table sets the dot tone of each run status: see [Lookup tables in components](#lookup-tables-in-components).
- **`ToolCall`** shows one tool call in an Activity stream. See below.
- **`Decision`** shows a judge decision as `Ostra chose <choice> because <reason>`. The `reason` must start with a lowercase letter, because it follows `because`. The row has a chip with the judge name, an optional time, an `Overridden by you` chip, and an `Override` button. If `canOverride` is false, the row shows `Settled` and the tooltip `Work that depends on this decision has already started`. Read [Judges, decisions, and YOLO mode](judges-and-yolo.md) for the rules of an override.
- **`GateCard`** is the shell of every gate. See below.
- **`DiffView`** shows unified diff lines. Each line has a `type` (`add`, `del`, `ctx`) and `text`.
- **`Terminal`** is the pane for a harness execution. See below.

### GateCard

`GateCard` shows a header with an icon, a title, and a status chip. It then shows an explanation and a body. An open gate shows its `children` (the form) and an `actions` row. The chip says `Waiting for you`. An answered gate shows the `answer` and an optional `Reason:` line. The chip says `Answered by you` or `Answered by Ostra (YOLO)`, from `answeredBy`.

The type `GateKind` has 13 values. The `KIND_ICON` table gives each value an icon. The table is in [Lookup tables in components](#lookup-tables-in-components).

The `kind` prop also accepts any other string. A kind that the component does not know, for example from a newer server, shows the `circle-pause` icon. Thus an older console still renders a new gate.

### ToolCall

`ToolCall` takes the canonical Claude Code tool name, a one-line `summary`, a `state` (`running`, `done`, `error`), a `duration`, and an optional `policy`. The `policy` has `decision` (`allow`, `ask`, `deny`), `layer` (`guard` or `permission`), `rule`, `reason`, and `advice`. A call that policy denied or asked about opens by default. Other calls start closed, unless `defaultOpen` is set.

- A denied call shows a `Denied` chip and a block that names the rule and layer, the reason, and a `What to do instead:` line.
- An asked call that is not done shows an `Asking you` chip and the text `Needs permission`.
- An allowed call with a rule shows `Allowed by <layer> rule <rule>` when open.
- A call with the state `error` that was not denied shows an `Error` chip. A running call that is not asked shows a spinner.

The icon comes from `TOOL_ICON`: `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `Skill`, `Report`, `Memory`, and `MemoryRecall` each have an icon. Any other tool uses `wrench`. For the policy layers, read [Policy engine](policy-guards.md).

### Terminal

`Terminal` draws the bar of a harness pane, with the title, the meta text, and a state: `Live` with a pulsing dot, or `Session ended`. The default height is 420px. The body has two forms:

- **Static lines:** pass `lines` as `[tone, text]` pairs or `{ tone, text }` objects. The tones are `""`, `muted`, `fn`, `ok`, `add`, `bad`, `del`, and `warn`. With `live`, a cursor shows. The pane follows new output.
- **Live screen:** pass `children`, usually the host element of xterm.js. The static lines, input row, and follow button are then off. Give the host `flex: 1; min-height: 0`, so that the fit addon measures the right size.

The pane stops following when the user scrolls more than 24px from the bottom. Then a `Follow output` button appears. With `interactive` and `live`, an input row sends the typed text to `onInput` on Enter. The console uses the live form in `web/src/screens/execution/TerminalStream.tsx`.

## Lookup tables in components

Nine constants in the component files map one value to another. The component code reads each table at render time. Other sections of this page describe how the components use them. This section lists the values in one place.

| Name | File | What it maps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CSS_PAL` | `design/src/components/brand/LiveMark.tsx` | Each of 8 mark roles to a CSS variable: `tile` to `--surface-raised`, `edge` to `--border-default`, `done` to `--accent`, `off` to `--border-strong`, `wait` to `--warn`, `fail` to `--bad`, `ok` to `--ok`, `rest` to `--text-primary`. |
| `ARC_D` | `design/src/components/brand/LiveMark.tsx` | Each arc index 0 to 7 to an SVG path string. |
| `LABELS` | `design/src/components/feedback/StatusChip.tsx` | A status kind and a status value to a label that replaces the default text. |
| `DRIVE` | `design/src/components/forms/FolderPicker.tsx` | The regular expression `/^[A-Za-z]:/`. It matches a path that starts with a drive letter. |
| `DRIVE_NAME` | `design/src/components/forms/FolderPicker.tsx` | The regular expression `/^[A-Za-z]:$/`. It matches a bare drive name such as `C:`. |
| `DRIVE_ROOT` | `design/src/components/forms/FolderPicker.tsx` | The regular expression `/^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]$/`. It matches a drive root such as `C:\\` or `C:/`. |
| `FILE_ICON` | `design/src/components/navigation/FileTree.tsx` | A lowercase file extension to an icon name. |
| `DOT` | `design/src/components/pipeline/ExecutionGroup.tsx` | An execution run status to a dot tone. |
| `KIND_ICON` | `design/src/components/pipeline/GateCard.tsx` | A gate kind to an icon name. |

### CSS_PAL and ARC_D

`LiveMark` draws with `CSS_PAL`, so the mark follows the active theme. The sibling table `PAL` holds fixed hex colors for `markSvg`, because a favicon cannot read CSS variables. The `run` state has no color of its own: an arc or pearl in the `run` state uses the `done` color, and the class `live-mark-pulse` adds the pulse.

`ARC_D` holds 8 path strings, one for each of the `MARK_ARCS` arcs. Arc `i` starts at `-90 + i * 45 + GAP` degrees and ends at `-90 + (i + 1) * 45 - GAP` degrees. The ring radius `R` is 9.5, and `GAP` is 4.5 degrees. Each path is an SVG arc command with a sweep flag of 1, which draws clockwise. `markSvg` uses the same `ARC_D` paths.

### LABELS

`LABELS` is a partial table. It has entries for the kinds `session` and `init` only. `session` maps `waiting` to `Waiting for you`. `init` maps `not_initialized` to `Not initialized` and `missing` to `Folder missing`. For every other kind and status, `StatusChip` formats the status with the first letter in capitals and each underscore replaced by a space.

### DRIVE, DRIVE_NAME, and DRIVE_ROOT

The three expressions detect a Windows drive in a typed path:

- `DRIVE` is used by `isWindowsPath`. A path that matches it, or a `~` path with a Windows home, is a Windows path.
- `DRIVE_NAME` makes the picker list the drive list, with the typed drive as the filter. It also makes `join` add `\\` after a drive name, and it makes `parentOf` return `/`.
- `DRIVE_ROOT` stops `trimSep` from removing the separator of a drive root. It also makes `parentOf` return `/`, which is the drive list.

### FILE_ICON

`FILE_ICON` has 16 extensions. `fileIcon(path)` lowercases the extension of the last path segment and reads the table. A name with no dot, a name that starts with a dot and has no other dot, and any extension that the table lacks give the icon `file`.

| Extensions | Icon |
| --- | --- |
| `rs`, `ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `jsx`, `py`, `go`, `java`, `kt` | `file-code-2` |
| `sql` | `database` |
| `toml`, `yaml`, `yml` | `file-cog` |
| `json` | `file-json` |
| `md`, `txt` | `file-text` |

### DOT

`DOT` has 9 entries, one for each `ExecutionRunStatus`. The constant is not exported. `ExecutionGroup` shows a `StatusDot` of size 6 with the tone from `DOT`, and uses `neutral` for an unknown status. A run with the status `running` shows a `Spinner` of size 10 and not a dot. The helper `RunIcon` reads `DOT` only when the status is not `running`. Thus the `running` entry is never used for rendering.

| Run status | Tone |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | `ok` |
| `running` | `accent` |
| `stuck`, `interrupted` | `warn` |
| `handoff`, `waiting` | `info` |
| `error`, `denied` | `bad` |
| `cancelled` | `neutral` |

The tones match the `execution` row of `StatusChip`, so a dot and a chip for the same run have the same color.

### KIND_ICON

`KIND_ICON` has 13 entries, one for each `GateKind`. `GateCard` reads it with the `kind` prop and falls back to `circle-pause`.

| Gate kind | Icon |
| --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `message-circle-question` |
| `spec_approval` | `file-check` |
| `plan_approval` | `list-checks` |
| `permission` | `shield-alert` |
| `review_cap` | `repeat` |
| `stuck` | `life-buoy` |
| `phase_blocked` | `octagon-x` |
| `closing_gate` | `flag` |
| `skill_approval` | `book-check` |
| `harness_failure` | `plug-zap` |
| `execution_failed` | `circle-x` |
| `budget_reached` | `coins` |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `refresh-ccw` |

## Brand mark

`LiveMark` in `design/src/components/brand/LiveMark.tsx` draws the Ostra mark as an SVG. The mark is a rounded square with eight arcs in a ring and a pearl in the center. The doc comment on `MarkState` says that each arc is one board lane from research to docs, and that a pearl of `off` or `null` is hidden. The `markState` doc comment in `web/src/shell/markState.ts` says that the center shows what the session needs from the user.

The state is a `MarkState` value: `{ arcs, pearl }`. `MARK_ARCS` is 8. An arc has one of five states: `done`, `run`, `wait`, `fail`, `off`. The pearl has one of six states: `run`, `wait`, `fail`, `ok`, `rest`, `off`, or `null`. Two states are constants:

- `REST` has eight `done` arcs and a `rest` pearl.
- `IDLE` has eight `off` arcs and no pearl.

### Where the console shows the mark

`REST` is not in the title bar. `web/src/shell/TitleBar.tsx` passes the live session state (`mark`) to `LiveMark`, and it sets the label to `Ostra: <markLabel>`. The console uses `REST` in these places:

- `web/src/shell/SignIn.tsx`: the sign-in page, at size 20.
- `web/src/shell/Home.tsx`: the home page, at size 20.
- `web/src/screens/setup/Onboarding.tsx`: onboarding, at size 20.
- The `NothingOpen` pane in `web/src/shell/WorkspaceShell.tsx`: the empty workspace pane, at size 36.
- `web/src/mobile/MobileShell.tsx`: the mobile shell, at size 26.
- `web/src/mobile/screens/MSetup.tsx`: the mobile setup screen, at size 44.

### Geometry and motion

Each arc covers 45 degrees of the ring and starts at the top. A gap of 4.5 degrees (`GAP`) on each side leaves 36 degrees of visible arc. The ring radius is 9.5 on a 32 by 32 view box. The arc stroke is 3.6. The pearl radius is 3.6.

The component draws an `off` track under each arc. When an arc leaves `off`, it draws clockwise over the track. The `draw` prop sets the duration of one arc, and the default is `0.32s`. The pearl scales in and out in 0.55 seconds. A `run` arc uses the accent color and pulses with the class `live-mark-pulse`. The pulse is 1.4 seconds long and stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Without a `label`, the SVG is decorative. With a `label`, it has `role="img"`.

### Favicon

The function `markSvg(state, theme)` returns the mark as a standalone SVG document. It uses fixed hex colors from the `PAL` table, because a favicon cannot read CSS variables. The web app uses it in `web/src/shell/markState.ts`. The function `markState` maps a session to arcs. Lanes before the current lane are `done`. The current lane is `run`, `wait`, or `fail`. Later lanes are `off`. The pearl has the same state as the current lane. A completed session gives eight `done` arcs and an `ok` pearl. A `null` session gives `IDLE`. The hook `useLiveFavicon` sets the tab icon to a data URL of that SVG and restores the old icon on unmount.

## Gallery

`Gallery` is a page that shows every component in its variants. It is the default export of `design/src/Gallery.tsx`. The comment states that it is a dev-only page, translated from the cards of the design project. The route is `/_design`, and `web/src/App.tsx` adds it only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true.

The page has a `Dark` and `Light` theme toggle (a `segmented` `Tabs`). The toggle sets `data-theme` on `<html>`, and removes it for dark. The page has seven cards. In file order, the names are `Core`, `Icon map`, `Forms`, `Feedback`, `Navigation`, `Data`, and `Pipeline`. The card `Icon map` has the subtitle `Every mapped Lucide name` and the count of `ICON_NAMES`. It lists every name in `ICON_NAMES`.

The file defines its own demo data. `GALLERY_CSS` holds the page layout styles with the prefix `gx-`. `PALETTE` is a list of `PaletteItem` values for the command palette. `TREE` is a map of folder listings for `FileTree`. `SRC` is a Rust snippet for `CodeView`. `ROWS` is a list of execution rows for `ExecutionGroup`. These constants are demo values and not part of the package API.

When you add a component, add a variant to the matching card. The gallery is the only visual check of the package, because no test renders a screenshot.

## Docs renderer

The `design/src/docs/` folder holds the renderer that shows Markdown books. The console uses it for documentation books. The comment in `docs/index.ts` states that the site's docs and the console's books share it. For the content and the storage of books, read [Documentation books](documentation-books.md).

The renderer has three parts:

- **`Docs`** in `model.ts` parses Markdown, builds the pages, the table of contents, the anchors, and the search index.
- **`Markdown`** in `Markdown.tsx` turns the blocks of one page into React elements.
- **`Diagram`** in `Diagram.tsx` draws a fenced `mermaid` block as SVG.

### The Docs model

The constructor `new Docs(nav, sources, fileUrl?)` takes navigation groups, a map from file key to Markdown source, and an optional link resolver. A `PageDef` has `id`, `title`, `file`, and an optional `section`. The `section` selects one `##` part of a file by its number (`"8"` matches `## 8. The engine`) or by its exact heading text. The empty string selects the text before the first `##`. If `section` is omitted, the page shows the whole file. If a `file` key is not in `sources`, the constructor throws `The docs page file <file> is not in the sources.`

The model builds each page in these steps:

1. It parses the file with `mdast-util-from-markdown` and the GFM extensions.
2. It picks the section with `pickSection`.
3. It drops the first heading, because that heading becomes the page title. The headings one level below it form the table of contents.
4. It gives each heading an id from `slug`. A repeated id gets the suffix `-2`, `-3`, and so on.
5. It indexes global anchors. A page title and the text of a section heading come first, and then every heading id. The first owner of an anchor wins.
6. It indexes the search text of each page.

`slug` lowercases the text, removes backticks and characters other than `a-z`, `0-9`, space, and `-`, trims, and joins words with `-`.

### Links and hashes

The hash of a page is `#<id>` or `#<id>/<anchor>`. The method `fromHash` decodes the hash. If the page id is unknown, it tries the value as a bare anchor from an older link. If that fails, it opens the first page.

The method `link(href, page)` decides where a Markdown link goes:

- A link that starts with `http:`, `https:`, or `mailto:` is external and opens in a new tab.
- A link with any other scheme, such as `javascript:` or `data:`, returns `null`. The renderer shows the text without a link.
- A link with only `#anchor` resolves inside the page, then in the global anchors.
- A relative path resolves against the folder of the current file with `resolvePath`. If the file is a page of the docs, the link goes to that page. If it is not, `fileUrl` of the file gives the link. If `fileUrl` returns `null`, the link shows as plain text. The default `fileUrl` always returns `null`.

### Search

`search(query)` finds the case-insensitive text in the index. It returns one hit for each page section. Titles come before headings, and headings come before body text. The model returns at most `MAX_HITS` hits, which is 80. Each hit has the text before the match (up to 48 characters), the match, and the text after it (up to 90 characters). An ellipsis marks a cut. Table cells are joined with a middle dot (`·`), because the plain `mdast` text function runs them together. The console shows `80+ matches` when the list reaches the limit.

### The Markdown renderer

`Markdown` renders headings, paragraphs, code blocks, thematic breaks, block quotes, lists (with task checkboxes), tables, and footnotes. The comment in `Markdown.tsx` states the reasons for the safety rules:

- Raw HTML is never rendered. The only exception is `<br>`.
- Only images that the caller lists in the `images` prop render, keyed by source path. Any other image becomes a link to the file, because the pages load no image from another origin. This is the same rule as the Content Security Policy of the console.
- A heading that is deeper than the page title shifts to a relative level. The renderer uses the classes `md-h2`, `md-h3`, and `md-h4`.

### Diagrams

`Diagram` loads `mermaid` with a dynamic `import`, so a page without a diagram does not load it. The call to `mermaid.initialize` sets `securityLevel: "strict"`, `htmlLabels: false`, `startOnLoad: false`, and `suppressErrorRendering: true`. The theme is `dark` for the dark theme and `neutral` for the light theme.

The `SECURE` constant in `design/src/docs/Diagram.tsx` holds six keys: `secure`, `securityLevel`, `startOnLoad`, `maxTextSize`, `suppressErrorRendering`, and `maxEdges`. The call site passes `secure: [...SECURE, "htmlLabels"]`. The effective list has seven keys, and the seventh is `htmlLabels`. A diagram cannot change these keys with its own directives or frontmatter.

The comment states what these settings guarantee. Strict mode ignores click callbacks. The renderer replaces each link that a `click` line makes with its text. Labels are SVG text and never HTML. Thus a diagram cannot carry an image or leave the page.

#### What happens when

- If a diagram does not parse, the renderer shows its source in a `pre` block.
- If the source or the theme changes while a render runs, the renderer ignores the old result.

### Docs styles

`docs.css` styles the navigation (288px wide), the search hits, and the `md-*` classes. `standalone.css` imports `colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css`, and `docs.css`, and leaves out the fonts. The comment states the reason: an exported book is one file that loads nothing, so it carries no bundled fonts. The export uses the system font fallbacks.

## Tests and checks

The package has three test files that run with Vitest in a jsdom environment. The config is `design/vitest.config.ts`, and it includes `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`.

| File | What it checks |
| --- | --- |
| `design/src/feedback.test.tsx` | `Dialog` close paths, required answer, focus trap and restore, inline form. `StatusChip` tone and label. `Icon` glyph, stroke, and accessible name. |
| `design/src/navigation.test.tsx` | `CommandPalette` filter, highlight, Enter, Escape, and focus return. `Tabs` selection, arrows, close, and reorder. `Menu` focus, select, close, and checked item. `TreeItem` keys and toggle. |
| `design/src/forms.test.tsx` | `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `Input`, `splitPath` and the Windows path helpers, `FolderPicker` in both modes, and `Combobox`. |

The scripts in `design/package.json` are `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`), `test` (`vitest run`), `lint` (`biome lint`), `check` (`biome check`), and `check:fix` (`biome check --write`). The root `biome.json` sets the format: 2 spaces, a line width of 120, double quotes, semicolons, and trailing commas. It turns the `a11y` lint group off.

These checks are separate from the Rust commands `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, and `cargo fmt --all`. Read [Testing and verification](testing.md) for the whole set.

## Rules for a change to the package

- Use a semantic token, not a base color, in a component style, because only the semantic tokens change with the theme.
- Add the new component class to `components.css` with the prefix `os-`.
- Export the component and its prop types from `design/src/index.ts`. A screen imports only from the package root.
- Add a new icon to `ICONS` in `design/src/components/core/icons.ts`. A name that is not in `ICONS` is not a valid `IconName`.
- Add a variant of the component to the matching card in `design/src/Gallery.tsx`.
- Keep the keyboard behavior in the shared helpers (`arrowIndex`, `useFocusTrap`, `activateOnKey`), so that all components behave the same way.

sections.title: Testing and verification
sections.summary: The commands that build, test, and format Ostra, where each kind of test lives, what each kind proves, and the steps to add a test.
sections.body:
The commands that build, test, and format Ostra, and where each kind of test lives: unit tests, engine conformance fixtures, web tests, evals, the browser security suite, and the Windows probes. It also states how to add a test.

Ostra runs agents that write code, so a wrong change in the planner, the policy, or the sandbox has a real cost. Without tests, such a change shows up only in a live session. Ostra has six kinds of check. Each kind covers a different risk, and each kind has its own command. This page lists the commands, says what each kind proves, and says how to add a test to each.

The page covers:

- the three workspace commands
- the Rust unit and integration tests
- the structured document tests and their fixtures
- the engine conformance fixtures
- the web tests
- the eval files and the test stage project
- the browser security suite
- the Windows probes
- the steps to add a test

## Run the build, test, and format commands

Run these commands from the repository root. They are the same commands that [Running Ostra](running-ostra.md) lists for the toolchain.

| Goal | Command | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compile | `cargo build --workspace` | Compiles the 15 crates in `crates/`. |
| Test | `cargo test --workspace` | Runs every Rust test that is not marked `#[ignore]`. |
| Format | `cargo fmt --all` | Formats every Rust file. |

The workspace in `Cargo.toml` has `members = ["crates/*"]`. It excludes `tests/windows-probes`. For that reason `cargo test --workspace` never builds the Windows probes.

The Rust toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` to channel `1.98.1`. The workspace sets `rust-version = "1.98"` and `edition = "2024"`.

The live eval tests are marked `#[ignore]`. They call paid models. For that reason `cargo test --workspace` skips them. Read [Run the eval files](#run-the-eval-files) to start them.

The web app has its own commands. Run them in the `web` folder.

| Goal | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Run the web tests once | `npm test` (runs `vitest run`) |
| Check types | `npm run typecheck` (runs `tsc --noEmit`) |
| Check lint and format | `npm run check` (runs `biome check`) |
| Fix lint and format | `npm run check:fix` |

## Find the Rust tests of each crate

A crate keeps its tests in one of three places. Unit tests sit in a `#[cfg(test)]` module inside `src/`. Larger unit suites sit in a file named `src/tests.rs`. Integration tests sit in the folder `tests/` of the crate. The last place also holds the engine conformance fixtures, which Cargo reads from the repository folder `tests/conformance`.

| Crate | Integration tests | What they cover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ostra-engine` | `tests/runner.rs`, `tests/pause.rs`, `tests/recover.rs`, and the conformance target | A real `Engine` with a scripted executor and scripted judges, pause and resume, and recovery after a restart. |
| `ostra-server` | `tests/e2e.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`, and the four `*_evals.rs` files | The whole stack with a scripted model, workspace MCP servers, and the evals. |
| `ostra-policy` | `tests/policy.rs` | Guard and permission cases: scope, Bash scope, artifacts, ledgers, tool self-protection, reports, the lesson gate, the build streak, and the permission modes. |
| `ostra-providers` | `tests/anthropic.rs`, `tests/openai.rs`, `tests/fixtures/*.sse`, `tests/common/mod.rs` | Provider streaming against recorded server-sent event files, such as `anthropic_tool_use.sse` and `anthropic_midstream_error.sse`. |
| `ostra-code` | `tests/index.rs`, `tests/graph.rs`, `tests/graph_ostra.rs`, `tests/outline.rs`, `tests/usages.rs`, `tests/lsp.rs` | The index, the dependency graph, the outline, usage resolution, and LSP servers. |
| `ostra-mcp` | `tests/client.rs` | The MCP client. |
| `ostra-store` | `tests/workspace_db.rs` | The workspace database. |
| `ostra-sandbox` | `tests/env_scrub.rs` | `scrub_startup_env` against `sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2)`. The test compiles on macOS only. |
| `ostra-core` | `tests/fixtures/models-dev-sample.json` | A sample price catalog for `pricing.rs`. The structured document tests and fixtures sit in `src/doc/tests.rs` and `src/doc/fixtures`. |

Many other crates have `#[cfg(test)]` modules next to the code, for example `ostra-tools`, `ostra-policy`, `ostra-server`, `ostra-exec-harness`, `ostra-workspace`, `ostra-store`, `ostra-notify`, `ostra-providers`, `ostra-mcp`, and `ostra-code`. Run one crate with `cargo test -p <crate>`.

## Read the unit tests of agents, sandbox, and native executor

Three crates keep a large unit suite in `src/tests.rs`. Each suite states rules that the other pages describe.

### `crates/ostra-agents/src/tests.rs`

These tests check the embedded assets and the spawn contract:

- Every agent definition loads with its tier. For example, `Explore` is `Advanced` and `Implementer` is `Balanced`.
- Read-only agents have no edit capability, and the quick answer agent cannot write.
- Every prompt renders for every executor with no unresolved token.
- Every prompt contains the sentence `Write no text outside tool calls`. The test `every_prompt_forbids_text_outside_ostra_tool_calls` checks it.
- No asset file contains an em dash. The test `no_em_dashes_in_any_asset` scans every `.md` and `.toml` asset.
- No asset names `ultracode`, except in a short list of allowed phrases. The initializer names the old `.ultracode/` bootstrap on purpose, because it migrates that bootstrap.
- Every spawn parameter struct renders a block that its own contract accepts, and `parse_block` refuses bad blocks.
- The repo brief selects sections per agent and is idempotent.

For the rules behind these checks, read [Agents, prompts, skills, and the spawn contract](agents-and-prompts.md).

### `crates/ostra-sandbox/src/tests.rs`

These tests render a `Profile` and run real commands under the backend of the machine. The helper `run_in` returns `None` when the machine has no sandbox. In that case the test prints `no sandbox here` and returns without a failure. Tests that need bubblewrap print `bubblewrap unavailable; skipping`. Tests with a `seatbelt_` prefix need the macOS backend.

A passing run on a machine with no backend proves little. Run the suite on Linux with bubblewrap and on macOS before you change the sandbox.

The tests check these behaviors:

- Profile arguments bind roots, hide secrets, and set caches.
- Nested repositories and git files are protected and pinned.
- Opening a decoy is reported, and listing a decoy is not.
- A private network leads out only through its own proxy.
- A sandboxed command cannot make new user namespaces.
- Seatbelt strings cannot break out of the policy. The test `sbpl_strings_cannot_break_out` checks quoting.
- Seatbelt members die with the invocation, even after `setsid`.

For the design, read [Sandbox](sandbox.md).

### `crates/ostra-exec-native/src/tests.rs`

These tests run the native loop with `ScriptedProvider` from `ostra_providers::mock`, so no model is called. A `FakeHost` records deltas, messages, permission asks, and transcripts. The `fixture` function sets `OSTRA_SANDBOX_CACHE` once and makes a temporary folder inside `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`. The folder is outside the OS temp folder because the policy never asks for writes in the OS temp folder.

The tests check these behaviors:

- A read outside the scope is denied with `Denied by guard`, and a run that reports and submits ends `Ok`.
- An invalid submit is retried, and a missing submit gets one reminder.
- `explore` submits only after its document exists.
- Permission asks allow and deny, and YOLO skips asks.
- A cancel is immediate, and a timeout is an error.
- A run resumes from its transcript, and a resume in place records only the new turn.
- The loop compacts near the context window and continues from the summary.
- A run that owes an answer is reminded to reply and cannot submit.

For the loop itself, read [Native executor and model providers](native-executor.md).

## Read the structured document tests and fixtures of ostra-core

The file `crates/ostra-core/src/doc/tests.rs` tests the structured documents: research, spec, plan, and the project profile. It keeps four fixtures at the top and in the middle of the file. Three are JSON files that the file loads. One is a TOML text in the file itself.

| Fixture | Visibility | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RESEARCH` | `pub(crate)` | The text of `src/doc/fixtures/research.json`, loaded with `include_str!`. |
| `SPEC` | `pub(crate)` | The text of `src/doc/fixtures/spec.json`, a specification for order cancellation with 4 requirements and 2 deliverables. |
| `PLAN` | `pub(crate)` | The text of `src/doc/fixtures/plan.json`, a plan with 2 phases. |
| `PROFILE` | private | A minimal `project.toml` as a Rust string constant. |

The test `fixtures_parse_and_pass` checks that `RESEARCH`, `SPEC`, and `PLAN` parse with `DocKind::parse` and give no issue from `check`. Other tests start from these texts and change one field to cause one error. For example, `broken_references_are_errors` sets `covers` to `C9` and expects the message ``covers` names `C9``.

### The `PROFILE` fixture

`PROFILE` is the text of a valid project profile, the file that the initializer agent writes to `.ostra/project.toml`. It sits at lines 182 to 195 of `tests.rs`. It holds these entries:

- `schema_version = 1`, `stack = "rust-axum"`, and `build_tool = "cargo"`.
- A `[commands]` table with `build = "cargo build"`.
- One `[[module_map]]` row with `glob = "src/**"` and `area = "app"`.
- A `[conventions]` table with `notes = ["one"]`.

One test uses `PROFILE`: `inventory_submit_needs_a_profile_that_parses`. The test calls `check_submit(AgentName::Initializer, ...)` on files in a temporary folder. The submit check must refuse each broken input and accept the valid one. The test runs these steps in order:

1. Write `PROFILE` and no `INVENTORY.md`. The check refuses the submit with a message that holds `INVENTORY.md before you submit`.
2. Write `INVENTORY.md`. The check accepts the submit, because `PROFILE` parses.
3. Change `PROFILE` with `replace` and expect a refusal. The change `reference = null` gives `Line 11: TOML has no null. Omit `reference``. The change `[[conventions]]` gives ``Write `[conventions]`, not `[[conventions]]```. The change `schema_version = "0.1"` gives ``Write `schema_version = 1```.
4. Remove `project.toml`. The check refuses the submit with a message that holds `project.toml before you submit`.
5. Submit the results of the other initializer roles. Each role has a result with its own fields, and each is accepted.

The fixture is valid on purpose and small on purpose. Each broken variant differs from `PROFILE` by one change, so the refusal message names the one cause. To test a new profile rule, add one `replace` call on `PROFILE` that breaks the rule, then assert on the message. Run the file with `cargo test -p ostra-core doc`.

For the documents and their checks, read [Artifacts and structured documents](artifacts-and-documents.md).

## Read the engine conformance fixtures

The conformance suite checks the planner against its rules. It is one file, `tests/conformance/main.rs`, with about 126 tests. Cargo builds it as the test target `conformance` of `ostra-engine`, because `crates/ostra-engine/Cargo.toml` has this entry:

```toml
[[test]]
name = "conformance"
path = "../../tests/conformance/main.rs"
```

Run it alone with `cargo test -p ostra-engine --test conformance`. The file header says that each fixture belongs to a rule ID of section 8.2 of the handover document. The suite compares values with `pretty_assertions`.

### How a fixture works

The planner `next_steps` is a pure function. It reads a `SessionState` and a `PlanCtx` and returns a list of `Step` values. A fixture needs no model, no database, and no clock. It builds an event history, folds it, and checks the steps. The helper struct `H` does the work:

- `H::new(projects, options)` writes a `SessionCreated` event with `PlanCtx::default()`. It also sets a format command `fmt-<key>` for each project.
- `h.ev(event)` appends a `StoredEvent` with the next `seq`.
- `h.state()` calls `SessionState::fold`.
- `h.summaries()` calls `next_steps` and returns the `summary()` text of each step, for example `spawn generate-spec spec#1`.
- `h.classify`, `h.decide`, `h.start`, `h.finish`, `h.run`, `h.open_gate`, and `h.answer` write the events that the runner writes.

The helper `h.answer` follows the runner. It calls `answer_needs_route`, so an answer with content waits for the judge (rule J1).

This test shows the pattern:

```rust
#[test]
fn d1_explore_leads_to_spec_never_plan() {
    let h = H::explored(&["p"], SessionOptions::default());
    let s = h.summaries();
    assert_eq!(s, vec!["spawn generate-spec spec#1"]);
}
```

### What the fixtures cover

The file has one section per rule family. Test names start with the rule ID, so you can search for a rule by name. Some examples:

| Prefix | Topic |
| --- | --- |
| `d1` to `d10` | Explore, spec, plan, fact check, approval, scheduling, test stage, blocked phases, and changes at plan approval. |
| `t1` to `t6` | The test stage: no tests between phases, one format run, a fan-out of the analyzer, and a batched closing gate. |
| `p2`, `p3`, `p4` | Resume of the same execution, three containment signals that pause the session, and a YOLO session that leaves a stopped execution to the user. |
| `j1` | Judge routing of gate answers that carry content. |
| `f1` | Feedback on an implementation. |
| `h1` to `h9` | Helper coordination, `subagent_ask`, and pair loops between agents. |
| `b1` to `b7` | Documentation sessions and books. |
| `o2` to `o6` | Projects that a plan creates. |
| `rule_i1` | The init flow. |

Other tests check pause and resume, budget pause, attached files and uploads, the quick answer and quick change categories, and the light and full tracks.

For the rules themselves, read [The session pipeline](session-pipeline.md) and [Engine runtime](engine-runtime.md).

The web tests use Vitest in the `jsdom` environment. `web/vite.config.ts` sets `env: { VITE_MOCK: "1" }` and includes `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`. The mock flag makes the app use the mock API in `web/src/api/mock`, so no server is needed.
