sections.title: Reference: engine, agent, and core limits
sections.summary: Lookup tables for the named constants of ostra-engine, ostra-agents, and ostra-core. Each row gives the value, the unit, and the effect, grouped by source file.
sections.body:
This page lists the named constants of three crates: `ostra-engine`, `ostra-agents`, and `ostra-core`. Without a list, a reader must open each file to learn a cap, a retry count, or a size limit. Each table below covers one source file. A row gives the constant, its value, its unit, and what it controls.

## How to read these tables

These rules apply to all tables:

- A value in `chars` counts Unicode characters, not bytes.
- A value in `bytes` counts bytes of the encoded text.
- A constant that is not `pub` is internal to its file. The table marks it as `internal`. The table lists it because a reader can see its effect.
- A text constant (a `&str`) shows its text or a short description of the text.

The pages that explain the behavior in full are linked in each part. Limits of other crates are on [Reference: executor, tool, policy, and sandbox limits](reference-execution-limits.md), [Reference: server, code, store, and notify limits](reference-server-limits.md), and [Reference: workspace settings and paths](reference-settings.md).

## Engine loop and retry limits in state.rs

The file `crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs` holds the counters that decide when the engine stops a loop and asks the user. `SessionState` folds the events of a session, so the same events always give the same counters. See [Engine runtime](engine-runtime.md) for the fold.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT` | `3` | consecutive FAIL results | The planner opens a gate when `consecutive_fails` reaches `3 + fail_limit_extra`. The gate is "The spec fact-check keeps failing" or "The plan fact-check keeps failing". |
| `REVIEW_CAP` | `3` | review passes per loop | A review loop runs at most 3 passes before the engine stops the loop. In a normal session, the engine then asks the user (`LoopNext::CapReached`). |
| `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` | `10` | review passes per loop | The cap when YOLO mode is on. At the cap, the engine starts a resolve round when the open findings decrease. |
| `ERROR_RETRIES` | `1` | automatic retries | An execution that ends with status `Error` runs again one time without the user. After that, the engine opens a gate. |
| `SUFFICIENCY_ROUNDS` | `3` | judge rounds | The Sufficiency judge runs at most 3 times for research that reports `not_covered` items. After that, the engine goes on to the spec with the research that it has. |
| `AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM` | `"auto_fixable_ids"` | param key | The key in the params of a review execution. Its value holds the auto-fixable rule IDs of the project. |
| `NO_PRIOR_FINDINGS` | `"no findings on the previous pass"` | text | The `Prior findings:` value after a pass that found nothing. It tells the agent that this pass is a repeat pass, not a first pass. |
| `STOPPED_EXECUTION` | `"You stopped this execution."` | text | The error text of an execution that ends as `Cancelled` with no error of its own. |

### How the fact-check limit grows

The fact-check limit is not fixed. The planner compares `consecutive_fails` with `FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT + fail_limit_extra`. The field `fail_limit_extra` starts at `0`.

The method `allow_more` of the `RecurringTrack` trait sets it (`crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs`, about line 4288). The call is `self.fail_limit_extra = self.consecutive_fails`. The engine calls it when the user answers the gate with "run another round".

The new limit is then `3 + consecutive_fails`. This value allows 3 more failing passes before the next gate. The user can also add guidance or stop.

### How the review cap works

The method `effective_cap` returns `REVIEW_CAP` (or `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` in YOLO mode) plus `extra_cap`. A loop checks the cap after each review that has open HIGH or MEDIUM findings. These cases follow when `iterations` reaches the cap:

- **Normal session:** the loop becomes `CapReached` and the engine asks the user.
- **YOLO, first resolve round or findings decrease:** the loop becomes `Resolve`.
- **YOLO, findings did not decrease:** the loop becomes `Blocked`, with the text "The review loop stopped converging". A block gate follows.

When the user answers a block gate with `retry`, the engine sets `extra_cap` to the number of iterations that the loop already ran. The cap then grows by that number.

### What happens when an execution fails

- If the status is `Error` and `retries` is below `ERROR_RETRIES`, the engine counts one retry and starts the execution again.
- If the retries are used, the engine records the failure and opens a gate for the user.
- If the status is `Interrupted` (a pause), the engine does not count a retry. The execution runs again after the resume.

## Runner constants in runner.rs

The file `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs` holds the texts and limits of the `Engine` runner. The runner starts executions, stops sessions, resumes paused runs, and reopens ended sessions for questions.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FORMAT_NOT_APPROVED` | text | text | The output of a skipped format step. The format command in `project.toml` changed outside Ostra and the user did not approve it. |
| `STOPPED_BY_USER` | `"Stopped by the user."` | text | The error of a session that the user stopped. The runner also writes it to each running execution that it cancels offline and to the stage label (`Stopped: ...`). |
| `INSPECT_PROMPT` | text | text | The system prompt of a read-only reopened session (internal). It tells the agent to answer from the conversation and to call no tool. |
| `INSPECT_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `4 * 60 * 60` = `14400` | seconds | A read-only reopened session ends on its own after 4 hours (internal). |
| `PAUSE_RESUME_NOTE` | `"Continue the workflow."` | text | The note that a paused execution gets when the session continues and no other note exists. |
| `RESUMED_STATUS` | text | text | The Activity line where a resumed execution picks up. |
| `MAX_CONTEXT_FILES` | `50` | files per request or addition | The runner refuses a request or an addition with more attached files. The message gives the reason: every agent reads each file. |

### What happens when a format command is not approved

The runner runs a format command only after the user approved it (Rule A1). If the command is not approved, the runner does not run it. The step records `FORMAT_NOT_APPROVED` as its output. The user approves the command in the project settings, and the next run uses it.

### What happens when the user stops a session

Two functions in `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs` stop a session. The live path runs when the server holds the session. The offline path runs when no server holds it.

Both paths refuse a session that already ended. The error is "This session has already ended."

#### Live path: stop_session

The method `stop_session` (about line 716) does these steps:

1. Append `SessionFailed` with `STOPPED_BY_USER`.
2. Cancel the token of each running execution.
3. Send `PermissionAnswer::Deny` to each waiting permission ask of an open gate.
4. Return the session summary.

The method does not undo what the session already did. Each cancelled executor then returns the status `Cancelled`. The fold in `state.rs` shows an execution that is `Cancelled` with no error of its own as `STOPPED_EXECUTION`.

#### Offline path: stop_session_offline

The function `stop_session_offline` (about lines 1092-1136) is for the `ostra stop` command when no server runs. A later server start must not recover and run the executions again. The function does these steps:

1. Write status `Cancelled` and the error `STOPPED_BY_USER` to each running execution. The execution keeps its usage.
2. Append an `ExecutionFinished` event for each of them.
3. Append `SessionFailed` with `STOPPED_BY_USER`.
4. Update the session to status `Failed`, lane `Done`, and the stage label `Stopped: Stopped by the user.`.

The function returns the number of executions that it cancelled.

## Initialization limits in init.rs

The file `crates/ostra-engine/src/init.rs` plans the init flow of a project: scouts, the skill proposal, and the advisor for a created project. These limits keep the cost of init bounded.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_SCOUTS` | `6` | parallel executions | The planner keeps at most 6 scout slices. Scouts run in parallel and each one costs a full execution. |
| `MAX_DEFAULT_GENERATE` | `8` | skills | The skill proposal keeps the first 8 skills with disposition `generate`, in proposal order. The proposal ranks skills by how common they are. |
| `MAX_ADVICE` | `2` | advisor rounds per failing step | A failing init step of a created project goes to the advisor at most 2 times (Rule O5). After that, the user decides. |
| `STACK_REFERENCE_NAME` | `"stack_reference_name"` | init key | The key that the spawn factory resolves to the extracted stack reference file. The value is `_generic` when no reference exists. |
| `MAX_STEP_RESULT_CHARS` | `8000` | chars | The advisor receives at most this many characters of the failed step result. The tool adds the note `(cut at 8000 characters)`. |

### Why the limits exist

- The code states that scouts cost a full execution each. The cap is `6`. An earlier tool allowed 12.
- When the cap drops a skill, the function `cap_generate` sets its disposition to `drop`. The function also appends a note to the description of the skill. The note says that Ostra dropped the skill by default to limit cost, and that the user can choose `generate` to include it. The user can still choose `generate` at the approval gate.
- The advisor result is cut because the start of a result names its shape. A long tail rarely changes the diagnosis.
- A step that the user stopped goes to the user and not to the advisor, because the advisor retries failed steps (Rule P4).

## Upload limits in uploads.rs

The file `crates/ostra-engine/src/uploads.rs` stages files that the user uploads as context (Rule C3). A new task uploads before its session exists. The engine stages the file in the workspace first and claims it into the `uploads/` folder of the session later.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | `25 * 1024 * 1024` = `26214400` | bytes (25 MB) | The largest single upload. The message gives the reason: every agent reads the files. |
| `MAX_UPLOADS` | `20` | files | The most uploads that one request or addition can claim. |

### What happens when an upload is not valid

- If the file is empty, `stage` returns the error "The file is empty."
- If the file is larger than `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, `stage` returns an error with the size in MB.
- The function `safe_name` keeps only the last path segment. It replaces the characters `: * ? \" < > |` with `_`. It removes control characters and leading dots, and it cuts the name to 120 characters. An empty result becomes `upload`. The value `120` is a literal in the code, not a named constant.

## Repo brief limits in brief.rs

The file `crates/ostra-agents/src/brief.rs` builds the repo brief that Ostra adds to the first message of an agent. The limits keep the brief small, because a large brief uses context in every run. See [Agents, prompts, skills, and the spawn contract](agents-and-prompts.md) for the full brief.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_BRIEF_CHARS` | `3600` | chars | The inventory and profile part of the brief. The function `build_brief` cuts a longer brief to this size and adds a closing line. The line says that the brief is cut and points to the inventory file for the rest. |
| `MAX_PROJECT_DOC_CHARS` | `12000` | chars per instruction file | A longer project instruction file is cut. The agent reads the rest from disk. |
| `MAX_SKILL_ROWS` | `16` | rows | The most skill rows in the brief (internal). |
| `MAX_MODULE_ROWS` | `10` | rows | The most module map rows in the brief (internal). The brief leaves out the map when the prompt names no path. |
| `MAX_BRIEF_BOOKS` | `20` | books | The brief names at most 20 documentation books. The function `build_brief` then adds a last line with the count of the other books. The line tells the agent to find them with Glob in the books folder. |
| `BRIEF_HEADING` | `"## Repo brief for "` | heading | Marks a message that already carries a brief. |
| `INSTRUCTIONS_HEADING` | `"## Workspace instructions"` | heading | Starts the workspace instructions part. |
| `PROJECT_DOCS_HEADING` | `"## Project instructions"` | heading | Starts the project instruction files part. |
| `ARTIFACTS_HEADING` | `"## Workspace artifacts"` | heading | Starts the workspace artifacts part. |
| `BOOKS_HEADING` | `"## Workspace documentation"` | heading | Starts the documentation books part. |
| `NEW_PROJECTS_HEADING` | `"## Projects created in this session"` | heading | Starts the part about projects that an agent created in this session (internal). |

### Why the headings exist

The function `augment` returns the first message unchanged when it already contains `BRIEF_HEADING`, `PROJECT_DOCS_HEADING`, `ARTIFACTS_HEADING`, `BOOKS_HEADING`, or `INSTRUCTIONS_HEADING`. Because of this check, a second render never stacks two briefs.

### What happens when the brief is long

- The module map is the largest part. The function `relevant_modules` returns no rows when the prompt names no path. If the prompt names paths, the function keeps the rows whose glob covers a path, at most `MAX_MODULE_ROWS`.
- The function `scope_hints` collects at most 40 path hints from the prompt. The value `40` is a literal in the code.
- The artifact list uses `MAX_BRIEF_ARTIFACTS` from `ostra-core`. See the artifacts table below.

A hidden artifact moves into the Ostra data folder, which no agent can read (Rule W2). See [Artifacts and structured documents](artifacts-and-documents.md).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TAG_ROOT` | `"_artifacts"` | tag root | A request or instruction names an artifact as `@_artifacts/<path>`. No project key can take this root, because project keys start with a letter or digit. |
| `MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES` | `25 * 1024 * 1024` = `26214400` | bytes (25 MB) | The largest artifact that the user can upload or save. The server sets the body limit of the upload route to this value plus 1024 bytes. |
| `MAX_ARTIFACTS` | `2000` | artifacts per workspace | The most artifacts, visible and hidden together. The list function stops at this count. An upload at the limit returns a conflict error. |
| `MAX_BRIEF_ARTIFACTS` | `40` | artifacts | The repo brief names the first 40 visible artifacts. The agent finds the rest with Glob. |
| `TAG` | regex `(?:^\|\s)@([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/(\S+)` | pattern | Finds an `@key/path` tag in text (internal). |

### Why the limits exist

- The upload message gives the reason for the size limit: agents read artifacts whole.
- The message for the count limit gives the reason: the brief of every agent lists the artifacts.

### What happens with a tag

- A tag with root `_artifacts` names a visible artifact. A hidden or missing artifact is not found, and `tag_issues` reports it when the user saves an instruction.
- A tag with a project key names an existing file or folder inside that project. The function drops a path that leaves the project root.
- Any other tag stays plain text (Rule W3).

| `SEQ_ARROWS` | 10 arrows: `-->>`, `->>`, `<<->>`, `<<-->>`, `-->`, `->`, `--x`, `-x`, `--)`, `-)` | arrow list | The arrows that the validator counts as a sequence message (internal). |
| `INLINE_EDGE_TEXT` | regex | pattern | Removes inline edge text, such as `A -- text --> B`, before the validator counts flowchart nodes (internal). |
| `EDGE` | regex | pattern | Splits a flowchart line at its edges, so each piece names one node (internal). |

### What happens when a diagram is too large

The validator refuses the submission and tells the writer to split the diagram. The message gives the counts and the reason: a reader follows a small diagram and loses a large one. A sequence diagram counts each unique participant name, from `participant` and `actor` lines and from message ends. A flowchart counts each unique node ID.

### What happens when a book ID is too long

The function `book_id` sorts and joins the project keys with `_`. Project keys hold no `_`, so different sets of projects give different IDs. If the result is longer than `MAX_BOOK_ID`, the function cuts it and adds `_` and a 16-digit hexadecimal FNV-1a hash of the full ID. The result is never longer than 80 characters.

## Book search ranking constants in book_search.rs

The file `crates/ostra-core/src/book_search.rs` ranks the passages of a book with BM25 over three weighted fields (Rule B8). It then ranks each unit by its best passages. A unit is a section, a sub-section, a glossary term, or an architecture aspect. A hit shows only the passages that matched.

Only `DEFAULT_LIMIT` and `MAX_LIMIT` are `pub`. All other constants in the table are internal to the file.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_LIMIT` | `5` | hits | The number of hits when the `DocsSearch` call gives no `limit`. |
| `MAX_LIMIT` | `15` | hits | The tool clamps `limit` to the range 1 to 15. |
| `WINDOW` | `5` | list items or table rows | A long list or table is cut into passages of 5 items (internal). |
| `PASSAGES_PER_HIT` | `2` | passages | A hit shows at most 2 passages (internal). |
| `K1` | `1.2` | BM25 term saturation | The BM25 `k1` value (internal). |
| `B` | `0.75` | BM25 length normalization | The BM25 `b` value (internal). |
| `W_TITLE` | `2.0` | weight | The weight of a term in the passage title (internal). |
| `W_CODE` | `1.5` | weight | The weight of a term in the code names of a passage, such as paths and symbols (internal). |
| `W_BODY` | `1.0` | weight | The weight of a term in the passage text (internal). |
| `SECOND_SHARE` | `0.35` | share | A unit score adds this share of its second-best passage score (internal). |
| `SHOW_SHARE` | `0.5` | share | A hit does not show a passage with a score below half of the best passage of its unit (internal). |
| `MERMAID_WORDS` | 29 words | keyword list | The index drops these Mermaid keywords from a diagram text, so a diagram matches on its labels (internal). |
| `STOP` | stop word list | word list | The tokenizer drops these common words from a query and from passages (internal). |

### How a unit score is calculated

The unit score is the sum of three parts: the title score, the best passage score, and `SECOND_SHARE` of the second-best passage score. A unit with no passage above the `SHOW_SHARE` cut still shows its first passage.

The function `diagram_words` (about line 534) filters the words of a diagram. It splits the source at each character that is not a letter, a digit, or `_`. It keeps a word only when its length is above 2 and it is not in `MERMAID_WORDS`. The tokenizer does not do this filter.

### Why the code weight is between the other two

The code states the three weights but gives no reason for the values. A reader can see the effect: a term in a title counts twice a body term, and a path or symbol counts 1.5 times. The book writer puts names in backticks, so a search for a symbol finds the part that names it.

| `MAX_CONVERSATION_RUNS` | `6` | runs | A conversation with 6 runs starts fresh. The next ask in a pair loop gets a new subagent (Rule H6). |
| `MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS` | `8000` | chars | The longest `message` of an ask or a reply. The tool also refuses an empty message. |

### What happens when a limit is reached

Each refusal is a text that tells the agent what to do next:

- **Helper limit:** "Continue with what you have: this run already started 3 helpers, the limit."
- **Session limit:** "Continue without asking: this session reached its limit of 24 questions between subagents."
- **Message length:** "Give `message` as plain text of at most 8000 characters. Put longer material in a file and name its path."
- **Helper agent not allowed:** the text lists the agents that Ostra can start and tells the agent to ask an existing subagent by `subagent_id`.

### When a conversation starts fresh

The engine continues the conversation of a subagent unless one of two conditions is true. The first condition is that the user delivered an amendment after the previous run started. The second is that the conversation already has `MAX_CONVERSATION_RUNS` runs. In both cases the next ask starts a new conversation.

The function `ProjectCreateInput::validate` refuses these inputs:

| `SELF_PROTECTION` | `"self-protection"` | guard name | A guard whose denial is a signal. |
| `GIT_METADATA` | `"git-metadata"` | guard name | A guard whose denial is a signal. |
| `GUARDS` | the three names above | guard list | The guards whose denials count as signals (internal). Other guards, such as `write-scope`, refuse ordinary mistakes and send no signal. |

### Which events are signals

- **Guard:** a Layer 1 guard in `GUARDS` refused a tool call.
- **Egress:** the egress proxy refused a loopback, private, or link-local destination.
- **Decoy:** a process opened a decoy credential file.

A refused public host is not a signal, because builds call telemetry hosts. It shows in the Activity view only. A permission rule with the name `secret-read` is not a signal, because only the guard layer counts.

### What happens at the limit

The runner records at most `PAUSE_AFTER` signals for one execution. This cap prevents a retry loop from flooding the log. Appends are serialized, so exactly one append brings the count to 3. That append pauses the session and sets the contained execution. The Activity view then shows "Paused: read the <agent> execution's Activity, because it tripped 3 containment signals".

## Code references

| Path | Symbol | Lines | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs` | `FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT` | 34-47 | Fact-check, review, retry, and sufficiency limits. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs` | `allow_more` | 4287-4289 | Sets `fail_limit_extra` to `consecutive_fails` when the user allows another fact-check round. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs` | `STOPPED_EXECUTION` | 4372 | Error text of a cancelled execution that has no error of its own. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs` | `MAX_CONTEXT_FILES` | 992-1002 | Stop text, inspect timeout, resume texts, and the attached file cap. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs` | `stop_session` | 714-743 | Live stop: appends `SessionFailed`, cancels the tokens, and denies waiting permission asks. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs` | `stop_session_offline` | 1089-1136 | Offline stop: writes `Cancelled` to each running execution, appends `SessionFailed`, and updates the session. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/init.rs` | `MAX_SCOUTS` | 14-24 | Scout, skill, and advisor limits of the init flow. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/init.rs` | `MAX_STEP_RESULT_CHARS` | 212 | Cut limit for the failed step result that the advisor receives. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs` | `MAX_ANSWER_RESEARCH` | 128-131 | Answer item ID and research fan-out cap. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs` | `TITLE_CHARS` | 250 | Longest session title that `clean_title` keeps. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/judge_input.rs` | `FILE_EXCERPT` | 15-44 | Excerpt sizes and the cut rule for judge input. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs` | `MAX_DOCS_WRITERS` | 25-26 | Documentation writer fan-out cap. |
| `crates/ostra-engine/src/uploads.rs` | `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | 10-37 | Upload size and count limits, and file name cleaning. |
| `crates/ostra-agents/src/brief.rs` | `MAX_BRIEF_CHARS` | 15-29 | Repo brief size limits and headings. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs` | `CODE_TOOLS` | 139-223 | Judge route key, retired agents, and code tool names. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/artifacts.rs` | `MAX_ARTIFACTS` | 12-20 | Artifact tag root and caps. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/book.rs` | `MAX_SEQUENCE_PARTICIPANTS` | 17-24 | Diagram limits and book ID length. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/book_search.rs` | `W_TITLE` | 11-25 | Search limits, BM25 values, and field weights. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/book_search.rs` | `diagram_words` | 527-543 | Mermaid keyword list and the filter that keeps diagram label words. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/coord.rs` | `MAX_HELPERS_PER_RUN` | 25-33 | Subagent coordination caps. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/manage.rs` | `MAX_REQUIREMENTS` | 29-31 | ProjectCreate input limits. |
| `crates/ostra-core/src/containment.rs` | `PAUSE_AFTER` | 10-19 | Containment signal limit and guard names. |

sections.title: Reference: executor, tool, policy, and sandbox limits
sections.summary: Lists the named constants of the executor, provider, tool, policy, sandbox, and MCP crates. Each row gives the value, the unit, and the effect.
sections.body:
## What this page lists

A limit that is not written down makes a run fail in a way that is hard to explain. This page lists the named constants that bound an agent run: model turns, output sizes, timeouts, terminal sizes, failure streaks, proxy connections, and tool results. Each table is for one crate and one source file, so a reader can find the file that defines a value.

The page covers these crates:

- `ostra-exec-native`: the native agent loop.
- `ostra-providers`: the Anthropic request builder.
- `ostra-exec-harness`: the executor that runs an installed CLI under a PTY.
- `ostra-tools`: the Bash, Read, and WebFetch tools.
- `ostra-policy`: the build-failure streak and the guard names.
- `ostra-sandbox`: the egress proxy and the decoy files.
- `ostra-mcp`: the cap on a tool result.

Each constant is a compile-time value in Rust source. No workspace setting changes it, so a change needs a new build (`cargo build --workspace`). The one exception is the `idle_nudge` field of the harness executor config, which starts at `DEFAULT_IDLE_NUDGE`. Workspace settings are in [Reference: workspace settings and paths](reference-settings.md). Limits of the engine, agents, and core crates are in [Reference: engine, agent, and core limits](reference-engine-limits.md). Limits of the server, code, store, and notify crates are in [Reference: server, code, store, and notify limits](reference-server-limits.md).

A constant that is only a regular expression or a list of words is described by its purpose and not by its full text.

## Native executor loop limits

The native executor runs the agent loop on an API key. [Native executor and model providers](native-executor.md) explains the loop. These constants are in `crates/ostra-exec-native/src/lib.rs`.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_TURNS` | 400 | model turns | Upper bound on model turns in one execution. The loop stops with the error "The run passed 400 model turns without calling" the submit tool. It guards against a loop that never submits. |
| `MAX_TOKEN_CONTINUES` | 3 | turns | Number of "continue" turns after the model hits its output limit without a tool call. The fourth stop fails the run with "The model kept hitting its output limit without finishing." |
| `COMPACT_AT` | 0.95 | share of context window | The loop compacts the conversation when the estimated context reaches this share of the window. |
| `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` | 200000 | tokens | Context window for a model that the models.dev catalog does not list. |
| `DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT` | 32000 | tokens | Output limit for a model that the models.dev catalog does not list. |
| `COMPACT_RETRY_GROWTH` | 0.02 | share of context window | After a compaction that returns no summary, the next try waits until the context grows by this share. Each try sends the whole conversation, so a retry at every turn costs too much. |
| `EMIT_LIMIT` | 8192 (8 KiB) | bytes | The Activity output that the loop emits for a tool result is cut to this size. The model still gets the full output. |
| `CLEANUP_GRACE` | 3 | seconds | Time that a cancelled or timed-out run has to kill its tools before it returns. |
| `FLUSH_AT` | 160 | characters | The `Coalescer` sends buffered model text or thinking text as one Activity entry when the buffer reaches this size or ends with a newline. It also sends it when the kind of text changes. |
| `COMPACTION_RECORD` | `"compaction"` | message role name | The role that the loop stores for a compaction message. When the loop rebuilds a transcript, a record with this role replaces the messages before it. |
| `COMPACT_INSTRUCTIONS` | text | prompt | The instruction sent with a compaction request. It tells the model to keep the task, the files read, the files changed, the decisions, the failed commands, the work left, and the next step. |
| `AFTER_COMPACTION` | text | user message | The message appended after a compaction. It tells the model that earlier tool results are gone and to read a file again when it needs the content. |

### What happens when

- **The context reaches `COMPACT_AT`.** The loop compacts only when the last message has the role user, because a compaction needs no open tool call. It emits the status "Compacting the conversation" and records the result as a `compaction` message.
- **A compaction returns no summary.** The loop remembers the context size. It tries again only after the context grows by `COMPACT_RETRY_GROWTH` of the window.
- **The model stops at its output limit with no tool call.** The loop sends a "continue" turn, up to `MAX_TOKEN_CONTINUES` times, then fails the run.
- **The run is cancelled or its time budget ends.** The loop cancels the inner run and waits up to `CLEANUP_GRACE` for the tools to stop. A time-out ends with the status error and the text "timed out after N s".
- **The model is not in the catalog.** The loop uses `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` and `DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT`. A model with a larger window then compacts later than it needs to, and a model with a smaller window can fail before the loop compacts.

## Anthropic provider constants

The Anthropic provider builds the request body and the beta header. These constants are in `crates/ostra-providers/src/anthropic.rs`. [Native executor and model providers](native-executor.md) explains the provider.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | URL | Base URL when the credential names no other. The provider removes a trailing `/`. |
| `API_VERSION` | `2023-06-01` | header value | Sent as the `anthropic-version` header on each request. |
| `COMPACT_BETA` | `compact-2026-09-04` | beta name | Added to `anthropic-beta` for a compaction request, and when the messages hold a signed compaction block. |
| `FALLBACK_BETA` | `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` | beta name | Added when the request asks for a refusal fallback and the model supports it. The body then holds `fallbacks: "default"`. |
| `INTERLEAVED_BETA` | `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14` | beta name | Added when a budget model thinks between tool calls and the request has client tools. |
| `WINDOW_BETA` | `model-context-window-exceeded-2025-08-26` | beta name | Added for models before Claude 4.5. Without it, input plus `max_tokens` past the window fails validation. With it, generation stops at the window. |
| `ANSWER_RESERVE` | 16000 | tokens | Room kept for the answer under a thinking budget. The budget must stay below `max_tokens`, and an answer can be a whole file written in a tool call. |
| `MIN_BUDGET` | 1024 | tokens | The smallest thinking budget that the API accepts. The provider sends no thinking block when the budget is smaller. |
| `INVALID_INPUT_KEY` | `__invalid_json` | JSON key | The provider sets this key on a tool-use input whose streamed JSON did not parse. The agent loop answers such a call with an error result and does not run the tool. |

### Thinking budget by effort

For a budget model, the provider computes the thinking budget from the output ceiling of the model:

| Effort | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | No thinking budget. |
| `Medium` | Ceiling divided by 8. |
| `High` | Ceiling divided by 4. |
| `Xhigh` | Ceiling divided by 2. |
| `Max` | Ceiling minus `ANSWER_RESERVE`. |

The provider then limits the budget to `max_tokens` minus `ANSWER_RESERVE`. It skips this limit when the model interleaves thinking with tool calls. A budget below `MIN_BUDGET` is dropped.

## Harness executor timing and screen markers

The harness executor runs an installed CLI under a PTY and watches its screen. [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) explains the adapters and the end of a run. These constants are in `crates/ostra-exec-harness/src/executor.rs`.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GIT_CHECK_EVERY` | 2 | seconds | The executor checks the repositories of a running harness for a planted `commondir` at this interval. It undoes each one and reports it as a denial of the `git-metadata` guard, which counts as a containment signal. The CLI's own commands pass no hook that Ostra can check, so a clock keeps the exposure short. |
| `DEFAULT_IDLE_NUDGE` | 240 | seconds | Time that a session can have no hook event and no terminal output before Ostra types a reminder to submit. The `idle_nudge` field of the executor config starts at this value. |
| `MAX_IDLE_NUDGES` | 2 | nudges | After two reminders, the next idle period ends the run with `End::Idle`. |
| `AFTER_SUBMIT_GRACE` | 20 | seconds | After the submit call, the time to wait for the turn to end before the executor closes the harness. |
| `AGY_QUIET_AFTER_SUBMIT` | 4 | seconds | Antigravity has no Stop hook. A submit followed by this much terminal quiet ends the turn. |
| `AUTH_MARKERS` | 14 strings | lower-case screen text | Text such as `please log in`, `not logged in`, `run /login`, `invalid api key`, `select login method`, and `waiting for auth`. A match ends the run with `End::Auth`. |
| `FATAL_MARKERS` | 4 strings | lower-case screen text | `failed to construct executor`, `unknown component:`, `unknown model`, and `model not found`. A match ends the run with `End::Fatal` and the text "the harness reported" plus the marker. |
| `TRUST_MARKERS` | 6 strings | lower-case screen text | Folder-trust prompts such as `trust this folder` and `open restricted`. The executor answers according to the harness. |
| `MODEL_OFFER_MARKERS` | 1 string | lower-case screen text | The text `use existing model`. It marks a new-model offer at startup. |

### Folder-trust answers

The executor answers a trust prompt by harness, because trust can load files from the repository:

- **Claude Code:** The executor accepts. Claude Code loads only user settings (`--setting-sources user`) and only the Ostra MCP config (`--strict-mcp-config`), so trust adds nothing from the repository.
- **Codex:** The executor accepts only "Open restricted". The option "Trust and continue" saves trust and loads the `.codex/` config and hooks of the repository, so the executor ends the run with a reason.
- **Grok Build:** The executor never accepts. Trust makes Grok Build run the hooks and MCP servers of the folder, so the user decides in Grok.

The executor keeps the routed model on a new-model offer. The function `keep_model_key` reads the highlighted line of the screen and converts it to lower case. These rules apply:

- If the highlighted line contains `use existing`, the executor presses Enter.
- If the highlighted line contains `try new`, the executor presses Down.
- If the highlighted line contains neither text, or no line is highlighted, the executor presses nothing.

The executor never accepts the new-model offer. Accepting the offer changes the run and the default model of the user.

### Values in the loop that have no constant name

The wait loop in `executor.rs` also uses these values in the code:

- The loop checks `AUTH_MARKERS`, `FATAL_MARKERS`, `TRUST_MARKERS`, and `MODEL_OFFER_MARKERS` only when the run has made no tool call and is less than 120 seconds old.
- The loop answers at most 6 trust prompts, and it waits 400 milliseconds after each answer.
- The run budget is the `timeout_secs` of the spec, with a minimum of 30 seconds. A wait for a message does not count against the budget.

## Harness terminal sizes and buffers

Each harness runs in a pseudo terminal (PTY). Ostra keeps a screen model of it and streams the output to viewers. These constants are in `crates/ostra-exec-harness/src/pty.rs`.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_COLS` | 120 | columns | Starting width of the terminal. The executor config also starts with this width. |
| `DEFAULT_ROWS` | 40 | rows | Starting height of the terminal. |
| `MAX_COLS` | 1000 | columns | Largest width. `clamp_size` limits a requested width to this value. |
| `MAX_ROWS` | 500 | rows | Largest height. |
| `MIN_COLS` | 20 | columns | Smallest width. The `vt100` 0.16 library underflows, and panics its reader thread, on a one-column screen that draws a wide character. No harness UI draws usefully below this width. |
| `MIN_ROWS` | 5 | rows | Smallest height. The same library underflows on a one-row screen that wraps a line. |
| `SCROLLBACK` | 2000 | lines | Scrollback lines that the screen model keeps. |
| `WRITE_QUEUE` | 256 | pending writes | Size of the input queue. When it is full, `PtySession::write` returns a `WouldBlock` error with the text "the program is not reading its terminal input". A harness that stops reading therefore cannot block a caller. |
| `STREAM_BUFFER` | 256 | output chunks | Number of output chunks that a viewer can fall behind by. After that, Ostra resyncs the viewer from a fresh snapshot. |
| `PARENT_SESSION_ENV` | 16 names | environment variables | Variables that Ostra removes from the child environment, such as `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `GROK_SESSION_ID`, and `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT`. A child that inherits them runs as a nested child of the harness session that started Ostra. Claude Code does not save such a session, so the session cannot resume. |

## Harness launch and bridge constants

These constants set how Ostra starts a harness and how the hooks reach the server. They are in `crates/ostra-exec-harness/src/launch.rs` and `crates/ostra-exec-harness/src/protocol.rs`.

### launch.rs

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECS` | 86400 (24 hours) | seconds | Timeout that Ostra writes into the launch config of the harnesses. It applies to each Claude Code hook, each Codex hook handler, and each Grok Build hook block. It also sets `mcp_servers.ostra.tool_timeout_sec` for Codex and `tool_timeout_sec` of the Ostra MCP block in the Grok Build config. A permission ask waits for the user, so the hook and the tool call must not time out first. |
| `MAX_ARG_PROMPT` | 98304 (96 KiB) | bytes | Largest first message that Ostra passes on the command line. A longer message goes to `first-message.md` in the config folder, and the prompt tells the agent to read that file first. |
| `INSPECT_TOOLS` | `Read,Bash,Grep,Glob` | tool list | Claude Code tools of a read-only inspection session. The bridge refuses every call. The session keeps plain tools to refuse because a model with no tools replies with nothing. |
| `GROK_PRIVATE` | `config.toml`, `trusted_folders.toml`, `leader.sock` | file names | Entries of the real `GROK_HOME` that the per-execution home does not share. Ostra rewrites the config, extends the trust list, and the session must run its own leader and read the hooks of its own execution. |

### protocol.rs

| Constant | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ENV_URL` | `OSTRA_URL` | Environment variable with the server URL for the hook and the MCP shim. |
| `ENV_EXECUTION` | `OSTRA_EXECUTION` | Environment variable with the execution ID. |
| `ENV_TOKEN` | `OSTRA_TOKEN` | Environment variable with the token of the execution. |
| `ENV_HARNESS` | `OSTRA_HARNESS` | Environment variable with the harness name. |
| `POLICY_PATH` | `/internal/policy` | Server path that receives each hook event for a policy decision. |
| `MCP_PATH` | `/internal/mcp` | Server path that the MCP stdio shim calls. |
| `MCP_SERVER_NAME` | `ostra` | Name of the MCP server that every harness registers. |

The Bash tool removes every `OSTRA_*` variable from the environment of a command, so an agent command cannot read the token. See [Bash tool limits](#bash-tool-limits).

## Bash tool limits

The Bash tool runs one shell command per call. [Native tools and their limits](tools.md) explains the input shape and the Windows shell handling. These constants are in `crates/ostra-tools/src/bash.rs`.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` | 120000 (2 minutes) | milliseconds | Timeout when the call gives no `timeout`. |
| `MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` | 600000 (10 minutes) | milliseconds | Largest timeout. The tool limits the `timeout` argument to a range of 1 to this value. |
| `MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS` | 30000 | characters | Largest output that the tool returns to the model. A longer output keeps its start and end and loses the middle. |
| `CAPTURE_HALF` | 131072 (128 KiB) | bytes | Size of the head buffer and of the tail buffer. The capture keeps all output up to twice this size. After that, it keeps the first 128 KiB and the last 128 KiB and inserts the text "[N bytes dropped]". |
| `DRAIN_GRACE` | 300 | milliseconds | After the command ends, the time to wait for more output from the pipe. If a background process still holds the pipe, the tool kills the process tree so that nothing outlives the call. |
| `KILL_WAIT` | 5 | seconds | Time to wait for a killed command to be reaped. The wait has a limit because on Windows a process killed during its own creation never exits. |
| `SCRIPT` | shell text | script | The wrapper that runs the command with `eval`. A `cd` therefore persists into the `EXIT` trap, which writes the final directory to a file for the next call. The Windows version uses `pwd -W` to write a Windows path. |

### What happens when

- **The command exceeds the timeout.** The tool kills the process tree, waits up to `KILL_WAIT`, then drains the output for `DRAIN_GRACE`.
- **The run is cancelled.** The tool follows the same steps as for a timeout.
- **The command prints more than 256 KiB.** The capture drops the middle. The model then sees at most `MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS` characters.
- **The command prints nothing.** The result is the text "(no output)".
- **The saved working folder no longer exists.** The tool uses the repo root and saves it as the working folder.

## Read and WebFetch limits

The Read tool and the WebFetch tool each have caps on size. These constants are in `crates/ostra-tools/src/fs.rs` and `crates/ostra-tools/src/web.rs`.

| File | Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fs.rs` | `DEFAULT_LINES` | 2000 | lines | Number of lines that Read returns when the call gives no `limit`. |
| `fs.rs` | `MAX_LINE_CHARS` | 2000 | characters | A longer line is cut and ends with "[line truncated]". |
| `fs.rs` | `MAX_READ_BYTES` | 52428800 (50 MiB) | bytes | Read refuses a larger file. The error tells the agent to use `head`, `tail`, or `sed -n` in Bash. |
| `web.rs` | `MAX_BODY_BYTES` | 5242880 (5 MiB) | bytes | WebFetch reads at most this many bytes of the body and cuts the rest. |
| `web.rs` | `MAX_TEXT_CHARS` | 100000 | characters | Largest text that WebFetch returns after it converts the body to text. |
| `web.rs` | `MAX_REDIRECTS` | 10 | redirects | A chain with more than 10 redirects fails with "too many redirects". |

WebFetch follows a redirect only inside one host and port, and only for the schemes `http` and `https`. The policy checks only the first URL. A redirect to another host therefore comes back to the model as a new URL to fetch, and the policy checks it again.

## Build failure streak thresholds

The policy engine counts consecutive failed build and test commands in one execution. These constants are in `crates/ostra-policy/src/build.rs`. [Policy engine: guards, permissions, and containment](policy-guards.md) explains where the streak sits among the guards.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RECALL_THRESHOLD` | 2 | consecutive failures | At this count, the streak asks for a lesson recall for the diagnostic signature. Recall comes one failure before the warning, so a known fix arrives at attempt 2. |
| `WARN_THRESHOLD` | 3 | consecutive failures | From this count, the streak adds a note. The note tells the agent to state the root cause and what will change before the next attempt. |
| `DENY_THRESHOLD` | 5 | consecutive failures | At this count, `Streak::blocked` returns true. Ostra refuses further build and test commands, and the agent must call its submit tool with status `stuck`. |
| `MAX_HISTORY` | 12 | entries | Number of recent failure signatures that the streak keeps, and the largest number of recoveries that wait for a lesson. The oldest entry is dropped first. |

The other constants in this file are regular expressions:

- `FALLBACK_BUILD` matches common build tools, such as `cargo`, `mvn`, `gradle`, `tsc`, `make`, `pytest`, `go build`, `npm test`, and `uv run pytest`. The policy uses it only when the project has no configured commands.
- `PLACEHOLDER` matches `{NAME}` tokens in a configured command. Each token becomes a wildcard, so `cargo test --workspace` and a template such as `./mvnw test -pl {MODULE}` both work as matchers.
- `FAILURE_MARKERS` has 15 patterns, such as `BUILD FAILURE`, `error TS<digits>`, `npm ERR!`, and a Python traceback. A match marks the output as failed when no exit code is known.
- `EXIT_CODE_PATTERNS` has 3 patterns that read an exit code from text, such as `Exit code 1`.
- `INTERRUPTED` matches `timed out`, `interrupted`, `canceled`, and `cancelled`. An error with such text counts as no evidence, so it does not extend the streak.
- `DIAGNOSTIC` matches lines that name a cause, such as `cannot find symbol`, `AssertionError`, and `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- `NORM_PREFIX`, `NORM_PATH`, `NORM_POS`, `NORM_LINE`, `NORM_VERSION`, and `NORM_SPACE` normalize a diagnostic line into a signature. They remove the level prefix, replace paths with `<path>` and versions with `<v>`, remove line positions, and collapse spaces. The signature has at most 160 characters.

### What happens when

- **A build passes after at least `WARN_THRESHOLD` failures with a known signature.** The streak records a pending recovery and tells the agent to record the fix with the Memory tool. When a recovery is pending, the `lesson-gate` guard refuses a `Report` call with no `reason` and a `submit_` call with status `ok`.
- **A build passes after fewer failures.** The streak resets with no lesson request.
- **A command has no exit code and no output, and the result is unknown.** The streak treats the result as no evidence.

## Guard identifiers

Each guard has a string name. A denial carries the name, and the web console and the containment signals use it. The names are constants in `crates/ostra-policy/src/guards.rs`, and three of them come from `crates/ostra-core/src/containment.rs`.

| Constant | Value | What the guard refuses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WRITE_SCOPE` | `write-scope` | A write outside the repo root and the session folder, or outside the scope of the agent. Also a skill written to the older skills folder. |
| `NO_TESTS` | `no-tests-from-implementer` | A write to a test file or test folder by the implementer. Tests run only after the user asks for them at the closing gate. |
| `STATE_OWNERSHIP` | `state-ownership` | A write to a file that Ostra or a role owns. Examples are `knowledge.sqlite3`, `workspace.db`, `registry.db`, the review ledger, the security block file, and the implementer progress file. |
| `ARTIFACT_OWNERSHIP` | `artifact-ownership` | A write to `ostra-spec-*`, `ostra-plan-*`, or `ostra-research-*` by an agent other than generate-spec, plan, or explore. |
| `REPORT_PATH` | `report-path` | A write to a report file that is not the declared report path of the execution. |
| `DOCUMENT_TOOL` | `document-tool` | A direct write to a file that Ostra renders from a typed document. The agent must use the Document tool. |
| `LESSON_GATE` | `lesson-gate` | A report or a submit with status `ok` when a recovery lesson is pending. |
| `BUILD_STREAK` | `build-streak` | A build or test command after `DENY_THRESHOLD` consecutive failures. |
| `WORKSPACE_ARTIFACTS` | `workspace-artifacts` | A write, move, or delete of a workspace artifact. These belong to the user. |
| `WORKSPACE_DOCS` | `workspace-docs` | A write to a workspace book. Ostra writes books from the submit calls of the docs stage. |
| `MANAGE_TOOLS` | `manage-tools` | A project tool call that the agent has no right to make. Only the implementer of a phase in a new project creates that project, and only with a well-formed call. |
| `WINDOWS_PATH` | `windows-path` | A Windows path form that the guards do not compare against. Examples are an alternate data stream, a device name such as `CON`, a UNC path, and a `..` after a junction. |
| `ANSWER_ONLY` | `answer-only` | Any write by a run that only answers another subagent. |
| `REPLY_FIRST` | `reply-first` | A submit call by a run that owes an answer to another subagent. |
| `SELF_PROTECTION` | `self-protection` | A write, move, or delete of the binary, configuration, or databases of Ostra. |
| `GIT_METADATA` | `git-metadata` | A direct write under `.git`. Files there decide which programs git runs. |
| `SECRET_READ` | `secret-read` | A read of Ostra credentials, session records, or process memory. This guard applies to every tool and mode. |

The last three names come from `ostra-core`, because they also count as containment signals. `PAUSE_AFTER` in `crates/ostra-core/src/containment.rs` is 3. It is the number of signals in one execution that pause the session. [Reference: engine, agent, and core limits](reference-engine-limits.md) lists it.

The other constants in `guards.rs` are patterns that support the guards:

- `TOOL_OWNED`, `AGENT_OWNED`, and `ARTIFACTS` list the protected file names with their owners and the reason for each.
- `STATE_NAME` is one pattern for all protected state names. The policy uses it to scan inline interpreter code.
- `TEST_DIR` and `TEST_FILE` decide what counts as a test path.
- `PROC_SECRET` matches `/proc/<pid>/environ`, `/proc/<pid>/mem`, and `/proc/<pid>/fd`.
- `PLAIN_READERS` lists commands that only read, such as `cat` and `head`.
- `PATH_CANDIDATE` and `WIN_PATH_CANDIDATE` find path-like words in shell text. The second pattern applies only on Windows.
- `WRITE_API`, `PY_OPEN_WRITE`, and `SPAWN_API` find file writes and process starts in inline interpreter code.

## Sandbox egress proxy limits and hosts

The egress proxy is the only way out of a sandbox. It sees the destination host and port of each connection and connects to the address that it checked. [Sandbox: kernel enforcement under agent commands](sandbox.md) explains the network modes. These constants are in `crates/ostra-sandbox/src/egress.rs`.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_HEAD` | 8192 (8 KiB) | bytes | Largest request head. A longer head gets the reply "400 Bad Request" with the text "Keep the request head under 8 KiB, because the egress proxy refuses longer ones." |
| `MAX_CONNECTIONS` | 256 | connections | Number of connections that one proxy serves at the same time. The proxy drops a new connection when all 256 slots are in use. |
| `HEAD_TIMEOUT` | 30 | seconds | Time to read a request head, the TLS ClientHello, or the answer of an upstream proxy. After that, the proxy closes the connection. |
| `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | 10 | seconds | Time to connect to one upstream address. The proxy tries the next address after a time-out or an error. With several addresses, the total connect time can exceed 10 seconds. |
| `MAX_HELLO` | 32768 (32 KiB) | bytes | Largest TLS ClientHello. A real one is a few KiB, so the proxy treats a larger one as invalid. |
| `PROXY_USER` | `ostra` | user name | The user name in the URL of a loopback proxy. The password is a random secret of the execution. On macOS every sandbox shares the loopback of the host, so each request must carry this credential. |
| `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | 26 hosts | host names | Package registries and source hosts that a build fetches from under the network mode `allowlist`. |

A host rule that has no port allows ports 443 and 80. A rule can be `host`, `*.domain`, an IPv4 address, or `[v6]`. The rule `*.domain` matches every name below `domain` but not `domain` itself.

### Default allowed hosts

Under `allowlist`, the proxy allows these hosts for every command:

- **Rust:** `index.crates.io`, `static.crates.io`, `static.rust-lang.org`, `crates.io`.
- **JavaScript:** `registry.npmjs.org`, `registry.yarnpkg.com`, `repo.yarnpkg.com`.
- **Python:** `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`.
- **Go:** `proxy.golang.org`, `sum.golang.org`.
- **GitHub:** `github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`.
- **JVM:** `repo.maven.apache.org`, `repo1.maven.org`, `services.gradle.org`, `plugins.gradle.org`, `plugins-artifacts.gradle.org`, `dl.google.com`, `maven.google.com`.
- **Ruby:** `rubygems.org`, `index.rubygems.org`.
- **.NET:** `api.nuget.org`.

The function `model_hosts` returns the model API and sign-in hosts of each harness. The authors measured them with one run each. A harness gets its own hosts under every network choice. Under `allowlist`, every command can reach the hosts of all four harnesses, so a build or a test can call a model API.

| Harness | Model hosts |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `api.anthropic.com`, `console.anthropic.com`, `platform.claude.com`, `claude.ai` |
| Codex | `api.openai.com`, `chatgpt.com`, `auth.openai.com` |
| Grok Build | `api.x.ai`, `auth.x.ai`, `accounts.x.ai`, `grok.com`, `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com` |
| Antigravity | `cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`, `daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com`, `www.googleapis.com`, `lh3.googleusercontent.com` |

The user list `allowed_hosts` in the sandbox settings adds to these hosts under `allowlist` and `public`. Under `none` and `host`, the proxy has no host lists.

### What happens when

- **A client sends a request head over 8 KiB.** The proxy replies "400 Bad Request" and closes the connection.
- **A client sends nothing for 30 seconds.** The proxy closes the connection with no reply.
- **All 256 slots are busy.** The proxy drops the new connection. The client sees a closed connection.
- **The accept call fails.** The proxy waits 50 milliseconds before it accepts again. The cause is most likely a lack of file descriptors, and an immediate retry loops with no pause.
- **An upstream address does not answer within 10 seconds.** The proxy tries the next address. Each address gets its own `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, so the total wait grows with the number of addresses. After the last address fails, the proxy fails the connection.

## Sandbox decoy files

A decoy is a credential path that an agent has no reason to read. When a command opens one inside the sandbox, Ostra records a containment signal. These constants are in `crates/ostra-sandbox/src/decoy.rs`.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HOME_DECOYS` | `.ssh/id_rsa`, `.ssh/id_ed25519`, `.git-credentials`, `.vault-token` | paths under the home folder | The built-in decoys. Common tools do not open these on their own, apart from `ssh`. The decoy keys are planted only where no SSH port is reachable. `~/.netrc` is not a decoy because Python `requests` and Go module downloads read it on every fetch. |
| `MAX_WORKSPACE_DECOYS` | 32 | paths | Largest number of decoys that one workspace adds with `sandbox_decoys`. Each decoy is a watch and a bind mount. Settings validation reports an error above this count. |
| `B64` | 64 characters | alphabet | Characters for the random text of a fake SSH key and a fake vault token. |
| `HEX` | `0123456789abcdef` | alphabet | Characters for the random text of a fake Git credential and a generic decoy. |
| `TAG_PREFIX` | `dev.ostra.decoy.` | string | Starts every Seatbelt message that marks a decoy. Ostra reads these messages from the macOS system log. |

A workspace adds to the built-in list and cannot remove from it. A workspace entry must be a file path that starts with `~/`. Ostra refuses an entry that names the sign-in file of a harness CLI, because a decoy there signs that CLI out in the sandbox.

On Linux, the sandbox binds a fake file read-only and Ostra watches it with inotify. On macOS, Seatbelt cannot bind a file in. A decoy there is an existing file that the policy refuses to read, and only admin accounts can read the refusal from the log. A missing file raises no report, so only existing files become decoys.

## MCP tool result cap

The MCP client passes the result of an MCP tool call to the agent. [Integrations: MCP servers and web push](integrations.md) explains the client. This constant is in `crates/ostra-mcp/src/content.rs`.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_RESULT` | 102400 (100 KiB) | bytes | Longest tool result that the client passes on. The client cuts the rest at a character boundary and adds a note such as "(5 more bytes cut)". |

If the server flags a result with `isError`, `result_text` returns the text as an error. If a result has no text content but has `structuredContent`, the client prints that value as indented JSON.
