sections.title: Reference: server, code, store, and notify limits
sections.summary: Lists the named constants of ostra-server, ostra-code, ostra-store, ostra-notify, and ostra-workspace with value, unit, and effect: sign-in lifetimes, WebSocket caps, file and git limits, code index and LSP limits, store limits, and push encryption sizes.
sections.body:
Ostra keeps its safety limits and timeouts as named constants in the Rust source. Without a list, a reader must open each file to learn how long a sign-in lasts, how large a pasted terminal message can be, or when a language server stops. This page lists these constants with their value, unit, and effect, grouped by crate and file.

None of these constants is a setting. To change one, edit the source and compile again with `cargo build --workspace`. The only exception is the environment variable `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL`, which the server reads at start. Settings that a user can change are on [Reference: workspace settings and paths](reference-settings.md).

A value that has a reason in the code or in a comment has the reason next to it. When the source gives no reason, the page gives the rule alone. Sizes use KiB (1,024 bytes) and MiB (1,048,576 bytes). A `Duration` constant shows its unit in seconds or milliseconds.

## Sign-in and cookie constants

The constants in [`crates/ostra-server/src/auth.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/auth.rs) control how long a sign-in token and a sign-in cookie live. They also control how fast a revoke takes effect and how many failed exchanges one address can make. [Server security](server-security.md) explains the full sign-in design.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COOKIE` | `ostra_session` | name | Name of the HTTP cookie that holds the sign-in. |
| `TOKEN_TTL_SECS` | 900 (15 minutes) | seconds | Lifetime of a one-time sign-in token that `mint_token` creates. The registry stores it as `auth:token:<hash>`. |
| `COOKIE_TTL_SECS` | 2,592,000 (30 days) | seconds | Lifetime of a sign-in. It sets the record expiry and the `Max-Age` of the cookie. |
| `RECHECK` | 5 | seconds | How long the server trusts a cookie that it already checked before it reads the registry again. |
| `COOKIE_KEY` | `auth:cookie:` | registry key prefix | The registry stores each sign-in under this prefix plus the SHA-256 hash of the cookie. |
| `SEEN_EVERY_SECS` | 60 | seconds | The server writes `last_seen` for a sign-in at most this often. |
| `MAX_FAILURES` | 5 | failed exchanges | Failed token exchanges that one address can make in one `FAILURE_WINDOW`. |
| `FAILURE_WINDOW` | 60 | seconds | Length of the window in which the server counts failed exchanges. |
| `KEY` (in `private_name`) | `server:private_host` | registry key | Stores the private host name, in the form `ostra-<16 hex digits>.localhost`. The name comes from 8 random bytes. |

### How the server checks a cookie

The cache in `RECHECK` keeps the server from reading the registry on every request. The cache also sets the delay of a revoke from another process. A revoke from this server removes the cached entry at once. A revoke with `ostra sessions` runs in another process, so the running server sees it after at most 5 seconds.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["check_cookie(value)"] --> B{"Checked less than 5 s ago?"}
  B -- yes --> C["Return: expiry is after now"]
  B -- no --> D["Read auth:cookie:hash from the registry"]
  D --> E{"Record found and not expired?"}
  E -- no --> F["Reject the cookie"]
  E -- yes --> G{"last_seen older than 60 s, or legacy record?"}
  G -- yes --> H["Write the record with a new last_seen"]
  G -- no --> I["Accept the cookie"]
  H --> I
```

### What happens when

- **A token is older than 15 minutes.** The exchange fails, because the token has expired. Run `ostra url` to mint a new token.
- **A non-loopback address fails 5 exchanges in 60 seconds.** The method `Auth::exchange_wait` returns the seconds that the address must wait. This is the rest of the window, and at least 1 second. After a successful exchange, `note_exchange` removes the address from the failure map. The test `failed_exchanges_are_limited_per_address` shows this behavior.
- **A loopback peer fails many exchanges.** The server does not count them. The code gives two reasons: a one-time token cannot be guessed, and a count lets any local process lock the user out of sign-in. Tokens have 256 bits, so the limit only stops a guessing loop from filling the log and the registry.
- **A sign-in is 30 days old.** The cookie check fails and the browser must sign in again.
- **An older server stored a sign-in as a bare creation time.** The server reads it as a legacy record and rewrites it in the current form on the next check.

## WebSocket limits

The constants in [`crates/ostra-server/src/ws.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/ws.rs) bound one `/ws` connection. They keep one slow or noisy browser tab from using the memory of the server. [Server API](server-api.md) lists the message kinds.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_MESSAGE` | 1,048,576 (1 MiB) | bytes | Largest client message and largest frame. The upgrade sets both. The comment says terminal pastes are the big messages. |
| `MAX_TERM_INPUT` | 65,536 (64 KiB) | bytes | Largest `term_input` message. One paste cannot fill the write queue of the PTY on its own. |
| `MAX_CHANNELS` | 256 | channels | Largest number of subscriptions on one connection. |
| `TERM_QUEUE` | 64 | binary frames | Frames that the server queues for one socket. A slow socket makes its PTY streams lag and resync. |
| `HINT_QUEUE` | 8 | answers | Hint answers that the server queues for one socket. |
| `HINT_COMPLETE` | `hint:complete` | stream key | Key of the in-flight completion request of a socket. |
| `HINT_SIGNATURE` | `hint:signature` | stream key | Key of the in-flight signature request of a socket. |
| `HINT_NAVIGATE` | `hint:navigate` | stream key | Key of the in-flight navigation request of a socket. |
| `RECHECK` | 5 (same as `auth::RECHECK`) | seconds | How often an open socket checks its sign-in again. |

### What happens when

- **A client subscribes to a 257th new channel.** The server sends the error `Too many subscriptions on one connection. Unsubscribe from channels you no longer show.` A subscribe to a channel that the connection already holds is not refused.
- **A client sends `term_input` of more than 64 KiB.** The server sends the error `Terminal input is limited to 64 KiB per message. Paste in smaller parts.` and does not write the data to the PTY.
- **A client sends a newer hint request of the same kind.** `Streams::replace` stops the older request. The older request never answers, so the editor must ignore it.
- **The cookie of an open socket expires or a CLI revoke removes it.** The socket disconnects at the next 5-second check. A revoke from this server closes the socket at once.

## Files view limits

The Files view reads the project folder and git status on request. Its caps keep one huge folder or one huge file from blocking the server. [Project files and git](project-files-and-git.md) describes the routes. The constants are in [`crates/ostra-server/src/files/mod.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/files/mod.rs), [`browse.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/files/browse.rs), [`watch.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/files/watch.rs), and [`git.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/files/git.rs) in the same folder.

### Sizes and counts

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TEXT_CAP` | 1,048,576 (1 MiB) | bytes | Largest text file that the server serves. A write with a larger body fails with the message `The text is larger than 1 MB, the size Ostra edits in the browser.` |
| `INDEX_CAP` | 50,000 | paths | Most paths in the file name index. The index shows a `truncated` flag when it reaches the limit. |
| `TREE_CAP` | 5,000 | entries | Most entries in one tree listing. |
| `MAX_DEPTH` | 4 | levels | Largest `depth` of a tree request. The server clamps `depth` to 1 through 4 and uses 1 when the request has none. |
| `DIFF_CAP` | 4,194,304 (4 MiB) | bytes | Largest diff that the server returns. A larger diff is marked `truncated`. |
| `CHANGES_CAP` | 500 | files | Most files in the changes list. |
| `ATTRIBUTION_SESSIONS` | 20 | sessions | Sessions that attribution reads, most recently updated first. |
| `MAX_LIVE` | 5,000 | paths | Most live write records for one project. At the limit, the server clears the map. |
| `MAX_PUSHED_PATHS` | 500 | paths | Most paths in one pushed change batch. |
| `MAX_PENDING` (`watch.rs`) | 4,096 | tool calls | Most write tool calls that wait for a result. The comment says calls of the hook bridge log no result, so the map must have a bound. At the limit, the server clears the map. |

### Cache and batch times

A change that an editor or a shell makes outside the tools of Ostra shows up within the windows below.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INDEX_TTL` | 30 | seconds | Life of the cached file name index. |
| `GIT_TTL` | 5 | seconds | Life of the cached git status. |
| `ATTRIBUTION_TTL` | 3 | seconds | Life of the cached attribution map. |
| `DEBOUNCE` | 150 | milliseconds | The watcher collects change events for this time and then pushes one batch. |
| `GIT_TIMEOUT` (`git.rs`) | 15 | seconds | Time limit of a git read for the Files view. After the limit, the read returns nothing. |

### Folder browser

The folder browser in [`browse.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/files/browse.rs) lists folders for the folder picker.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CACHE_TTL` | 2 | seconds | Life of a cached folder listing. |
| `DEFAULT_LIMIT` | 200 | entries | Entries returned when the request has no `limit`. |
| `MAX_LIMIT` | 2,000 | entries | Largest `limit`. The server clamps the request to 1 through 2,000. |
| `MAX_SCAN` | 50,000 | entries | The server stops reading a folder after this many entries, so folders of the size of `/usr/lib` stay fast. |
| `DRIVE_LIST` | `/` | path | On Windows, `/` lists the drives, because Windows has no single root. |

## Git operation limits

Git commands run as child processes with a time limit. After the limit, the server stops the command and reports an error. The constants are in [`crates/ostra-server/src/git.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/git.rs) for clone, pull, and credentials, and in [`crates/ostra-server/src/repo.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/repo.rs) for the repository operations of the Files view.

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CLONE_TIMEOUT` | `git.rs` | 1,800 (30 minutes) | seconds | Time limit of `git clone`. |
| `PULL_TIMEOUT` | `git.rs` | 600 (10 minutes) | seconds | Time limit of `git pull --ff-only`. |
| `QUICK_TIMEOUT` | `git.rs` | 30 | seconds | Time limit of a quiet read that `git_quiet` runs. |
| `PROGRESS_EVERY` | `git.rs` | 250 | milliseconds | The server pushes clone progress at most this often. |
| `TAIL_LINES` | `git.rs` | 12 | lines | The server keeps the last 12 lines of git output for an error message. |
| `DEFAULT_TOKEN_USER` | `git.rs` | `x-access-token` | user name | User name for a saved token that has none. GitHub and GitLab accept any user name with a personal access token. |
| `PREFIX` | `git.rs` | `git_credential:` | registry key prefix | Registry prefix of saved git credentials. The store seals these values. |
| `USE` | `git.rs` | text | message | Hint `Use an https:// or ssh:// URL, or git@host:owner/repo.git.` for a rejected clone URL. |
| `LIST_CAP` | `repo.rs` | 2,000 | paths | Most paths in one change list. A longer list sets `truncated`. |
| `BRANCH_CAP` | `repo.rs` | 500 | branches | The server passes it to `git for-each-ref --count`. |
| `LOCAL_TIMEOUT` | `repo.rs` | 60 | seconds | Time limit of the local git operations: stage, unstage, and checkout. |
| `COMMIT_TIMEOUT` | `repo.rs` | 300 (5 minutes) | seconds | Time limit of `git commit`. Commit hooks can run formatters and tests, so the limit is longer. |
| `REMOTE_TIMEOUT` | `repo.rs` | 600 (10 minutes) | seconds | Time limit of `git fetch --prune` and of push. |

### What happens when

- **A clone runs longer than 30 minutes.** The server stops it and reports the error.
- **A commit hook runs longer than 5 minutes.** The server stops the commit. Make the hook faster or run the commit in a terminal.
- **A repository has more than 2,000 changed paths.** The list holds the first 2,000 and marks the answer as truncated.

## Code request limits in the server

The code endpoints of the server clamp the limits that a browser or an agent sends. The constants are in [`crates/ostra-server/src/code.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/code.rs) and [`crates/ostra-server/src/code_watch.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/code_watch.rs). [Code navigation](code-navigation.md) explains the index and the providers.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_USAGES` | 500 | results | Usages returned when the request has no `limit`. |
| `MAX_USAGES` | 2,000 | results | Largest usages `limit`. The server clamps it to 1 through 2,000. |
| `DEFAULT_SYMBOLS` | 50 | results | Symbols returned when the request has no `limit`. |
| `MAX_SYMBOLS` | 200 | results | Largest symbols `limit`. The server clamps it to 1 through 200. |
| `MAX_SYMBOL_LEN` | 256 | bytes | Longest symbol name in a usages request. The server rejects an empty symbol, a longer symbol, or a symbol with a space or a control character. A symbols query is cut to 256 characters. |
| `HINT_WAIT` | 3 | seconds | How long a hint waits for a language server that is starting. The server keeps starting, and the code index answers completions meanwhile. |
| `MAX_URI_LEN` | 4,096 | bytes | Longest outside URI that a request can name. The server rejects an empty or longer URI with status 400. |
| `MAX_GRAPH_DEPTH` | 3 | levels | Largest `depth` of a dependency graph request. The server clamps it to 1 through 3. |
| `MAX_PUSHED_PATHS` | 200 | paths | Paths that a browser learns about per outside change. For more paths, the browser reloads the whole listing. |
| `QUIET` (`code_watch.rs`) | 250 | milliseconds | The code watcher ends a batch after this much time without a new event. |
| `MAX_WAIT` (`code_watch.rs`) | 2 | seconds | The code watcher ends a batch after this time, even when events continue. |

## Other server limits

These constants belong to smaller areas of `ostra-server`. Each area has its own page that explains the feature.

### Network, artifacts, and commands

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_PORT` | `app.rs` | 7878 | TCP port | Port that the server tries first. Without `--port`, `bind` starts here. With `--port`, the server binds that port only. See [Run and configure Ostra](running-ostra.md). |
| `ARTIFACT_LIMIT` | `api.rs` | 4,194,304 (4 MiB) | bytes | The artifact route returns the text of a file only when the file is not larger. |
| `ARTIFACT_INDEX_CAP` | `nav/mod.rs` | 4,194,304 (4 MiB) | bytes | Workspace search indexes a larger artifact by its label only. |
| `MAX_COMMAND_LEN` | `commands.rs` | 2,000 | bytes | Longest project command. The check uses the length in bytes of the trimmed command. The error message says 2000 characters. A command with a control character is also refused. |
| `MAX_SKILL_BYTES` | `skills.rs` | 524,288 (512 KiB) | bytes | Largest `SKILL.md`. The message gives the reason: agents read it whole, so long material belongs in files next to it. |
| `KINDS` | `skills.rs` | `convention`, `creation`, `test`, `other` | names | The allowed skill kinds. |
| `HARNESS_DIRS` | `skills.rs` | list of folders | paths | The folders where harness CLIs read skills. |

### Workspace search and live updates

The constants in [`crates/ostra-server/src/nav/mod.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/nav/mod.rs) and [`nav/search.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/nav/search.rs) set how often the server pushes updates and how search ranks matches.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TREE_TICK` | 250 | milliseconds | The server rebuilds dirty tree nodes and pushes them at most four times a second for each session. |
| `ACTIVITY_GAP` | 500 | milliseconds | The server sends at most two `activity` messages a second for each workspace. |
| `DEFAULT_LIMIT` (`search.rs`) | 50 | results | Search results when the request has no `limit`. |
| `MAX_LIMIT` (`search.rs`) | 200 | results | Largest search `limit`. |
| `LESSONS_PER_PROJECT` | 20 | lessons | Lessons that search reads from each project. |
| `HINT_CHARS` | 80 | characters | Length of the hint text of a search result. |
| `TEXT_ROWS` | 200 | rows | Rows that the text index returns before the server merges them. |
| `INDEX_ONLY` | 0.45 | score | Score of a match that the index found by word prefix and the in-memory scorer cannot place. |

### MCP, prices, and master key

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | `mcp.rs` | 30 | seconds | Time for an MCP server to start, finish its handshake, and list its tools. |
| `RELIST_AFTER` | `mcp.rs` | 30 | seconds | The server fetches a tool list again when an execution opens and the list is older. |
| `RETRY_AFTER` | `mcp.rs` | 20 | seconds | The server does not start a failed MCP server again sooner. Without this limit, each parallel execution starts it again. |
| `LOGIN_TTL` | `mcp.rs` | 600 (10 minutes) | seconds | Life of an MCP sign-in link. After it, the callback answers that the link expired or was used. |
| `CALLBACK_PATH` | `mcp.rs` | `/mcp/oauth/callback` | route | Path that the OAuth redirect URI ends with. |
| `REFRESH_EVERY` | `prices.rs` | 86,400 (24 hours) | seconds | Age at which the server fetches the model price catalog again. |
| `RETRY_AFTER` | `prices.rs` | 3,600 (1 hour) | seconds | Delay after a failed price fetch. The server keeps the cached prices. |
| `URL_ENV` | `prices.rs` | `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` | environment variable | Replaces the catalog URL. An empty value turns fetching off, for tests and machines without internet. |
| `BACKEND_KEY` | `master_key.rs` | `secrets:backend` | registry key | Records which master key backend the server uses. |
| `CHECK_KEY` | `master_key.rs` | `secrets:check` | registry key | Holds a sealed check value. A key that cannot open it means credentials were saved under another key. |
| `CHECK_PLAIN` | `master_key.rs` | `ostra` | bytes | The plain text of the check value. |
| `SERVICE` | `master_key.rs` | `ostra` | keychain service | Service name of the keychain entry. |
| `KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT` | `master_key.rs` | 10 | seconds | Time limit of a keychain read or write. After it, the keychain counts as unavailable (`timed out`). |

The MCP client is on [Integrations](integrations.md). The master key is on [Server security](server-security.md).

## Code index limits

The code index is in memory. It tokenizes files, links imports and names, and answers the code tools. The limits keep the index and its answers bounded for large projects. The code is in [`crates/ostra-code/src/index.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/index.rs), [`graph.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/graph.rs), [`usage.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/usage.rs), [`hint.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/hint.rs), [`tools.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/tools.rs), and [`lib.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/lib.rs).

### Index size and freshness

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_FILE_BYTES` | `lib.rs` | 1,048,576 (1 MiB) | bytes | The index does not tokenize or index a larger file. The file view shows it without color. |
| `MAX_INDEX_BYTES` | `index.rs` | 268,435,456 (256 MiB) | bytes | Source bytes that one project index holds. The check `self.bytes + st.size > MAX_INDEX_BYTES` skips only the file that exceeds the budget and sets `truncated`. A later, smaller file can still be added. |
| `MAX_SCAN_FILES` | `index.rs` | 4,000 | files | Files that one usages query reads. The index ranks files first, cuts the list, and sets `truncated`. |
| `MAX_IMPORTERS` | `index.rs` | 2,000 | importers | Importers that a dependency answer lists. The index sets `truncated` for more. |
| `FULL_SYNC` | `index.rs` | 30 | seconds | After this time, the index checks every file on disk again, to find edits made outside Ostra. |
| `TRUNCATED` | `provider.rs` | text | message | `The project is larger than the size Ostra indexes, so some files are not searched.` |
| `CLASSES` | `lib.rs` | 11 token classes | list | The order of `CodeFile::classes`. Every native answer uses it. |
| `MAX` (in `signature`) | `lib.rs` | 300 | bytes | A signature longer than this ends with an ellipsis. |
| `MAX` (in `preview`) | `lib.rs` | 240 | bytes | A preview line longer than this is cut at a character boundary. |

### Dependency graph and usage resolution

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_DEF_FILES` | `graph.rs` | 3 | files | A name defined in more files than this links none of them, unless the mentioning file imports the defining file directly. |
| `MAX_LINK_NAMES` | `graph.rs` | 8 | names | Names listed for each step of a walk or a chain. |
| `MAX_REACH` | `graph.rs` | 5,000 | files | Files that a transitive walk visits before it stops. |
| `MAX_CALLER_REFS` | `graph.rs` | 5,000 | references | References that a callers query reads. |
| `MAX_BRIDGE_DEGREE` | `graph.rs` | 200 | links | `related` does not use a file with more links as a stepping stone. |
| `MAX_VIEW_FILES` | `graph.rs` | 150 | files | Files in a package view. |
| `MAX_VIEW_NEIGHBORS` | `graph.rs` | 80 | files | Files in a file view. |
| `MAX_VIEW_CALLEES` | `graph.rs` | 200 | callees | Callees that a symbol view reads for each definition. |
| `MAX_MEMBERS` | `graph.rs` | 40 | members | Members that a type node lists. |
| `MAX_FILE_DEFS` | `graph.rs` | 30 | definitions | Top-level definitions that a node lists from its file. |
| `MAX_VIEW_EDGES` | `graph.rs` | 300 | links | Links that a symbol view draws. The view keeps implementations first and then the heaviest references. |
| `NONE` | `graph.rs` | `u32::MAX` | marker | The unset value in the strongly connected component search (iterative Tarjan). |
| `TOP` | `graph.rs` | `u32::MAX` | marker | Stands for the top level of a file in the key of a symbol view. |
| `MAX_SUPER_DEPTH` | `usage.rs` | 8 | hops | Supertype hops that a member lookup follows. |
| `MAX_CHAIN` | `usage.rs` | 6 | calls | Calls that a receiver chain follows back, as in `a.b().c().d()`. |
| `WRAPPERS` | `usage.rs` | list of type names | list | Types whose members are the members of their first type argument. |
| `PASSTHROUGH` | `usage.rs` | list of call names | list | Library calls that hand back the value that a wrapper holds, as in `repo.find(id).orElseThrow().name`. |
| `FIRST_ARG` | `usage.rs` | `verify`, `spy`, `requireNonNull` | list | Library calls that return their first argument, as Mockito `verify(repo).save(x)` does. |

### Hints and code tool answers

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_INDEX_COMPLETIONS` | `hint.rs` | 50 | items | Index completions per request. The list is incomplete, so the editor asks again as the word grows. |
| `MAX_NAVIGATION` | `hint.rs` | 50 | locations | Locations per jump. The answer is marked `truncated` for more. |
| `NAVIGATION_GROUPS` | `hint.rs` | 8 | definitions | Definitions that the index asks about when the name at the cursor is not defined in its own file. |
| `DEFAULT_LIMIT` | `tools.rs` | 40 | results | Results of a code tool when the call has no `limit`. |
| `MAX_LIMIT` | `tools.rs` | 300 | results | Largest `limit` of a code tool. The tool clamps `limit` to 1 through 300. |
| `MAX_NAMES` | `tools.rs` | 12 | names | A name list longer than this shows the first 12 and the text `+N more`. |
| `MAX_IMPL_GROUPS` | `tools.rs` | 8 | definitions | Definitions that a `CodeImplementations` answer lists when the name has several. |

### Other tables of the index

Several constants in `ostra-code` are tables of names, not limits. [Code navigation](code-navigation.md) explains how each table works.

- `crates/ostra-code/src/lang.rs`: the language definitions `C_COMMENT`, `RUST`, `JS_KEYWORDS`, `JS_DEFS`, `TYPESCRIPT`, `JAVASCRIPT`, `PYTHON`, `GO`, `JVM_MODIFIERS`, `JAVA`, `KOTLIN`, `SCALA`, `CSHARP`, `SWIFT`, `PHP`, `C`, `CPP`, `RUBY`, `LUA`, `SHELL`, `SQL`, `TOML`, `YAML`, `JSON`, `CSS`, `HTML`, and the list `ALL`.
- `crates/ostra-code/src/resolve.rs`: `MANIFESTS` (project manifest file names) and `JS_EXTS` (JavaScript file extensions that import resolution tries).
- `crates/ostra-code/src/outline.rs`: `NOT_BEFORE_MEMBER` (words that cannot start a member).

## Language server and external provider limits

A language server (LSP) is a program that answers code questions for one language. The pool in [`crates/ostra-code/src/lsp/mod.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/lsp/mod.rs) starts a server on the first request for one of its languages, keeps it while it is used, and stops it after it is idle. The constants bound the number of servers, open documents, and wait times.

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IDLE` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 600 (10 minutes) | seconds | A server with no request for this time is stopped. |
| `SWEEP` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 60 | seconds | The pool looks for idle or failed servers once each interval. |
| `MAX_SERVERS` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 8 | servers | Servers that run across all projects. A new server stops the least recently used one. |
| `MAX_OPEN` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 32 | documents | Documents that one server keeps open. An opened document closes the least recently used one. |
| `RETRY` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 30 | seconds | A server that failed to start, or that died, is not started again sooner. |
| `INIT_TIMEOUT` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 60 | seconds | Time for the `initialize` request. It is longer than a normal request, because some servers read the project first. |
| `MAX_DEFINITIONS` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 50 | definitions | Most definitions that the pool collects for one name. |
| `MAX_EXTERNALS` | `lsp/mod.rs` | 20,000 | URIs | Outside URIs that the pool remembers across projects. A new one makes the pool forget the oldest. |
| `MAX_COMPLETIONS` | `lsp/convert.rs` | 1,000 | items | Completion items kept from one server answer. A longer list is marked incomplete. |
| `KINDS` | `lsp/convert.rs` | 25 completion kinds | table | Maps the LSP number of a completion kind to `CompletionKind`. |
| `MAX_MESSAGE` | `lsp/rpc.rs` | 268,435,456 (256 MiB) | bytes | A server message larger than this ends the connection. |
| `STDERR_LINES` | `lsp/rpc.rs` | 20 | lines | The client keeps the last 20 stderr lines of a server for error messages. The client cuts each line to 300 characters. |
| `CONTENT_MODIFIED` | `lsp/rpc.rs` | -32801 | LSP error code | The server dropped the request while it loads. |
| `SERVER_CANCELLED` | `lsp/rpc.rs` | -32802 | LSP error code | The server cancelled the request while it loads. |

### What happens when

- **A ninth server must start.** The pool stops the server that it used least recently and then starts the new one.
- **A server fails to start.** The pool remembers the failure for 30 seconds and returns the error. After 30 seconds, the next request starts the server again.
- **A hint arrives while the server starts.** The hint waits 3 seconds (`HINT_WAIT` on the server side). After that, the index answers completions and the server keeps starting.
- **A document is larger than 1 MiB.** The pool does not open it and returns `is larger than 1 MB, the size Ostra reads.`

### External provider limits

A `CommandProvider` is a program of the project that runs once for each request in the project folder. It reads one JSON request on stdin and writes one JSON answer on stdout. The code in [`crates/ostra-code/src/provider.rs`](crates/ostra-code/src/provider.rs) checks its output against these limits.

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_OUTPUT` | 67,108,864 (64 MiB) | bytes | Largest answer on stdout. A larger answer fails with `Its answer is larger than 64 MB.` |
| `MAX_STDERR` | 1,048,576 (1 MiB) | bytes | Stderr that the server keeps for the error message. |
| `MAX_TOKENS` | 16,777,216 | numbers | Largest token array of a file answer. The length must also be a multiple of 4: line, column, length, and class. |
| `MAX_ITEMS` | 20,000 | items | Most locations, symbols, imports, or importers in one answer. |

## Store limits

The store crate keeps the SQLite files. [Storage](storage.md) describes the tables. The constants below bound the size of stored data and set the first migration state. The code is in [`crates/ostra-store/src/workspace.rs`](crates/ostra-store/src/workspace.rs), [`registry.rs`](crates/ostra-store/src/registry.rs), [`secrets.rs`](crates/ostra-store/src/secrets.rs), and [`memory.rs`](crates/ostra-store/src/memory.rs).

| Constant | File | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TOOL_OUTPUT_LIMIT` | `workspace.rs` | 8,192 (8 KiB) | bytes | The `tool_calls` table keeps at most this much output for one call. |
| `SESSION_COLS` | `workspace.rs` | 13 column names | SQL list | Columns that a session query selects: `id`, `kind`, `request`, `category`, `status`, `lane`, `stage_label`, `projects`, `yolo`, `cost_usd`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `title`. |
| `EXECUTION_COLS` | `workspace.rs` | 17 column names | SQL list | Columns that an execution query selects, from `id` to `summary`. |
| `GATE_COLS` | `workspace.rs` | 10 column names | SQL list | Columns that a gate query selects, from `id` to `answered_at`. |
| `DECISION_COLS` | `workspace.rs` | 9 column names | SQL list | Columns that a decision query selects, from `id` to `at`. |
| `MIGRATIONS` | `workspace.rs` | 3 steps | SQL list | Schema steps of the workspace database. The `user_version` pragma records the number of steps that ran. |
| `MIGRATIONS` | `registry.rs` | 1 step | SQL list | Creates `workspaces`, `push_subscriptions`, and `kv` in the registry. |
| `SCHEMA` | `memory.rs` | SQL text | schema | Creates `lessons`, the `lessons_fts` full-text index, and three triggers that keep the index current. A lesson is unique by `area` and `lesson`. |
| `DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT` | `memory.rs` | 8 | lessons | Lessons that `MemoryRecall` returns when the call has no `limit`. The tool clamps larger values to its own maximum. |
| `NONCE_LEN` | `secrets.rs` | 12 | bytes | Length of the random nonce of each sealed value. |
| `SECRET_KEYS` | `secrets.rs` | `vapid_private`, `provider_credentials:`, `git_credential:`, `mcp_oauth:`, `mcp_secret:` | registry keys | Registry keys whose values the store seals. A name that ends with `:` is a prefix. |
| `SECRETS_VACUUMED` | `registry.rs` | `secrets_vacuumed` | registry key | Set after the rewrite that follows sealing. Without it, the next start runs `VACUUM` again to remove plaintext that an interrupted rewrite left. |
| `ONBOARDED_AT` | `registry.rs` | `onboarded_at` | registry key | Time when the first-run setup finished. A second call of `mark_onboarded` keeps the first time. |

### What happens when

- **A tool call writes output of more than 8 KiB.** The store cuts the text at a character boundary at or below 8,192 bytes. It then adds the line `[truncated: N bytes]` with the full size.
- **A stored value starts with `enc:v1:` and a key cannot open it.** The store reports it as undecryptable. A value without the prefix is returned as it is.
- **Two executions write lessons at the same time.** `MemoryStore` opens a new connection for each call, so the two calls wait on the SQLite file lock.
- **The database is locked.** The connection waits up to 5,000 milliseconds. This value is a literal in `open_connection`, not a named constant. The same function sets the WAL journal mode and sets file mode 0600 on the database, `-wal`, and `-shm` files on Unix.

## Push encryption sizes

The notify crate encrypts a Web Push message with RFC 8291 (`aes128gcm`) and signs the request with a VAPID token. [Integrations](integrations.md) describes the flow. The constants are in [`crates/ostra-notify/src/lib.rs`](crates/ostra-notify/src/lib.rs).

| Constant | Value | Unit | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RECORD_SIZE` | 4,096 | bytes | Record size in the `aes128gcm` header. One record holds the whole message. |
| `MAX_PLAINTEXT` | 3,993 | bytes | Largest message before encryption. Push services accept at most 4,096 bytes of body. |
| `JWT_TTL` | 43,200 (12 hours) | seconds | Life of the VAPID token that signs each request. |
| `PUSH_TTL_SECS` | 86,400 (24 hours) | seconds | Value of the `TTL` header. A push service holds an undelivered message for this long. |

### Why the limit is 3,993 bytes

The body has a fixed overhead, and `MAX_PLAINTEXT` leaves room for it. The header has 16 bytes of salt, 4 bytes of record size, 1 byte of key length, and 65 bytes of sender public key. That is 86 bytes. The AES-GCM tag adds 16 bytes, and the padding delimiter `0x02` adds 1 byte. The overhead is 103 bytes, and 4,096 minus 103 is 3,993.

### What happens when

- **A message is larger than 3,993 bytes.** `encrypt_with` returns `NotifyError::TooLarge` with the size. The text is `payload is N bytes; the limit is 3993`.
- **A request is sent.** It carries the headers `Content-Encoding: aes128gcm`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `TTL: 86400`, and `Urgency: high`.

### Test constants

The constants `PLAINTEXT`, `AS_PRIVATE`, `AS_PUBLIC`, `UA_PRIVATE`, `UA_PUBLIC`, `SALT`, `AUTH`, and `EXPECTED` are in the test module. They are the test vector of RFC 8291 Appendix A. The test checks that `encrypt_with` produces the exact expected body. They are not limits and do not change at run time.

## Workspace constants

The workspace crate holds three named constants. They are messages and a key, not numeric limits.

| Constant | File | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PENDING_MESSAGE` | `crates/ostra-workspace/src/trust.rs` | `Approve the changed commands in settings, because they changed outside Ostra.` | Shown where a program did not start because its settings wait for approval. The MCP connection code uses it. |
| `STARTING` | `crates/ostra-workspace/src/runtime.rs` | `Wait a moment and try again, because Ostra is starting work in this workspace.` | Returned as `Busy` when a project removal or a workspace delete cannot take the work lock. |
| `META_KEY` | `crates/ostra-workspace/src/ui_state.rs` | `ui_state` | Key in the `meta` table of the workspace database that holds the saved console layout as JSON. |

The size limit of the saved layout is `UI_STATE_MAX_BYTES`, which `ostra-core` defines as 65,536 bytes (64 KiB). A patch larger than this, or a merged state larger than this, fails with `Keep the UI state under 64 KiB of JSON.` See [Workspaces, projects, and settings](workspaces-and-settings.md) for the trust approval and the saved UI state.

sections.title: Reference: web console and design constants
sections.summary: Lookup tables for the named constants of the web console and the design package: timings, breakpoints, delays, graph sizes, limits, form lists, content tables, tone maps, and tokens.
sections.body:
Lookup tables for the named constants of `web/` and `design/`: shortcut timings, breakpoints, delays, graph sizes, size limits, settings form lists, lane and stage texts, console filters and defaults, tone and label tables, and lane stepper tokens.

Ostra keeps many fixed values in the `web/` and `design/` source files. Without a list, a reader must open each file to learn a delay, a size, or a menu choice. This page lists those values with their units and their effect. Each table names the source file that holds the constants. For the behavior around them, read [Web console](web-console.md) and [Design system](design-system.md).

This page covers these groups:

- Keyboard shortcut timings, default bindings, and reserved strokes.
- Panel sizes and the viewport width that switches to the mobile shell.
- Delays, polling periods, and time limits.
- Dependency graph layout sizes and zoom limits.
- Size and count limits, including the private key file limit.
- The lists of the settings form.
- The lane and stage content tables.
- Other console constants: cost ranges, session filters, default preferences, editor triggers, the drag type, and the wizard steps.
- Console lookup tables: gate answer tables, tone maps, label maps, editor jump tables, wizard labels, and mock API fixtures.
- The lane stepper icons, the color tokens that it uses, and the focus helpers of `design/`.

For the server-side values, read [Reference: server, code, store, and notify limits](reference-server-limits.md). For the keys of `workspace.toml`, read [Reference: workspace settings and paths](reference-settings.md).

## Keyboard shortcut timings and limits

The file [`web/src/lib/shortcuts.ts`](web/src/lib/shortcuts.ts) matches key strokes to actions. A stroke is a string in the form `ctrl+alt+shift+meta+<key>`. The modifiers always appear in that order. A shortcut is one stroke or two strokes pressed one after the other.

| Constant or rule | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SEQUENCE_MS` | `1500` ms | The second stroke of a two-stroke shortcut must follow the first within this time. After that time, `matchStroke` drops the pending first stroke. |
| `SECOND_STROKE_MS` (in `web/src/screens/workspace/ShortcutsSection.tsx`) | `1200` ms | When the user records a shortcut in settings, a first stroke becomes a one-stroke shortcut if no second stroke follows within this time. |
| Strokes in one shortcut | 1 or 2 | `parseOverrides` drops a stored binding that has 0 strokes or more than 2 strokes. |
| Key name length | 24 characters or fewer | `parseStroke` rejects a stroke whose key part is longer. It also rejects an empty key, a lone modifier, and a key part that contains `+` (except the key `+` itself). |
| Storage key | `ostra.shortcuts.<workspace>` | The browser stores the changed bindings for each workspace in `localStorage`. The stored value is `{ "v": 1, "bindings": { ... } }`. |
| `CHANGED` | `ostra-shortcuts` | The name of the window event that `saveOverrides` sends. Every `useShortcuts` hook in the page reads the new value after this event. The `storage` event updates other browser tabs. |

The shortcuts are stored in the browser only. They do not go to the server, so another browser or another machine keeps its own bindings. When `localStorage` is not available, `saveOverrides` keeps the change in memory and it lasts until the page reloads.

### What happens when

- If the user sets no override for an action, the action keeps its default.
- If an override is `null`, the action has no shortcut.
- If the stored text is not valid JSON, `parseOverrides` returns no overrides and the defaults apply.
- If a stored action name is not in `ACTIONS`, `parseOverrides` ignores it. The reason is that the user can edit the stored value.
- If the user records a stroke that equals another binding, or that equals the first stroke of a two-stroke binding, `conflicts` lists the actions that collide.
- If a modifier key such as Shift or Alt changes the typed character, `strokeOf` names the stroke from the physical key (`event.code`). For example, Alt+K types a different character on a Mac, but the stroke stays `alt+k`.
- Keys in `IGNORED_KEYS` (`Dead`, `Unidentified`, `Process`, `CapsLock`, `NumLock`, `ScrollLock`, and the empty key) use the physical key too. If the physical key has no name, the event makes no stroke.

## Default shortcut bindings

The constant `ACTIONS` lists the 11 actions that have a shortcut. The function `defaults` binds 7 of them: `palette`, `dock`, `sidebar`, `files`, `next-tab`, `prev-tab`, and `close-tab`. It sets 4 to `null`: `new-task`, `settings`, `theme`, and `keyboard-lock`. On a Mac the `mod` key is `meta` (the Command key). On other systems `mod` is `ctrl`.

| Action id | Label | Default stroke |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `palette` | Open the command palette | `mod+k` |
| `dock` | Toggle the quick-question dock | `mod+/` |
| `sidebar` | Toggle the sidebar | `mod+b` |
| `files` | Show the Files tab | `shift+meta+e` on a Mac, `ctrl+shift+e` elsewhere |
| `next-tab` | Next tab | `ctrl+Tab` |
| `prev-tab` | Previous tab | `ctrl+shift+Tab` |
| `close-tab` | Close the focused tab | `mod+w`, marked `reserved` |
| `new-task` | New task | none |
| `settings` | Open settings | none |
| `theme` | Toggle light and dark theme | none |
| `keyboard-lock` | Lock or release keyboard shortcuts in fullscreen | none |

The `close-tab` default is `reserved`. The browser owns `mod+w` for its own tab, so the console claims the stroke only when the browser passes it to the page. That happens when the keyboard is locked or when Ostra runs as an installed app. The argument `claimReserved` of `matchStroke` carries this state. A binding that the user sets is never `reserved`, because the user chose it.

## Reserved strokes

The function `reservedBy` tells whether the browser or the operating system probably handles a stroke before the page sees it. The console uses the result to warn the user when a new binding can fail. The result is a guess, not a guarantee.

| List | Strokes | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BROWSER_MAC` | `meta+w`, `meta+t`, `meta+n`, `meta+q`, `shift+meta+t`, `shift+meta+n`, `shift+meta+w` | `browser` |
| `BROWSER_OTHER` | `ctrl+w`, `ctrl+t`, `ctrl+n`, `ctrl+shift+t`, `ctrl+shift+n`, `ctrl+shift+w` | `browser` |
| `BROWSER_ANY` | `ctrl+Tab`, `ctrl+shift+Tab`, `ctrl+PageUp`, `ctrl+PageDown` | `browser` |
| `SYSTEM_MAC` | `meta+Tab`, `shift+meta+Tab`, `meta+Space`, `ctrl+Space`, `meta+h`, `meta+m`, `ctrl+ArrowUp` | `system` |
| `SYSTEM_OTHER` | `alt+Tab`, `alt+shift+Tab`, `alt+F4`, `ctrl+alt+Delete`, `ctrl+alt+ArrowLeft`, `ctrl+alt+ArrowRight` | `system` |

`reservedBy` checks the stroke in this order:

1. If the stroke is in the system list of the platform (`SYSTEM_MAC` on a Mac, `SYSTEM_OTHER` elsewhere), the result is `system`.
2. If the platform is not a Mac and the stroke has the `meta` modifier, the result is `system`, because the operating system uses the Windows key.
3. If the stroke is in the browser list of the platform (`BROWSER_MAC` or `BROWSER_OTHER`) or in `BROWSER_ANY`, the result is `browser`. The test for `BROWSER_ANY` is in the same condition as the platform list, so it has no priority over that list.
4. Otherwise the result is `null`.

The system checks come first. Thus a stroke that is in a system list never returns `browser`.

The set `MODIFIER_KEYS` has the key names that never make a stroke alone: `Control`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `AltGraph`, `Meta`, `OS`, `Hyper`, `Super`, and `Fn`. The table `CODE_CHARS` maps 11 physical key codes to characters: `Slash`, `Backslash`, `Period`, `Comma`, `Semicolon`, `Quote`, `BracketLeft`, `BracketRight`, `Minus`, `Equal`, and `Backquote`. ## Dependency graph layout

The file [`web/src/screens/project/DependencyGraph.tsx`](web/src/screens/project/DependencyGraph.tsx) draws the dependency graph as an SVG. All sizes are in SVG units, which are pixels at zoom `1`. The layout puts the nodes of one graph column in a stack. A column with more than `MAX_ROWS` nodes wraps into side-by-side lanes, so a wide fan-out stays on the screen.

| Constant | Value | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_W` | 208 | Width of a node. |
| `NODE_H` | 44 | Height of a node that shows no member rows. |
| `MEMBER_H` | 20 | Height of one member row inside a node. |
| `MAX_INLINE_MEMBERS` | 12 | A node shows at most 12 member rows. Extra members add one more row with the count of the rest. |
| `COL_GAP` | 80 | Space between two columns. |
| `ROW_GAP` | 14 | Space between two nodes in one stack. |
| `PAD` | 20 | Space around the whole graph. |
| `HEADER` | 28 | Extra space at the top for the column headings. It applies only to the `file` and `symbol` views. |
| `MAX_ROWS` | 10 | The most nodes in one lane of a column. |
| `LANE_GAP` | 16 | Space between the lanes of one column. |
| `MIN_ZOOM` | 0.2 | The lowest zoom factor. The zoom-out button turns off at this value. |
| `MAX_ZOOM` | 2.5 | The highest zoom factor. The zoom-in button turns off at this value. |

A node that shows member rows has the height `NODE_H + 6 + (rows + 1 if more members exist) * MEMBER_H + 6`. The fit-to-screen function uses a zoom of at most `1` and leaves 24 px on each axis. When the graph focuses on a node, the view centers on the node at zoom `1` and uses at most 240 units of the node height for the center.

The server caps the graph data before it reaches this view. For those caps, read [Reference: server, code, store, and notify limits](reference-server-limits.md) and [Code navigation](code-navigation.md).

## Settings form lists

The file [`web/src/screens/workspace/settingsForm.ts`](web/src/screens/workspace/settingsForm.ts) holds the lists that the settings page uses. The page edits a form model and not `WorkspaceSettings` itself, so a text field keeps what the user typed. The function `fromForm` derives the settings from the form, and `toForm` does the reverse. For the meaning of each setting, read [Reference: workspace settings and paths](reference-settings.md) and [Workspaces, projects, and settings](workspaces-and-settings.md).

### Choice lists

| Constant | Values | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPLEXITIES` | `low`, `medium`, `high` | The phase complexity levels. Routing tables have one entry for each level. |
| `TIER_NAMES` | `fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, `frontier` | The model tier names. A model route with one of these names has the kind `tier`. |
| `EFFORTS` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | The effort choices in the routing tables. An empty choice keeps the default of the agent definition. |

A model route has one of five kinds: `unset`, `default`, `tier`, `custom`, or `per-executor`. The kind `per-executor` holds the text `executor = model, ...`. The function `parsePerExecutor` accepts a name that matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, then `=`, then a model. It splits entries on commas and new lines. The help text is the constant `PER_EXECUTOR_HELP`: `Write each entry as executor = model, for example native = anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5, codex = gpt-5.6-terra.`

The executor of an agent route is `native` or `harness:<name>`. The function `fromForm` skips executor values that equal `native`, so the settings hold an absent entry for them. The function `toForm` shows an absent entry as `native`.

### Settings tabs

The constant `SETTINGS_TABS` lists 10 tabs in this order: `general`, `projects`, `git`, `routing`, `mcp` (label `MCP servers`), `permissions`, `instructions`, `notifications`, `shortcuts`, and `signin` (label `Sign-in`).

The function `tabOf` finds the tab of a settings path from the first part of the path:

- `mcp_servers` goes to `mcp`.
- `shortcuts` goes to `shortcuts`.
- A part that starts with `sandbox_`, and `tool_enforcement`, go to `permissions`.
- `projects`, `routing`, `permissions`, `instructions`, and `notifications` go to the tab of the same name.
- Every other path goes to `general`.

The tab shows the count of issues that `mapIssues` finds for it. The function `fieldForIssue` assigns an issue to the longest field identifier that equals the path or is a parent of it.

### Deep link aliases

A deep link names an element with the identifier `setting:<key>`. The function `anchorCandidates` tries the full key first, then each shorter parent key. The table `ALIASES` sends a key that names a whole table to the panel that shows it.

| Key | Target panel |
| --- | --- |
| `routing`, `routing.executor`, `routing.executor.byAgent`, `routing.model`, `routing.model.byAgent`, `routing.effort`, `routing.effort.byAgent` | `routing.byAgent` |
| `routing.executor.byPhaseComplexity`, `routing.model.byPhaseComplexity`, `routing.effort.byPhaseComplexity` | `routing.byPhaseComplexity` |
| `limits` | `limits` |
| `permissions` | `permissions.mode` |

### Other form rules

- The function `ports` keeps only words with 1 to 5 digits and a value of 65535 or less. The value `0` stays so that the server can name the error.
- The function `unlines` splits text on new lines, trims each line, and drops empty lines. The rule lists (`allow`, `ask`, `deny`), the allowed hosts, and the decoy paths use it.
- The function `splitCommand` splits an MCP command line into words. Spaces separate words, quotes group words, and a backslash escapes the next character. An open quote returns `null` and the form shows `Close the quote in the command.`
- The MCP header lines use `Name: value`. The MCP environment lines use `KEY=value`.
- The form has no fields for the code provider or the language servers of a project. `fromForm` keeps these values from the base settings, by project key or by path after a rename.

### Tool enforcement choices

The constant `TOOL_ENFORCEMENT` has three choices. The empty value follows the global `tool_enforcement`, which defaults to `disabled`.

| Value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `""` | Follows `tool_enforcement` in the global config. |
| `disabled` | Agents can reach files by any route, such as one script that edits several files. This saves tool calls. Write scope, the report path, and self-protection are off. The ownership, secret, git, and test guards still refuse, and the sandbox still limits every command. The console recommends it for capable models. |
| `enabled` | Every guard runs. This protects the pipeline from a weaker model that writes outside its scope or misnames its report. It costs more tool calls, because each refused call is spent. |

The guards are explained on [Policy engine: guards, permissions, and containment](policy-guards.md).

### Permission modes

| `PERMISSION_MODES` value | Label | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | Default | Asks before file edits and before any command that no rule allows. |
| `acceptEdits` | Accept edits | Allows file edits inside the project. Commands that no rule lists still ask. |
| `plan` | Plan (read-only) | Agents can read the project but cannot change it. |
| `bypass` | Bypass | Nothing asks. Guards and deny rules still apply. |

### Sandbox modes and networks

The constant `SANDBOX_MODES` has four choices. The empty value follows `[sandbox] mode` of the global config. That default is `required` on Linux and macOS and `auto` on Windows, because Windows has no sandbox backend yet.

| Mode | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `""` | Follows the global setting. |
| `required` | Agent commands run in the sandbox. An execution that cannot be sandboxed does not start. |
| `auto` | Agent commands run in the sandbox when the machine has one. Otherwise they run without it and a warning appears. |
| `off` | Agent commands run with the full rights of the user. Use it only to test a harness that the sandbox blocks. |

The function `runsUnsandboxed` is true when the sandbox is not active and the mode is not `required`. The function `takesHosts` is true for the networks `allowlist` and `public`, because only these two use the allowed host list.

| `SANDBOX_NETWORKS` value | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | Commands reach nothing. A harness CLI still reaches its own model API. |
| `allowlist` | Commands reach package registries, source hosts, the model APIs of the harness CLIs, and the listed hosts. |
| `public` | Commands reach any public address and the listed hosts. Loopback, private, and link-local addresses stay refused. |
| `host` | Commands use the network of the host without a filter. This includes every local service, the local network, and the cloud metadata address. |

The list `UNSANDBOXED_EFFECTS` has four warnings that the console shows when agent commands run without a sandbox. These effects apply to shell commands only. They do not apply to the file tools of Ostra.

- A shell command that walks the disk can read hidden workspace artifacts, for example `find ~`.
- A shell command that does not name them can read the data directory of Ostra and the sign-in files of the CLIs of the user.
- A program that a command starts can write anywhere that the user can write. Ostra checks only the writes that it can read in the command itself.
- The `[sandbox] network` setting does not apply. Commands reach any host, including local services and the local network.

The constant `DECOY_GUIDE` is the URL `https://github.com/diepquynh/ostra/blob/master/docs/security/sandboxing.md#decoy-credential-files`. The console links to the repository because it ships no documentation. For the sandbox layers, read [Sandbox: kernel enforcement under agent commands](sandbox.md).

### The requirement note

The constant `EARS_NOTE` is a collapsible note that the console shows the first time the user views a spec or a plan. It has the title `How to read requirements and acceptance criteria`. It explains the five EARS sentence forms and the Given / When / Then form of acceptance criteria.

| EARS form | Pattern |
| --- | --- |
| Ubiquitous | `The system shall ...` holds all the time. |
| Event-driven | `When <trigger>, the system shall ...` holds after the trigger. |
| State-driven | `While <state>, the system shall ...` holds during the state. |
| Unwanted behavior | `If <condition>, then the system shall ...` covers errors and edge cases. |
| Optional feature | `Where <feature is present>, the system shall ...` |

Each acceptance criterion becomes at least one test, and the reviewer checks the code against the criteria.

## Console lookup tables

This section lists the console constants that the other sections do not cover. Each row gives the file, the value or the meaning, and what the constant controls. Rows are grouped by file. Most tables map a status or a kind to a `Tone` of the design package. A `Tone` is one of `accent`, `ok`, `warn`, `bad`, `info`, or `neutral`, and it sets the color of a chip or a dot.

### Gate answer tables

The file [`web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts`](web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts) builds the answers that the console sends for a gate. The comment on `ANSWER_KIND` says that it mirrors `runner::validate_answer` in the engine. For the gates, read [The session pipeline](session-pipeline.md).

| Constant | Value or meaning | What it controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ANSWER_KIND` | A map from the 14 gate kinds to the answer kind that each gate accepts. `open_questions` takes `questions`. `spec_approval` and `plan_approval` take `approval`. `closing_gate` takes `closing`. `permission` takes `permission`. `skill_approval` takes `skills`. The other 8 gates take `choice`. | The function `isChoiceKind` reads it to find the gates that use the `CHOICES` table. |
| `CHOICES` | A map from each of the 8 choice gates to its options in button order. Each option has an `option` string, a `label`, a `variant`, and a `text` rule. | The buttons of a choice gate card, and the check that `choiceAnswer` runs before it sends an answer. |
| `PERMISSION_LABELS` | `allow-once` is `Allow once`. `always-in-workspace` is `Always in this workspace`. `deny` is `Deny`. | The button labels of a permission gate. |
| `DISPOSITIONS` | `generate`, `regenerate`, `reuse`, `drop` | The choices that the user has for each skill in a skill approval gate. |

The `variant` of an option is `primary`, `default`, or `danger`. Exactly one option of each gate is `primary`. The `text` rule is `none`, `optional`, or `required`. It tells whether the option sends the text field of the gate. If a `required` text is empty, `choiceAnswer` returns the `missing` message of the option.

| Gate kind | Options (`option`, label, variant, text rule) |
| --- | --- |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `another-round`, Run another fact-check round, primary, optional. `stop`, Stop the session, danger, none. |
| `review_cap` | `another-pass`, Run another fix and review pass, primary, optional. `stop`, Stop and block the phase, default, none. |
| `stuck` | `fact`, Re-run with this fact, primary, required. `block`, Block this work, default, none. |
| `phase_blocked` | `retry`, Retry the phase, primary, optional. `leave`, Leave the phase blocked, default, none. |
| `harness_failure` | `retry`, Retry after login, primary, none. `native`, Run on the native executor, default, none. |
| `execution_failed` | `retry`, Retry the execution, primary, none. `abandon`, Abandon this work, default, none. |
| `budget_reached` | `raise`, Raise the budget, primary, optional. `stop`, Stop the session, danger, none. |
| `implementation_review` | `done`, Accept the implementation, primary, none. `feedback`, Send feedback, default, required. |

The `raise` option of `budget_reached` has one more check. If the text is not empty, `parseDollars` must read it as a positive dollar amount such as `10` or `$12.50`. If the text is empty, the engine adds the budget again.

## Lane stepper constants and design tokens

The component `LaneStepper` in [`design/src/components/pipeline/LaneStepper.tsx`](design/src/components/pipeline/LaneStepper.tsx) draws the nine lanes as a horizontal strip. The console uses it on the session screen and in the setup wizard. The component is a `tablist` and each lane is a `tab`.

`LANE_ORDER` is `research`, `requirements`, `verification`, `design`, `build`, `review`, `test`, `docs`, `done`. The constant `TITLES` gives the same names as the `title` values of `LANES` in the web app. The two tables are separate copies, so a change to a lane name must go to both files.

A lane has one of six states. The constants `ICON` and `ICON_COLOR` set the icon and its color for each state.

| Lane status | Icon | Icon color token |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pending` | none | none |
| `current` | a pulsing dot (`os-dot--accent`) | none |
| `waiting` | `hand` | `var(--warn)` |
| `done` | `check` | `var(--ok)` |
| `failed` | `x` | `var(--bad)` |
| `skipped` | `minus` | `var(--text-muted)` (the fallback color) |

The icon size is 11 px. A lane that has no state in the `lanes` property shows as `pending`.

### Color tokens

The file [`design/src/tokens/colors.css`](design/src/tokens/colors.css) defines the tokens. Dark is the default theme. The light theme applies when the attribute `data-theme="light"` is set. The tokens of the lane stepper have these values:

| Token | Dark theme | Light theme |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--accent` | `var(--blue-400)` | `var(--blue-600)` |
| `--ok` | `var(--green-400)` | `var(--green-700)` |
| `--warn` | `var(--amber-400)` | `var(--amber-700)` |
| `--bad` | `var(--red-400)` | `var(--red-700)` |
| `--info` | `var(--violet-400)` | `var(--violet-700)` |
| `--text-muted` | `var(--gray-400)` | `#8a8a83` |

The tokens `--ok`, `--warn`, `--bad`, `--info`, and `--accent` each have a `-soft` variant for backgrounds. The other token files are `typography.css`, `spacing.css`, `fonts.css`, `effects.css`, `components.css`, and `base.css`. They are explained on [Design system](design-system.md).

## Focus helpers of the design package

The file [`design/src/focus.ts`](design/src/focus.ts) holds the keyboard focus rules of the design components.

The constant `FOCUSABLE` is a CSS selector for the elements that can take focus: `a[href]`, enabled `button`, enabled `input` that is not `type="hidden"`, enabled `select`, enabled `textarea`, and any element with a `tabindex` that is not `-1`. The function `focusables` returns the matching elements of a container and drops each element that is inside an element with the `inert` attribute.

The hook `useFocusTrap` keeps focus inside a modal. The components `Dialog` and `CommandPalette` use it:

1. When the trap becomes active, the hook checks the active element. If the active element is not already inside the container, the hook moves focus to the `initial` element. If there is no `initial` element, it uses the first focusable element, and if there is none, the container.
2. The returned key handler wraps `Tab` at the ends of the container. Shift+Tab on the first element goes to the last element, and Tab on the last element goes to the first.
3. If the container has no focusable element, the handler blocks `Tab`.
4. When the trap becomes inactive, the hook gives focus back to the previous element, if the element is still in the page.

The function `arrowIndex(key, index, count, orientation, wrap = true)` returns the next index for the arrow keys. The orientation `vertical` uses `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp`. The orientation `horizontal` uses `ArrowRight` and `ArrowLeft`. `Home` returns `0` and `End` returns `count - 1`. Any other key returns `null`, and a `count` of `0` returns `null`. If `wrap` is true, the index goes from the last item to the first and the reverse. The components `Menu`, `Tabs`, `TreeItem`, and `LaneStepper` call it. `TreeItem` passes `wrap = false`.

A file that the user keeps for every session of one workspace, in the visible or the hidden artifacts folder.
The Rust type for the workspace SQLite file `<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.db`, which holds the event log and the tables beside it.
The trait that gives a workspace the registry, the machine config, the environment scan, and the engine services.
The runtime of one open workspace in the server process. It owns settings access, the database, the engine, and project operations.
A session option that lets the engine answer most gates for the user. It leaves `budget_reached` and the `execution_failed` gate of a stopped execution open.
